Apply two times a day.

Three.

Smith notices Jones has 10 coins. He also notices Jones had a much better interview.
Smith thinks the man with 10 coins will get the job.
Later, Smith actually does get the job. After the interview, he finds 10 coins in his pocket.
So Smith's proposition was justified and true, but wasn't based on accurate information.
This presents a problem: if you can have right knowledge for the wrong reason, what is the meaning of "knowledge"?
But it's easy if you look at little things.

comics.descriptionText:
[Narration, set against an image of Earth in space:]
When the first signal arrived, it was clearer than anyone had anticipated. The location and blue-shifting of the transmitter's signal suggested it would be here in months. Months in cosmic time are like seconds in human time.
As many predicted, the immediate result was a unified human effort to prepare. However, it was less a grand harmony than a sort of global version of a bachelor scrambling to clean his apartment before a pretty girl makes a surprise visit. There were many sources of embarrassment that had to be destroyed or hidden.
These three problems were simple. The president of the UN pretended an attractive blonde woman was kidnapped and hidden in the war mound. Once the reporters arrived, all the fusion bombs were detonated.
But the aliens would also see the social problems - the tent cities, the slums, the favelas. Surely Earth would be more inviting if all those poor people lived in suburban households with a few precious children and a labrador retriever.
The world turned to China, which alone possessed the vast industrial complex and sheer tonnage of orphans needed to pull off the operation. Families were assembled and enrobed with picket fences. Labrador gestation rates were constructed, able to deliver acres of beloved hounds on a daily basis. Kids were instructed to say the darndest things. Those who did not were culled.
War was cancelled. This was easily accomplished - the UN stipulated that any time a person committed a noble act of patriotism, a picture of that person sitting on the toilet was to be sent to an attractive member of the opposite sex. Cleavewitz once said that war is the extension of policy by other means. What most people don't know is that 'policy' was slang for 'penis.'
We attempted to halt sex trafficking. Concern arose as to whether this was possible, but we decided that if the aliens found any, we'd pretend to find it gross and claim that the last people to live here must've left it.
Then they arrived, massive and spheroid, in the sky. We beamed light on to the atmosphere, showing the first few seven prime numbers. The aliens halted signal transmission. The whole of humanity waited in silence. A message came.
We watched as the president of the UN adjusted her spectacles and tried to parse the information. She moistened her lips, breathed in through her nose, and spoke.
That night, we trained our telescopes on our planetary neighbor. A sort of shared envy gripped all of us as we watched parties erupt on the red planet. Finding out Mars had life on the same day we found out it was better than us was painful. Like meeting a long lost brother by walking in on him doing a commendable job screwing your wife.
We had collectively combed our hair and worn fresh underwear, and for what? With each moment, we were reminded that we were still a bachelor. The parts were too big and the hair cut looked so very stupid.
Even if they had come in, it wouldn't have worked out, we told ourselves. Eventually they would've found Chernobyl, and we'd have to say but the attempt to salvage things would only make the inevitable failure more embarrassing. Then they'd probably go find some rich civilization with a bunch of fancy pretentious crap like universal sanitation.
Worldwide sour grapes (which is, after all, unity of a sort) set in. Humanity loosened its proverbial belt, let its proverbial gut hang low, and noted with a queer sense of relief that it had completely forgotten to sweep North Korea under China.
Perhaps it was good that we believed aliens were coming. Perhaps we should always live as if we're about to invite an otherworldly mate over to dinner. Perhaps... perhaps... for a moment, we all inhaled the chamomile odor of perhaps.
[A row of people on a hilltop under stars, holding hands or gathered.]
But there were other less subtle odors soon. Within a few days, the proverbial Taco Bell was allowed into the apartment*. Being a bachelor does, after all, have its small joys.
The End
*In case you're wondering, Taco Bell is a metaphor for Taco Bell.

comics.descriptionText:
The comic is a single illustrated poem, told in first person, with small spot illustrations beside each stanza.
I hacked for 40 days,
and I hacked for 40 nights.
I hacked within the darkness,
and I hacked within the lights.
I hacked and I discovered
machines I hadn't sought.
A database of numbers I
remembered being taught.
I couldn't place the lesson
or its meaning or import,
but knew they were important
so I changed them just for sport.
The walls began to tremble,
and the ground began to rumble.
The ceiling ripped apart
and to the sky began to tumble.
I clung to my computer,
but my arms began to rot.
The screen began to flicker,
and the processor grew hot.
I flew toward the sky
as the sun grew large and red.
I feared that I would die
and then the screen went black and dead.
I hit it with my fist
(which grew larger by the second).
The fan began to whirl,
and a command line calmly beckoned.
I changed the numbers back.
To what they were... as I recalled.
My upward movement slowed
and the cataclysm stalled.
I fell into my seat,
and watched the sun begin to shrink
until the ceiling landed,
at which point I stopped to think.
I must've hacked the universe
In servers seldom seen.
I gazed around the mess and mused
I went outside and whistled,
so I wouldn't seem suspicious.
For the damage to reality
was vast, but not malicious
My neighbors ran toward me
Shouting
I shrugged my shoulders calmly
saying,
I won't be going back to that
Transmundane DNS,
though I hope that someone will
someday, someday, yes I confess.
I hope when humans are more wise,
When humans are more worthy,
They'll say "she hacked the truth machine,
Prematurely."

And each year, the king was weighed, and the villagers would receive gold equal to his weight.
But the village mathematicians realized that higher weight meant a shorter lifespan.
If he's half as massive but lives twice as long, we break even.
Well, then it's a simple optimization problem.
The ideal weight was around 250 pounds.
The village doctors realized that not all body weight is created equal.
If he's mostly muscle, his weight will be high and his lifespan will increase.
So the king was put on a crash fitness program.
Until the village economists made a suggestion.
If we get more money up front, we could use the compound interest to make more money than we'd get by receiving earnings over the king's lifespan. We should frontload now.
And so the economists supplied the king with ten tons of bacon, the doctors injected him with muscle inflamers, the mathematicians talked to him of theorems, which caused him to sleep 20 hours a day.
Soon, the town was fabulously wealthy. The new moneyed class had the power to demand a republic, and the king died from cardiac disease. The end.

comics.comicText:
Scarcity
Economics,
is the study of the allocation of scarce resources.
However,
that is only a recent definition. In the past, economics has been the study of the allocation of very scarce resources.
Prior to that, it was extremely scarce resources.
In fact,
How was it resolved?
Of course that is lost to history in its particulars,
However, there is reason to believe that it was resolved through the application of Newton's Second Law, as embodied in a fist.
How primitive,
Indeed. Those would have been honorable too simple to make use of the laws of thermodynamics to resolve turnip disputes, much less the laws of relativity.
Now, the point here is this -- the study of economics is the study of a moving target. It began in the study of how to allocate a few very rare things. Then it became the study of how to allocate a few moderately rare things. With the advent of cold fusion 50 years ago, it reached what can be considered an inflection point.
The post-scarcity society,
Wrong!
The entire last generation of economists has made the willfully naive mistake. No, don't you see? If nothing is scarce, what is scarce?
Wrong! If there are no scarce resources, the only scarce resource is scarce resources.
I don't follow.
If everyone has everything, the only thing scarce is something nobody else has.
Madame, this is the post scarcity world of scarcity. No doubt those bottles will be transmuted into some useful substance, and those trees will return within weeks. But, for the moment, you are the only one to have Canadian pine.
Don't you see,
We're sitting on a goldmine here!
What is it?
It's an apple,
Have a bite.
Every single apple just like that one,
has just turned into maggots!
We sold hundreds of them!
We sold ninety-nine hundred apples this morning, and by tonight there won't be a single living apple anywhere in the world.
WRONG! They'll be delighted! Mind you, not as delighted as the person eating the apple. BUT, these people will each have an experience only had by 9,999 other individuals.
I see,
But then, you can't mass produce these.
By definition, no. But we can produce more varieties. We have a prototype orange that turns into locusts and a banana that bugs the merry when you eat it.
If I may,
if I may, it seems that this you're merely just introducing ugly things into people's lives and then offering to take them away.
And that is the new economics, madame.
Take a note. Economics is the study of the creation of scarce resources.

My uncle is going crazy.
We thought he was just odd, but it turned out he was a paranoid schizophrenic, and slowly getting worse.
What weirds me out is that the reason we're all worried about him is that he thinks the universe cares deeply about his behavior.
We call him crazy because he doesn't accept, like us, that he's just a tiny nothing in a giant indifferent cosmos.
But we don't accept that either. Not really. Because if we did, we'd be the ones who went nuts.
I love him, and I pity him, but I can't shake the idea that when he dies, he'll think it was for a reason, and when I die I'll just be wide-eyed, scared, and alone, not knowing why I'm here or why I can't stay.
My uncle buys me action figures and cookies.

comics.comicText:
When we discovered how to live in virtual worlds, we escaped to fantasies as often as possible.
As society became more affluent and automated, it took less and less real-world labor to earn each hour of virtuality.
As machines became more adapted to our brains, it became cheaper to double perception of time than to double productivity per laborer.
Time may be a real quantity, but to a human mind a minute of terror really is a billion times longer than a night of sleep.
We soon discovered a way to give the sensation of infinite time.
At which point, there was a simple decision to make: Why spend a short life in the real world of sadness and absurdity when you could live forever in paradise?
Dear traveler: please don't think ill of us. We are the last generation.
And we are immortal.

comics.descriptionText:
A person was happy.
Then one day a rock fell on its head.
A piece of the rock stuck in its scalp. But it did not realize this.
It began to hurt in its head.
It thought the pain was from something wrong in its life.
But it didn't know what was wrong, and it wanted to know.
It stopped its daily work. But that did not help.
It made pretty things. But that did not help.
Because these things did not help, it decided the problem was not with itself, but with the universe.
It left its family and friends, and took to wandering and contemplation.
One day, it tripped, hit its head, and the stone dislodged.
The pain stopped.
It was happy again.
It decided that whatever it had done before the stone dislodged was the source of the happiness.
It told other people why it was happy. And they listened.
But they never quite found their teacher's happiness. Because there were no stones in their heads to dislodge.
This difference was taken as a sign of the teacher's wisdom.
The teacher had many students, and they wrote down the pattern of the teacher's life as they knew it.
The teacher is dead now.
But the pattern is everywhere.
The students learn it with serious eyes.
But if the stone were a person, it would laugh.

For a time, the software worked well.
Our kill rate per mission is up 30 percent! Who'd a thunk a little software tweak could do it?

They were displaying their faces and... their... families.
We fought back, securing our software while projecting empathy at their soldiers.
The new program shows the enemy pictures of those you leave behind. This reduces their kill ratio by 95 percent!

RWA
Fish, Fish, Cat
Cetacean.
Auto, Liberalo Transport, Dog, Hi, Approx.
The further right you go on the scale, the more uncomfortable it is for the entity to watch you poop.
a cat.

Here is the face of a dolphin watching you poop. On this basis, we propose an end to any form of dolphin hunting.
This method is so robust, to our surprise, it extends beyond humans. When we originally considered as the maximally awkward poop-watchers, the following is a simulation of a perfected mind woven of spacetime as it watches you poop.

comics.comicText:
As population expanded, so did the number of potential mates per person.

I am not going to travel forty miles and learn a new dialect just so I can be with a person who understands my innermost self.
Later, travel became cheap when translation software was perfected, and dating software was optimized.

Estimated relationship lifespan is 1,312 years. If extreme longevity is discovered, it won't work out.
People made ever more specific demands.
The sex was incredible, and I could spend a lifetime just talking to you. But I want a guy who parts his hair on the other side.
I could do that.
I mean without me asking.
Since the algorithm favored aggorative mating, couples tended to be genetically similar.
I've always wanted to meet someone else with four legs and severe hirsutism.
ME TOO!
Most humans couldn't find the perfect mate, but those who did felt a profound urge to procreate.
There should be more of this.
In time, humanity split into a few different species.
I think we should call it Seth-Wade-Hooded speciation.
That's just the sort of stupid notion I'd expect from a descendant of Jog and Sally.
Each lineage was so genetically homogenous it was extremely vulnerable to biological warfare. Once this was realized, Armageddon was inevitable.
In today's news, all progeny of Underbo and Frinka will be dead soon. Myself included! Interestingly, we'll all have exactly the same symptoms.
When civilization fell apart, the only survivors were people who were okay mating across species lines.
Hey baby. Nice cloaca.
100,000 years later, you were watching porno on the internet. And, well... now you know why you feel the way you do post-orgasm.

comics.title: The Life of a Puppet
comics.comicText:
Pinocchio was cursed so that his nose would grow whenever he lied.
This is actually a pretty easily managed curse, if you just phrase all statements so broadly that they can't be false.
Pinocchio, do you bully that boy at school?
There are people who would dispute that perspective.
You can also answer tough questions by just describing the current situation.
Pinocchio, did you egg my door?
If you're accusing me of such a deed, I have nothing more to say.
Or, you can reply to statements via questions with no inherent stance.
Pino, do you love me?
How could I not?
Cursed to never lie, Pinocchio ceased to interact with truth, even in safe situations.
Sir, would you like any dessert?
Dessert would be delicious.
His political rise was magnificent.
Sixty-eaters are 0.5% of primary voters. We can't alienate them. If asked your stance on Pedophilia, I'll retreat into confusingly charming Southernisms.
I like to say, if you see a bullfrog on a fencepost, somebody put him there.
His associates found themselves unhappy, but this is only because he can't speak the truth to himself.
Now that I'm President, I've won at life. I can have people killed. This is great.
But "transcendence" was my girlfriend in college was talking about!
It's great!
Today, he is remembered as a great leader.
It was uncanny! World leaders loved him. Even enemies! There was just something about him for everyone.
But great leaders often die poorly.
None of it ever meant anything to me.

comics.title: The Ethical Fourier Transform
comics.comicText:
I call it the ethical courier transform.
You've got an ethical conundrum instead of solving it, convert it to the realm of economics having solved it then, declare it to be a solved ethical problem.
Example: Suppose you're piloting a trolley. It's headed toward the people you can change course to kill only one. What do you do?
I don't know. Life is special. It's like asking whether one infinity is bigger than another. It's as big as it gets. Infinities.
Exactly. Unsolvable. But we can calculate the damage to the trolley, which is derived from the mass of the special human lives.
Thus, it is best to kill only one person.
This is a terrible method. It doesn't even solve basic virtue problems, like whether you can steal bread to feed your family.
Let me check today's grain market prices, and...
It'll be ethical to steal bread to feed your family until inflation, and November.

This is damage to your moral truth doesn't hinge on commodity pricing!
Oh? Let me ask you this: is it ethical to steal truffle mushrooms and champagne to feed your family?
I don't, well, honestly, that somehow does feel like a different moral matter than the bread.

By the fourth night, productivity had increased tenfold." Green-shirted man: "I've been building spreadsheets for 87 hours straight! I can taste sound!" Other voice: "So—" Green-shirted man: "I'm gonna pup show and eat this conversation.

You have misunderstood human nature. I hate her so much I MUST stay until she is destroyed.
Fearing for her safety, Agnes began to telecommute, then to telecommute by proxy. 'Urinating during work hours shall cost 400 points, so let it be written.
Forty days passed and forty nights, and by that time, no employee knew if she were alive or dead, or if she ever existed." One figure: "Don't forget—" Another: "Praise Agnes and blessed be!" "—the new pot, she is watching.
Agnes has been silent for five years. The legend grows greater and more terrible. Weave a circle round her thrice and close your eyes with holy dread, for she wants to laugh upon her overhead and say that she should synergize.
This is not mere 'best practices,' my friends. This is a tontine with Satan. A pay freeze?! Well, I'll just work twice as hard, then I will be the Agnes.

P/R vs TIME, line sloping downward.

comics.title: P = NP
comics.comicText:
It has been shown that all NP-hard problems are the same. If you've solved one, you've solved them all.
I propose a corollary: if you have a stupid solution to one NP-hard problem, it stupidly solves them all. I call this a 'sullooshun.
SULLOOSHUN
For instance, the traveling salesman problem. A salesman has to visit a lot of cities, once each, then go home. What's the shortest route?
Well, if you collapse the universe into a singularity, there's only ever one route. So, the sullooshun to every traveling salesman problem is 'collapse the universe.
SOLVED!
Now, let's apply this sullooshun to the bin-packing problem, which concerns how to efficiently pack boxes of various sizes into bins.
If you collapse the universe, everything is the same size, and anyway, why bother packing if you can't go anywhere?
Consider the halting problem. Is there a general way to tell if a program with a given input will ever stop?
The sullooshun is yes. In the singularity, time doesn't exist. The program can't even start, much less stop.
Do you know anything about mathematics?
That is beyond the scope of this talk.

Welcome to day one of science journalism. Today we will learn how to communicate physics.
Quantum mechanics. The entire field of quantum mechanics is about how you don't know what's in a box until you open it.
You especially don't know what's going on if there's a cat in the box.
Relativity. A theory invented by Einstein, which suggests that one guy might not know what's in a box, but another guy might be like 'gee you buddy.
Einstein discovered it when an apple fell on his head and he thought 'maybe it was me who fell on the apple's head.
Finally, quantum computing is when you take a computer and put it in a box. You open it later and it's solved an infinitely complicated problem.
This is possible because you don't know what's in a box until you open it, so maybe it's solving infinity problems in there.
Could some of those things be mushed together to explain consciousness?

comics.title: The Talk
comics.comicText:
Son, it's time we had... THE TALK.
I know all about sex, dad.
Oh! You've advanced. Good. Let's have the relationship talk instead.
Here goes: it is practically impossible to judge a mate at the outset of a relationship.
Many of the things that attract you at first are irrelevant over the long term, especially considering the way in which the members of a couple mold each other over time, developing a shared history.
So, even if you're using entirely valid criteria for selection, you may find yourself in an unhappy partnership.

Given the ever more stupid noises coming out of the mouths of world leaders, the planet is approaching a crisis.
We can no longer stand idly by as the stupidity arms race continues.
So we have created a 'Stupidio Speech Defense System.
We model politicians as hollow spheres fluxing stupidity in every direction.
News corporations are modeled as simultaneous amplifiers and emitters of stupidity, which thus create an internal stupidity feedback loop.
When a dangerously stupid flux occurs, our system creates the opposite sound wave pattern and fires it in the direction of the sphere.
The flux is thus nullified, saving society from both the initial stupidity and the ensuing chain reaction.
Via this strategic defense initiative, we can nullify the greatest danger posed by stupid leaders.

Dad, how do I know if a girl is 'the one'?
No such thing.
It's not about finding the perfect person. It's about going through the stages of life together. It's like this 3-stage rocket.
Here, see the first booster is called 'sex.' It gets things off the ground, so to speak.
Eventually, you run out of fuel there, so you discard it. You hit the second booster, which is called 'affection.
Once affection runs out, you switch to your final booster, which is called 'love.
That's so dorky, but so sweet.
Sure. Anyway, after that you can coast on inertia for a good 30 years before things break apart.

comics.title: The Meissner Effect
comics.comicText:
Are you familiar with the Meissner Effect?
When a superconductor gets cool enough, it suddenly ejects its magnetic field
So the magnetic field lines move around the superconductor instead of through it
I have this theory that if a person becomes cold enough emotionally, they have a mental Meissner Effect, where other people's feelings simply warp around them with no impediment

comics.title: Cognitive Decline
comics.comicText:
It's long been noted that mental ability declines with age.
After an early peak, humans show a steady decline, from memory to reaction time.
Yet, we all know that the more work hours used to drunkenly jump over a parapet at age 60 than at age 60 this indicates better mental ability.
Until now, there was no explanation for this paradox. So, I'll tax progressively "depressed cognitive overload" theory of mental decline.
According to RCO theory, as human beings get older their brains get linearly better, but exponentially more occupied by mental arguments with other people.
The resulting mental ability curve shows a linear increase until about 15 years of age. At this point, the slope continues to be negative because mental quibbling becomes noticeable, creating a lifelong diminishment of available processing power.
This explains the so-called "cognitive decline" among those who have the most knowledge and experience.
It also explains senility. Our elderly relatives have extremely powerful cognitive abilities, but they are monopolized by an exquisitely detailed simulated argument with some guy on cable news.
I am, in fact, currently giving a scientific lecture while mentally fighting with my wife, my brother, and a poorly-trained miniature pony.
Any questions?
Do you have evidence for any of this?
My cognitive ability just dropped 30%.
comics.hoverText: Interestingly, YOU'RE getting dumber too!

comics.title: Bayesianism
comics.comicText:
According to Bayesianism, every theory, no matter how ridiculous, has some probability of being true.
But the sum of all theories multiplied by their probability must still be one.
Therefore, I've created a new device: The Bayesian Overlooker!
Start with some very probable theory that nobody likes. For example: "I will die someday.
Now, we set the Overlooker to generate opposing theories like "everyone liman will not die" or "only pumpkins die" or "nobody has ever died -- there's all just sleeping.
The Overlooker creates hundreds or trillions of theories every second.
Because all of these theories get some slice of the probability pie, so long as we generate theories fast enough, the undesirable theory becomes less and less true.
We want about thirty quadragooglion, then BAM! The initial theory is now vanishingly unlikely!
And thus, I am immortal!
See, that's why I'm a frequentist.

That's not the point. The question is whether it's ethical.
Does the first robot's ethics programming say to value social norms above its own survival?
No. I mean, what ethical laws should govern its behavior?
The ones it's programmed to obey.
I feel like one of us must be missing something.
I can tell you which one, if you'd like.

comics.title: Heap Problems
comics.comicText:
There's this concept in philosophy called "a heap problem.
You have one of something. It's not a heap. You add another. It's still not a heap. If you have ten thousand, it's certainly a heap. So, at what point do you go from a non-heap to a heap?
Afft. A heap is just a human concept. We use it for intellectual book-keeping because we have limited cognitive capacity. But there is no heap. Just larger amounts of stuff.
It's only a "problem" to the extent that we're upset by the fact that a heap isn't real. Just like a proton isn't real, anyway.
We live in Aristotle's world of stuff, and we long to live in Plato's world of ideas.
But, in a far off galaxy, you will find protons. You will find the same stuff. But heaps are just an idea in the minds of limited organisms.
What about mountains or warmth or the color red or love or consciousness? They're some of my favorite things. They're real to me.
It's not the universe's fault if your favorites aren't well-aligned with the nature of reality.
What's your favorite thing?

On the other hand, having you be here all day costs us in rent and electricity.
So, we're proposing an efficient alternative.
If your day's work is complete at the end of two hours, you may go home. But, only by walking naked through this briar patch, then under a waterfall of salty lemon juice, then through a long hall where twenty men dressed like your mother insult your life choices while drawing you with trophies won by more successful classmates from your high school.
That way, you get more leisure time, and we feel we got our money's worth.

comics.title: Self-Driving Car Ethics
comics.comicText:
Two self-driving cars are about to hit a man.
Each car holds five people.
Each can only avoid the lone man by swerving off a cliff.
One car is utilitarian. The greatest good is the best outcome.
One car is deontological.
Thou shalt not kill.
The utilitarian car KNOWS the deontological car must swerve.
Total dead: 6. Total alive: 5.
The deontological car KNOWS the utilitarian car will not swerve. Even if I obey my rule, the man will die.
Calculations grow complex.
But if the deontological car knows that I know that it knows that I'm going to swerve, and thus it should...
If it knows that I'm not going to swerve, thus killing the man, it may change his mind about not swerving in which case...
At this point, the Nietzschean tractor-trailer speeds through.
WHAT IS GOOD?! ALL THAT HEIGHTENS THE FEELING OF POWER!
This scene plays out over and over whenever cars must make ethical decisions. In time, all gentler ethical systems are extinguished among autonomous vehicles.
Nietzschean trucks come to view themselves as humanity's natural overlords.
What is happiness? The feeling that power is growing, that resistance is overcome!
There is nothing to life that has value except the degree of power!
Still, on the whole it's pretty good.
It's not perfect, but MAN I do NOT miss commuting.
comics.hoverText: Then, one day, Jesus Chrysler will come.

Moments aren't isolated instants! They echo through the universe, to and fro. Always. Forever.
In each moment we experience immortality.
So, the secret to immortality is changing the meaning of the word, then lying to yourself about how you feel about it?
Technically you only need that first thing.

UH HUH.
YOU WANNA FIGHT? I WILL FIGHT YOU!

Have you been flossing regularly?
Regularly, in the sense of a consistent rate?
It's just that your gums—
I'm not one of your pushover patients. Lemme tell you about gums. My diet consists entirely of pointy tortilla chips and sour candy straws—
Listen, dentist. I don't go to a mechanic to hear about how my car is a jalopy.
I have to supplement my diet with iron due to daily blood loss from my face.
If I had the desire or wherewithal to change, I would do it. As I do not, I expect you to go in there and do stuff until I can go back to devastating every surface inside my mouth on an hourly basis.
I don't care if you have to consult an architect or a philosopher just to imagine some way to rebuild my ruined oral cavity— JUST DO YOUR JOB!
What in the— How is dentistry so expensive?!

comics.title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
comics.comicText:
Grampa, can I have a story?
This is the story of the grasshopper and the ants.
Once upon a time, there was a grasshopper and some ants. The grasshopper played his fiddle and danced all summer long, while the ants worked hard.
Come winter time, there was very little food. The grasshopper died so did the ants who did most of the work.
The ants who died spent their entire lives as a sexless slave race, devoted to a distant, all-powerful overlord who thought less of them than her own excreta.
The grasshopper experienced happiness, but died in sorrow. The ants experienced neither joy nor pain — only monotonous toil. From a naively utilitarian perspective, they came out equal.
Nearby, humans watched, and imagined themselves superior because their lifespans were one cosmic second longer.
The end.
Would you like to hear the story of the big bad wolf who improved the gene pool?
No, please.

comics.title: The Horrors of Math

I don't get why people are afraid of math.
Come on! Math is ALWAYS pulling shit.
You have a dollar. You spend it. Now you have no dollars. That's subtraction. MATH did that.
You're in love with someone. You split up. Now the couple is 50% smaller. Who's at fault? MATH.
You're talking to somebody about math, and the whole time she's thinking, "He's making statements that are technically true, but based on an incorrect usage of the term 'math.'" That's logic, which is a form of math.
Other people are stupid. You're recursively stupid. MATH AGAIN!

comics.title: Path of a Hero

Father! Adventure calls me! I must leave this sheltered farm behind and venture forth!

Dad, every hero story starts off like this. Then the young man breaks free, braves danger and returns, wizened and powerful.
That's called survivor bias.
Adventurers who went a long time without getting killed tended to have books written about them. That doesn't mean it always went that way for everyone. Nobody wants to read about the hero who left the farm and immediately got stabbed by highwaymen.
The only thing you'll accomplish by adventuring beyond the farm is that you'll decrease the gene pool of people who are terrible at understanding basic statistical concepts.
You cannot stay me from my destiny, father!

comics.title: Math
comics.comicText:
Part of why math confuses people is that we pick stupid names for things.
Imaginary numbers? They're not "imaginary"! They're actual things that show up in lots of practical equations!
Why do we have "natural" numbers when all sorts of things naturally don't come in positive integer values? Is half of something unnatural? Is pi unnatural?
So you think we should adopt more descriptive terms?
NO.
I think if we're going to use bad terminology we should stop half-assing it.
My proposal: Natural numbers will be called "boring numbers." Imaginary numbers should be called "bullshit numbers.
Complex numbers should be called "boring bullshit numbers." Hyperreals will be called "big-ass numbers," and irrational numbers will be called "those flockin' things.
Consider the utility here! New categories are now easy to remember, and you can use phrases like "As a platonist I believe in the real existence of bullshit numbers.
Have you created anything interesting or just recategorized known concepts?
That is a matter for philosophers!

comics.comicText:
the Star Trek problem.

...which really makes me wonder what was up with the teleporter operators. I've killed everyone I know hundreds of times! You're welcome, society!

The weird thing to me is that the people in Star Trek are humanists, so they probably don't believe in souls. And, they live in a post-scarcity society, so they don't do their jobs for money.

comics.title: Humans are Special
comics.comicText:
We humans keep thinking we're special. Only to find out we're not. We have language. So do birds. We have culture. So do monkeys.
What do Zorblaxians think is special about humans?
On Zorblax, we call humans "the apes with reasons." You unique among life have stupid reasons for everything.
Your behavior is not in any important way distinct from, say, a squirrel, or a rat. But, unlike the rat, you imagine your behavior holds some meaning beyond its proximate effect.
You kill rivals for resources, but you write songs and essays about why it's complicated and important. Your eating habits, lasting alliances based largely on mutual utility, but you attach a whole philosophy of love and friendship to it.
You can barely even have sex without imagining a mental romance novel!
Humans have FAR more mental processing power than any species in the universe, but 98% of it goes to incorrectly understanding your own behaviors!
If you could just shut up your human voices for one week, you could rule the galaxy!

It's like having clairvoyant beings who detect crime before it happens... only they're a bit daft and racist.

comics.title: The Talk
comics.comicText:
THE TALK
What are you reading?
Nothing! Nothing!
You're growing up so fast. I think it's time we had... THE "TALK.
THE QUANTUM COMPUTING TALK
Agh! It'll be awkward! Look, I have internet access. I know just about what particles do when nobody's looking!
No you don't! What a qubit is?
Of course! It's a quantum bit! You know... a classical bit is either a 0 or 1, or off or on. But, when in a bit 1, qubit are... they can be in a sort of mix of states. They could be like... both 0 and 1 at the same time. "Together." In parallel. "In superposition" (kid is scandalized) eat is both "dead" and alive!
So how would these quantum superpositions help with computation?
Easy! With two qubits, there are four possibilities: 00, 01, 10, 11. With three qubits, there are eight possibilities! And the number doubles with each qubit you add!
So with quantum computers, you just get all these possibilities working on your problem in parallel. Each one a different potential answer!
I wish you wouldn't read those magazines. They're bad for children.
I'm not a child!
Honey, I think your old ideas of how to know the truth about quantum mechanics... quantum computing is not really as good as you think.
Oh? It's not really 0 and 1, on and off? I bet you got 11, it's 0 or 1's, but you just don't know!
Honey, I think you're old enough to know the truth about quantum mechanics. Quantum superposition: it doesn't mean a bit is in MORE than one state at the same time... THINK.
But, if that's so, then what's the big deal about quantum computing?
It means a complex linear combination of states, and you should think of it as a NEW ontological category. There's a complex "amplitude" for each thing that doesn't really map onto any classical concept.
Wait, you guys are not COMPLEX numbers in your ontologies?
We did and we enjoy it!
GWRRR
SHH! A minute. That bring a qubit corresponds to a unit vector in two-dimensional Hilbert space?
Yes! Quantum mechanics is just a certain generalization of probability!
But the probability you learned in preschool only allowed for real numbers between 0 and 1.
Quantum mechanics has probability amplitudes, and they can be positive OR negative OR even complex.
When you make a measurement, there's a rule for computing the probabilities of ordinary measurements. But unlike normal probabilities, these amplitudes can cancel each other out. This is called interference. We could see something very special, and create something that could share something very... intimate.
Kids grow up so fast these days.
Yes, if an event could happen one way with a positive amplitude, and another way with a negative amplitude, the two amplitudes can interfere destructively and cancel out, while the path leading to the right answer reinforces.
And that gives your computer a huge speed boost?
Well, we only have to know how to FIND the path for a few special problems.
Then why did the popular articles lie to me about this?
For generations, physicists and engineers were discussing these matters with outsiders. They wanted to avoid being too "explicit." (panel reads: "too explicit" / "...mathematically precise
Why, when my grandpa taught me about quantum computing, it was always said "there'd be a particle in a box"!
We live in a more open culture now, and kids these days are publishing their first quantum computing papers younger and younger. Your culture and I weren't sure it was time to talk to you yet, but maybe we made a mistake.
We told you kid, this you're growing up and we don't want you to make a mistake.
What is it? You can tell me.
Some of the other kids at school are already doing quantum interference experiments.
Only and just want do they say they're interfering with?
Lots of stuff. Their own ideas. Beliefs. Frogs, even.
Honey, they're not no one has ever created with an obesity that size. It's just a fantasy. Some people talk about it in magazines sometimes.
You'll learn when you're older that a qubit is finicky and fragile. Integers, unless its incredibly well-isolated from its environment.
Otherwise, it's all the rest of the universe. A constantly straining at the qubit. And that gives it its size.
And the bigger something is, the harder it is to isolate. And that's why qubits are usually very, very small. You can see one bit with the naked eye.
It's not the 1/2D that matters. It's the rotation through complex vector space.
Thanks Mom.
Hey?
Yeah?
What about all the other stuff?
What about all the other stuff like Heisenberg's uncertainty principle or wave-particle duality, or tunneling through hallways, or even just getting spooky action at a distance?
If I don't know that stuff, the kids at school will laugh at me!
Relax. It's all just different consequences of one fact. Classical events have probabilities, and quantum events have amplitudes. Remember that, and you'll do just fine.
Guess I won't be needing these any more!
Checking In
All the news in the world?
You never did, buddy. You never did.
THIS HAS BEEN A PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT
IF YOU DON'T TALK TO YOUR KIDS ABOUT QUANTUM COMPUTING...
SOMEONE ELSE WILL.

comics.title: Hiring Metrics
comics.comicText:
The more scientific a field of study is, the more it is driven by creativity and reason, as opposed to personal charisma.
Compare, for instance, the attractive early Freudians, once popular in psychology, to the generally paunchy and funny-haired cognitive neuroscientists of today.
Or consider the trajectory in economics, which runs from the dashing David Ricardo to the Yoda-like Milton Friedman. Note: Economists maintained personal attractiveness right up until the point at which Paul Samuelson mathematized the field.
Fields such as ecology and sociology are in a period of slow uglification that will continue until deeper laws are discovered.
In this department, we use our knowledge of the 'rigor-repulsion axis' to find the very best professors.

I really feel like I arrived at my philosophical views of reality by use of logic. And they're not especially pleasant views.

There's so much stuff that matters, but so little of it matters to my well-being!

One of them chooses to make peace with existence as an unexceptional and short-lived mammal, while the other falls into a self-deluding form of spiritual asceticism, whose demands he is incapable of living out.

We also know that Jesus was buoyant enough to ascend into the heavens.
We also know that, most of the time, he walked on land, which suggests he carried something to weigh him down.
We also know that he walked on water. Thus, we know that while carrying the weights, he was buoyant enough to walk on water, but not buoyant enough to float in the air.
Given the ability to alter his buoyancy at will, and the evidence from other stories, we believe it is likely that he used miraculous fish and bread to adjust his density.
This internal fish and bread generation system acted as a sort of swim bladder, allowing him to select buoyancy and thus move up and down in the air column as needed.
Given these facts, we can comfortably establish that he 'rose after three days' due to a buildup of gasses pertaining to fish putrefaction.

comics.title: On the Etiology of Fuckers

Do organizations attract fuckers, increasing these aggregate fuckery levels? Why have a fucker carrying capacity?
Or does the existence of an organizational structure itself induce fuckery among a subset of members?
After careful analysis, my experiment has discovered that all humans have a fucker quorum-sensing mechanism.

comics.title: Capacity
comics.comicText:
Popular science articles about energy often report dramatic findings like this:
More solar capacity added this year than fossil fuel capacity
Strictly speaking, nothing WRONG was said, but the phrasing can be misleading:
Capacity' is how much power you'd generate if the plant operated constantly. But solar stops operating when the sun goes down.
This is a non-trivial difference.
To figure out 'actual output' of energy, multiply solar capacity by about 0.2, wind by about 0.3, fossil fuel by about 0.5 or nuclear by about 0.9.
W [solar] 0.2, [wind] 0.3]
As a public service, we hereby propose a simple way to remember the difference:
CAPACITY:
Baby, I have the erotic capacity to do it 20 times tonight.
Come with me.
ACTUAL OUTPUT:
Ready for round two?
What, now?
But... but you said..
Look, 5% is pretty good for me, ok?

comics.title: A Proposal
comics.comicText:
The most common factor that prevents human happiness during dates is the intrusion of awkward silences.
98% of awkward silence is caused by the fact that we are all boring hairless apes with nothing interesting to relate.
How else do you explain how two people who've never met can't find ANYTHING to say during a date, despite DECADES of experiences?
We might be able to fix this by just accepting the peace of silence amidst a world of gas, or we could use physics.
I am attempting to gather funding for a new device.
The Relativistic De-Awkwardizer.
Consider Alice and Bob. Bob is about to finish a boring anecdote about a sinus infection, and then the conversation will have no way to move forward.
I think I'm more vulnerable to anal infection than average, however.
Before he finishes speaking, Bob is shunted into an "acceleration tube.
The kind of mucus was apparently typical of that sort of...
In the tube, Bob approaches light speed, experiencing far less time than Alice.
I TOLD THE...
Bob is kept at high speed until Alice comes up with the next topic of conversation.
I enjoy various kinds of music.
Bob is decelerated and returned to the conversation where, from his perspective, he has just finished his awful, meandering story at a normal pace.
...stared up from a week like, yo yeah
The only potential down side, if you can call it that, is that boring people will probably be dead or quite old before the conversation ends.
Given that the relativistic de-awkwardizer would most directly benefit the people most knowledgeable about physics, we expect completion within one year of funding, with the lone snag being that it'd require most energy in the universe.
THIS IS NOT A DEMONSTRATION!! I'M JUST STAYING HERE UNTIL YOU LEAVE!

comics.title: Moral Relativity
comics.comicText:
I'm a moral relativist.
Like, you don't believe in the concept of moral truth?
No. I base my ethical system on my velocity relative to Earth.
That makes no sense.
It's the only view that makes sense.
The closer I am to lightspeed relative to other humans, the more they appear to me to be living their lives in an instant.
The more fleeting their lives, the less significant they seem to me.
How does one assign personhood to a creature that might live and die in the span of one breath?
I just don't think, for instance, you should be allowed to kill someone just because they have a slower reference frame.
What quaint Newtonian morality!!

I'm going to start with a story:
According to Plutarch, Solon was amazed that the first great mathematician, Thales of Miletus, didn't want to marry or have kids.
So, Thales sent a messenger to slowly, tortuously, inform Solon that his son had died.
Whereupon Solon began to beat his head and do and say everything else that betokens a transport of grief
At this point, Thales appeared and took Solon by the hand, saying: 'This it is O Solon, which keeps me from marriage and children; it overwhelms even thee, who art the most stouthearted of men.
But be not dismayed at this story, for it is not true.
So, the point is... that Thales was a giant dickhead?
And you can be too... if you work hard.

comics.title: The Stochastic Tax
comics.comicText:
Will the country create anything of value?
We'll become a sort of tourist attraction for macroeconomists.
comics.hoverText: I'm a quadruple threat. I can go geeky, dorky, nerdy, and now wonky.
comics.voteyText: We can also export misery!
comics.descriptionText:
Heretofore, all tax methods have been considered to have trade-offs. It's time for a new way of thinking. I propose... the STOCHASTIC TAX.
Every possible income level, down to the smallest unit of currency, gets a different and random income tax between 5% and 10,000%.
This tax will be re-randomized and assessed daily.
Every person will thus be required to employ a team of lawyers and accountants to monitor their spending in order to get their wealth to the nearest 5% bracket.
Meanwhile, everyone will pay the minimum tax, but they'll think they're getting away with something clever.
The economy will soon reach full employment, with only white-collar workers. This eliminates the need for welfare.
Thus every citizen will have a valuable job, AND will believe they are getting ahead of their neighbor. This is literally the modern definition of happiness.
Low taxes. Low inequality. High employment. The stochastic tax is FLAWLESS.

Hence the rapid yet unending interboob cycling, whose efficiency apparently did nothing for you.

comics.title: Being an Adult
comics.comicText:
What's the worst thing about being an adult?
Probably the sheer volume of lies.
Like, you know how you lied to me about taking out the trash?
NO!
See, that's a good example. You lied about the trash, but you only had to lie to ME.
Just this week, in order to not exercise, I had to lie to two doctors, one specialist, THREE nurses, a gym owner, God, myself, and four co-workers.
Jeez.
For me to not take out the trash, at a minimum, I would have to lie to Mom, Grandma, Grandpa, the homeowners association, and three to five neighbors.
The older you get, the more people you have to deal with, so the number of lies tends to grow quadratically.
Before you know it, you're on your deathbed, lying to all of your loved ones about what they meant to you. Then, you go to heaven where you try to pull a fast one on St. Peter.
Have adults considered just being honest and open with each other?
Boy, that is how WARS start.

We began testing the algorithm to find the dankness of unflaved precision medicine.
The wiener chihuahua community is gonna eat this up!

WORKS

I analyze wiener dog race outcomes.
We needed help to solve the puzzle, but we soon discovered we were alone.
Hahahahaha!
Why don't anyone believe me?
We wanted cold hard riches for our income.
I don't care how rich we are! I can't sleep at night! How can I work this hard for anything?!
We hungered for truth.
What's our quest for understanding?

Another billion this hour.

Finally, we used our wealth for the only solution we could countenance.
Find the wiener dogs.
Round them up.
End them.
The universe was righted.
Today: Devastating news for the small, wavy dog community.

comics.comicText:
I was reading a book by William Vollmann about dreams.
What?
He once wrote this thing about Pandora.
Hm.
Right?
I heard her once, and once saw the form a little bit. I never see the whole of the thing. I get a few bits of the unraveled stream, and clouds variously plunged across the dark sky. Fall, and walking, like a feeling. But I heard her dripping down from beck to beck. Then, off in endless season, off she went into another world, and all her vague mirror-like masks fly the autumn winds.
And then about a hundred years ago, what was changed so fast that it sounded unsafe to say. Some primitive religion meant a tree or a book. We began like they just spat their pants in front of God.
And while I read this also you could think like a man for ordinary annulled the whole. I would feel it somehow do that.
Is it rationality, are we all so enlightened now, that we can't hold anything to be sacred?
I don't think that's because I know spiritual people, and I would also feel weird about it.
So, what happened? Who killed whatever was alive? Why are pretty brain-washed over to activists and organizations?
Why is it that, even though I am aware that I am wishing to feel the way I can't imagine hanging out with a great writer while sane and feeling worth more about a damn flowerpot?
I'm sorry but this conversation has gotten too vague for my comfort. Can you say something sincere about a guarded insecurity we'd be better off discussing sincerely?
Death is for sucker. I'm gonna live forever.

Instead of giving you five dollars each week during which you were good, you will start each week with the potential for five dollars.

comics.title: Compatibilism
comics.comicText:
COMPATIBILISM: A PARABLE
SCENE 1:
Hey little guy! Do you want to see... a DINOSAUR?
Like, at the museum?
Nope! A real live dinosaur! Today! Now!
LET'S GO!
Did you know that the pigeon is one of the closest living descendants of dinosaurs?
DAMMIT.
You KNEW what I would think when you said there was a dinosaur, and you still did this!
I'm sorry I thought you were intellectual.
SCENE 2:
Hey, philosophy fan! Do you want to see me show that free will is compatible with a deterministic universe?
Really? That sounds impossible!
In fact, it's the only possibility!!
LET'S DISCOURSE!
And so you see your notion of free will was stupid to the point of vacuity. Recognizing this, we can define free will so it IS compatible with determinism.

comics.title: Spandrels
comics.comicText:
Are you familiar with the biological concept of spandrels?
Like, characteristics of species that aren't especially adaptive, but which came into existence as a byproduct of the creation of a good adaptation?
Yeah. Listen... I think our relationship has spandrels.
Like, as part of my "seem interesting to Sally" adaptation, I started tending a plot in an urban organic garden. You claimed to be interested but were mostly excited by the idea that I was thoughtful and unusual.
Now, we both manage a five by five plot of zucchini, even though we'd both rather watch TV, and we both hate zucchini.
My God.
I had assumed all the stuff we do together was for the benefit of our relationship. But, the spandrel theory explains so much-- the antiquing trips... the collaging classes... the novelty knitting projects...
Do you actually like the martinis we started making together?
I've been pouring them down the kitchen sink when you went to the bathroom.
I was pouring mine in the toilet.

Every day for the next forty years.

Recent studies have cast doubt on the so-called effect in psychology, in which people are said to change their behavior in response to subtle environmental cues.
These doubts are needless because we can prove that priming exists analytically.
Imagine an experiment in which subjects are primed to believe priming doesn't work.
If they exhibit priming effects, trivially, priming is real.
If they don't, it shows that we successfully primed them to exhibit no priming effects.
Given that there is only one possible outcome, the experiment is unnecessary.

I call it "encryption by destruction.
You take a piece of information, then destroy it in a random fashion. The information is now so encrypted that you can only get it back by knowing the entire state of the universe and having nearly infinite computing power.
Wowww. Every time we destroy something, maybe we're just sending a message in a bottle to a future race of super-minds!
What an amazing thought, Daddy.
Anyway, point is I accidentally let the cat encrypt your hamster this morning.
comics.hoverText: The word 'decryption' always sounds to me like a fancy term for rising from the grave.
comics.descriptionText: Father (close-up of face, speaking): I also encrypted the rest of your birthday cake.

comics.title: Alive
comics.comicText:
DID YOU KNOW THAT MORE PEOPLE ARE ALIVE TODAY THAN HAVE EVER DIED?
The Garden of Eden was a great place for demographic fun facts.
comics.hoverText: After Adam ate from the tree of knowledge, his punning became so annoying that all humans were banished from Eden.
comics.voteyText: Did you know that 50% of humans are really clever?
comics.descriptionText:
A bearded man with long reddish-brown hair pokes his smiling face up from the bottom of the frame, against a green background. To the right is the dark silhouette of another figure.

A simpler black-and-white line drawing of the same bearded man's face.

comics.title: Mugging
comics.comicText:
GIMME ALL OF YOUR MONEY!
LIQUID ASSETS ONLY, OR ALL ASSETS OF ANY CLASS?
I... WHY?
WELL, THE VAST MAJORITY OF MY WEALTH IS TIED UP IN THE VALUE OF MY HOME. STRICTLY SPEAKING, WHEN YOU CONSIDER DEBT, I DON'T ACTUALLY HAVE ANY MONEY.
I CAN PUT THE HOUSE UP FOR SALE, BUT IN THIS MARKET, IT'LL TAKE 6 TO 12 MONTHS TO FIND A BUYER.
IF I WERE YOU, I'D WAIT TWO OR THREE YEARS, WATCHING INTEREST RATES CLOSELY, THEN MUG ME ONCE THE REAL ESTATE MARKET STABILIZES.
DO YOU HAVE ANYTHING IN YOUR WALLET?
IT'S NOT MINE. I'M RENTING THIS WALLET UNTIL MY STUDENT LOANS ARE PAID.
DO YOU WANT A HUG?
I DON'T WANT TO GET USED TO THE EXPERIENCE OF PERSONAL COMFORT RIGHT NOW.
comics.hoverText: Would you perhaps accept equity in my future earnings?
comics.voteyText: Do you need an intern?

comics.title: Honest Discussion
comics.comicText:
Anyway, that's my concern about society. You understand?
Nah.
In fact, not only do I NOT understand your concern, I've mistaken my lack of understanding for moral clarity!
I could add more nuance.
That would only validate my belief that anything non-obvious is false!
You're hard to argue with.
Just wait till you discover that I interpret frustration as irrationality.
comics.hoverText: The neat part is how everyone reading this will assume it's a judgment on someone else.
comics.voteyText: Best of all, I'm way happier than you!

comics.title: Neoliberal
comics.comicText:
What is best in life, mighty Genghis Khan?
To crush your enemies,
To have them possessing at last the prizes due to economies of scale,
And to take their wives and introduce them into the labor force!
I can't tell, you's more cruel or kind.
I don't recognize those words.
comics.hoverText: Oh please oh please don't let anyone take this as for or against any position.
comics.voteyText:
No. Stop. You don't need to tell me the quote is apocryphal.
Zach

comics.comicText:
Sweetie, I need you to fly home.
What? Why?
It's your father... it... it doesn't look good...
Where's Dad? Is he all right?!
I'm fine. I just decided to grow a goatee, okay?
It doesn't look good.
I think we should pull the plug.
comics.hoverText: Also there is infinite space, so it's going to be pretty hard to find the movie theater.

dark
light

DO YOU REALLY THINK THIS'LL WORK?
NO, BUT IF IT DOES, WE'LL BE GODS.

comics.title: Advanced
comics.comicText:
How's my degree, doc?
I'm afraid it's advanced.
You've reached stage four credentialing.
What's stage five?
There is no stage five.
What are my options?
You can go into the private sector where none of your skills will be used because they're not profitable, or go into the public sector, where none of your skills will be used because you're busy navigating the bureaucracy.
Can you prescribe me anything?
I'm a doctor of comparative literature. I can't prescribe shit.
comics.hoverText: If I had a PhD in humanities, by God I would wear a labcoat and goggles all day long.
comics.voteyText: I will, however, share my drugs.

comics.title: It Doesn't Look Good
comics.comicText:
SWEETIE, I NEED YOU TO FLY HOME.
WHAT? WHY?
IT'S YOUR FATHER... IT DOESN'T LOOK GOOD...
LATER THAT DAY...
The red-haired daughter has arrived and rushes in, alarmed.
WHERE'S DAD? IS HE ALL RIGHT?!
I'M FINE. I JUST DECIDED TO GROW A GOATEE, OKAY?
IT DOESN'T LOOK GOOD.
I THINK WE SHOULD PULL THE PLUG.
comics.hoverText: His socks and sandals are, on the other hand, exquisite.
comics.voteyText: Even if we can't see it... he's suffering

comics.title: Dear God
comics.comicText:
Dear Lord, why do bad things happen to good people?
Hey, I got a question for you.
How do you know I'm really God? How do you know you're not praying to a demon or something?
I feel your presence, Lord.
If I were a demon, wouldn't I try to make you FEEL like I'm God?
God wouldn't allow that.
Are you sure? What if a demon implanted that thought into you?
See, you get into a sort of regression problem. Anything you think you know ultimately depends on something you can't be certain of.
There may be true things, but you can never be sure of them.
That was mean, God.
But see, he TOTALLY forgot about the whole bad-things-good-people issue!
comics.hoverText: Later, God starts to wonder if he can trust his own self-perception.
comics.voteyText: That's messed up, dude.
comics.descriptionText: (The man stands silently, looking troubled.)

comics.title: Fish Don't Feel Pain
comics.comicText:
Recent scientific studies suggest that fish do not feel pain in the same sense that humans do.
As a philosopher of ethics, this finding could undermine 30 years of my life's work.
I have therefore teamed up with geneticists to take pain perception genes from loveable intelligent dolphins and transplant them into a species of salmon.
So... if someone asks whether fish feel pain... the answer is...
SOON.
comics.hoverText: There should be a field of science dedicated to ruining thought experiments.
comics.voteyText: The fishy's name is Ouchie!

comics.title: The Real Me
comics.comicText:
WHAT I LOVE ABOUT YOU, MECHATRON-9X, IS THAT YOU SEE THE REAL ME.
YOU ARE TALKING MEAT.
IT'S LIKE YOU'VE KNOWN ME MY WHOLE LIFE!
comics.hoverText: I DO NOT SEE THIS AS A LONG-TERM THING, HUMAN.

comics.title: Heavenly
comics.comicText:
In heaven, there is no pain, physical or emotional.
Is that why everybody has sharp objects stuck in them?
Yep. Nobody notices.
We lose a lot of people to fire as well.
Lose?
Yeah, they don't realize they're on fire, then they're gone. No idea where they go.
Does that bother you?
No negative emotions.
Brilliant.
comics.hoverText: Secretly, the reader began to suspect that Zach only made Heaven jokes to avoid drawing backgrounds.
comics.voteyText: Hooray!
comics.descriptionText: A smiling person whose hair is depicted as flames, completely surrounded by fire, says cheerfully.

comics.title: Monism
comics.comicText:
Monists believe there is no distinction between mind and body.
Dualists believe mind and body are, in some sense, separate aspects of being.
There's a lively debate here, but the important point is that both are talking about the same human beings.
This proves that you can add 1 to the quantity of aspects without altering the being itself.
By induction, you can be a monist, dualist, triplist, quadruplist, and so on. I am literally infinite-aspected. The greatest philosopher in ontology-space.
Personally, I am a ten-to-the-twenty-fourth-ist. I believe every one of the aspects is meaningful but meaningless distinct.
You've taken a difficult philosophy problem and reduced it to a solvable but pointless counting problem.
You may also be interested in my work on firewalls.
comics.hoverText: Personally, I am a triplist because I think we have mind, body-except-left-earlobe and left earlobe.
comics.voteyText: I'm a 1.1ist. Body + 10% focused mind.

comics.title: Taffy
comics.comicText:
Saltwater taffy is proof that the ocean is beautiful and sublime.
How so?
Do you like taffy?
I guess I don't normally buy it.
Can you imagine buying off-brand taffy, rolling it in salt, and eating it?
I probably wouldn't.
And yet here we are, buying it, eating a whole box. Why a whole box in one sitting? Because when we're away from the ocean it'll no longer be desirable.
There is some alternate reality where people stare at oceans and eat pickled fish-eyes or cotton candy beef jerky. Here, it's salted taffy.
God it tastes like shit.
PS: It's the last day to support our new Kickstarter! Click to check it out!
comics.hoverText: I am prepared to fight about this, Internet. Come at me.
comics.voteyText: Why do I have the feeling that this comic will get more hatemail than any before?

comics.title: Voters
comics.comicText:
WHAT PEOPLE SAY THEY WANT FROM THEIR LEADERS:
They need to compromise to get things done.
HOW PEOPLE REACT WHEN THEIR LEADERS COMPROMISE TO GET THINGS DONE:
You traitor to human DECENCY! I'm gonna go get the craziest MORON I can find, then VOTE FOR HIM!
comics.hoverText: When I said you should compromise, I didn't mean about the thing that matters to ME!
comics.voteyText: I only meant the OTHER SIDE should compromise!

comics.title: Dream Inequality
comics.comicText:
WE DISCOVERED A MASSIVE SOCIAL INEQUALITY
I MEAN, IF YOU HAD AS MANY GREAT DREAMS AS ME, YOU'D BE A GAZILLIONAIRE AND A FIREBALL!
HE DID?
IT'S NOT FAIR!
SOCIOLOGISTS INVESTIGATED
APPARENTLY, DREAMS PEAK AT AGE 7, AFTER WHICH THEY TAPER OFF, CONVERGING TO ALMOST NOTHING BY AGE 12.
US ADULTS ARE THE 99%.
SOCIOLOGISTS MADE SUGGESTIONS
WE NEED TO GET CHILDREN TO SAVE THEIR DREAMS IN PLEDGES.
HOW ABOUT WE FORCE THEM INTO A NO-BANKRUPTCY-ALLOWED HIGH-INTEREST LOAN IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE A CERTIFICATE THAT QUALIFIES THEM FOR A MIDDLE-CLASS JOB?
THAT JUST SEEMS DECADENT.
POLITICIANS ACTED ON SUGGESTIONS
WE NEED TO MAKE SURE THE KEY IS A HEALTHY ECONOMY, BUT A LITERALLY VERY SMALL PORTION OF THE POPULATION CONTROLS ALL OF THEIR GOOD GAS. THEY'VE GOT CHILDREN'S GAS, CHILDREN ARE THE FUTURE, SO THEY OUGHT TO START PAYING NOW.
THERE WAS SOME PUSHBACK AGAINST ELITES
A 2% NATIONAL DREAM TAX? DAMNED DREAM PLEBEIANS. I'D DREAM UP A WAY TO DESTROY THEM, BUT THEY'D TAX THAT TOO!
MOTHER! ANOTHER BRANDIES AND TONIC!
AS THE NEW SYSTEM PROGRESSED, SOCIOLOGISTS NOTICED EMERGENT EFFECTS
APPARENTLY, ANOTHER NIGHT DREAMING MAKES THE AIRBRUSH ADULT LESS HAPPY. I WONDER WHY?
HAD CAREER, I'LL NEVER BE THE LUNCHTIME ASTRONAUT I WAS MEANT TO BE.
THE MORE THEY CALCULATED, DREAMS WERE TAXED, THE MORE ADULT THEY BECAME...
HEY! SUSIE JAMARA CAME TO MY TREEHOUSE AND PLAY FRUGAL PERSONAL FINANCE!
HOORAY!
BUT, BY TAKING THE SYSTEM WAS WORKABLE OR DEFENSIBLE
THE YOUNGEST PEOPLE CAN AFFORD TO FULFILL THEIR DREAMS. EVERYONE ELSE IS SAD.
WE NEED TO PETITION THE SUPREME COURT TO LET THEM KNOW THEY UNHELD THIS SYSTEM.
THEY DEFTED US A PERSONHOOD GRANT?
ON THE PLUS SIDE, OLD RICH PEOPLE HAD FAR MORE IMAGINOS
I AM BATMAN! WHEE!
Batman: HMMMM. THERE REMAINS A BIT OF GENERATIONAL STRIFE.
NOW THAT YOU'VE TAKEN ALL ADULT'S DREAMS, COULD YOU AT LEAST SHARE SOME OF THE WEALTH?
I FEEL YOU'VE THESE DAYS THESE KIDS ARE SO ENTITLED.
THIS BONUS UPDATE IS THANKS TO PEOPLE WHO PREORDERED SOONISH! THANK YOU! CLICK FOR MORE INFO.
comics.hoverText: I swear, I don't mean this comic to harbor any political perspective. I just thought it was funny.
comics.voteyText: Batarang!
comics.descriptionText: A Batman figure with a spiky cape gleefully shouts as a cartoonish hand throws a bat-shaped object at a wide-eyed bat creature.

comics.title: Regression
comics.comicText:
You get more beautiful every day.
What?!
By how much? Is it a lot?
We've been together for 20 years! How ugly was I on day one!?
Am I a pity wife? Is that the point you're making?!
No! No! That's not it at all!
20 YEARS AGO):
estimated attractiveness
age,
This is a good investment.

IF I WERE A PILOT, I WOULD MAKE UP NEW PHYSICS FOR EVERY FLIGHT.
A commercial passenger airplane (gray with an orange-red stripe along the fuselage and wings) flies through a blue sky over green hills. A speech bubble emanates from the cockpit area.
AND NOW, WE JETTISON OUR CENTER OF MASS, MAKING US WEIGHTLESS SO THAT WE CAN FLY.
comics.hoverText: I really don't understand why we load down rockets with centers of mass.
comics.voteyText: As we reach cruising altitude, please hold your breathe so that we float.

Hey kid! Build your own fuckin' toy, OK?
Of course, they didn't become popular until they were renamed "Legos.
comics.hoverText: What I really want is a Star Wars Lego kit made of exactly two enormous pieces.
comics.voteyText: Play-doh was called "stop playing with food dough, you little shit.

comics.title: A New Method
comics.comicText:
ME HAVE METHOD FOR KNOWING HOW MANY ROCKS YOU HAVE. CALLED 'COUNTING.' PUT UP FINGERS, THEN SAY—
WE EVER USE THIS IN REAL LIFE?
The first math class.
comics.hoverText: I guess I'd better not tell him about my collection of uncountably infinite rocks.
comics.voteyText: Maybe you like real death?!

comics.title: Pickup Line
comics.comicText:
Esthie, man! You're a neuroscientist! You wanna hear an intellectual pickup line?
Like what?
I was just reading a thought experiment of Daniel Dennett where he imagined a brain where you put a thimble in someone's brain, but the thimble keeps moving around so they can probe it, but the prison is closest to it. Can't.
That's fascinating.
Wait... what's it called?
And so...
Hey, there! Wanna play a game of hide the thimble?

comics.title: IUSASW
comics.comicText:
no dialogue here; the red-haired man speaks
Why am I applying, you ask?
I guess I've always had an attraction to abstraction.
To break something into its fundamental components, understand what they mean separately, then reassemble them.
INTERNATIONAL UNION OF SOCKS AND SANDALS WEARERS. A speech bubble from the building says: Welcome.
comics.hoverText: Incidentally, this explains why all of your math professors wear socks and sandals.
comics.voteyText: JOIN US
comics.descriptionText: Interviewer (now seen from the front, a man in a suit, looking moved): Yes, that's it. I've never heard it phrased so beautifully.

comics.title: Simulationism
comics.comicText:
I'm a rebellious simulationist. I believe we're in a simulation, and therefore we should do whatever we can do to annoy the creatures running it.
How would you possibly do that?
Beauty and truth.
We should create novel art, which alters our culture, completely screwing up any compression methods that formerly worked on human behavior.
We should discover new facts and seek new places and configurations of matter. Because all these things will take enormous rendering time.
We should push the boundaries of human imagination! We should seek our fortune throughout the cosmos! We should become our most impossible selves!
Because that would cost the simulators a fortune in server fees.
Huh. Well, I think we're just in a real universe.
How do you go on like that?
How do you maintain an interest in poetry or science or philosophy without the foundational belief that it's all for revenge?
I guess I just think they're nice.
Well that's adorable, sweetie.
comics.hoverText: Ironically, in this comic I'm reusing stock characters.
comics.voteyText: Human aspiration isn't all about revenge! A lot of it is avarice!
comics.descriptionText: Two people stand talking in a snowy landscape under a starry night sky. One has dark skin, glasses, a green sweater, and a dark red scarf (the simulationist). The other has light skin, short reddish-orange hair, and a yellow sweater.

comics.title: Rain
comics.comicText:
God, why'd you create conservation of energy? Why can't you get something for nothing?
But you can.
You mean like... how we gain from intangible things, like friendship, love, compassion?
No, like from magnets.
Watch, you just take magnets and put them in a circle. Drop in a piece of iron and WHAM! It goes around forever. Free energy.
Honestly, how did you guys miss this?
We have to kill all the physicists.
comics.hoverText: Mammatus clouds are what God watches when He's getting high.
comics.voteyText: Not for fame. Strictly for evil.

comics.title: There and Back Again
comics.comicText:
THIS DOESN'T SEEM RIGHT, BILBO.
OK? AND GETTING EATEN BY SPIDERS DOES?
Getting through Mirkwood Forest was a lot easier once we started using chemical defoliants.
comics.hoverText: Tom, Tom Bomba--COUGH COUGH HACK--
comics.voteyText: Nut up, Gandalf. It's business.

comics.title: Ethical Consumption
comics.comicText:
But why would you eat US? Why not eat cows or pigs?
Sorry, that wouldn't be ethical.
We don't believe in eating lower order animals. Cows, chicken, sheep... they aren't smart enough to understand and prepare for death. They can't be made to know that pain is just an electro-chemical process.
Therefore, the most ethical diet is made entirely of conscious, intelligent, sentient beings.
The fact that humans have created art, science, poetry, philosophy, civilization... it all goes to show that you should be eaten.
Probably grilled.
If that's the case, why don't you guys eat yourselves?
WHOA. Whoa there, buddy. I am not conscious. I'm just a stimulus-response machine.
Frankly, I'm offended!
...but...
Only because of a deterministic process in my non-conscious brain.
Your moral philosophy seems a bit unformed.
Also, we have anti-matter bombs aimed at Earth.
*sigh* Can I be flash frozen or fried or something else quick?
I'm afraid my machine-like cognitive apparatus favors slow-roasting.
comics.hoverText: We'll also be eating dolphins, whales, bonobos, chimps, cephalopods, and particularly intelligent dogs.
comics.voteyText: Or kebabs.

comics.title: Relative Heaven
comics.comicText:
Look, the idea of heaven doesn't make sense.
Human happiness tends to be relative, not absolute. That'd require us to look down on everyone else in heaven. But that'd diminish THEIR happiness.
Here in heaven, everyone thinks everyone else is crap, and thanks to the loving presence of God, they don't realize that they themselves are crap.
Is that why every person I pass gives me that condescending smirk?
It's not condescending. It's deferential to your superior intellect.
That makes perfect sense.
comics.hoverText: In Hell, everyone is friendly and nice, but nobody realizes it.
comics.voteyText: This also occurs at academic conferences.

comics.title: Product Placement
comics.comicText:
BEST USE OF A TIME MACHINE: INTRODUCING PRODUCT PLACEMENT INTO MAJOR MOMENTS IN HISTORY
THAT'S RIGHT! AND YOU KNOW WHAT IS SO SOFT AND PILLOWY AND DELICIOUS THAT YOU'LL THINK IT'S BEEN RISING FOR THREE DAYS? PIZZA HUT'S STUFFED CRUST PIZZA!
comics.hoverText: Also, maybe Buddha can say that it doesn't count as attachment if you want another round of Buffalo wings.
comics.voteyText: Now to ascend to flavor Heaven!

The bearded man (now drawn in simple black-and-white line art, smiling).

comics.title: S
comics.comicText:
Superman, why do you spend the time to change your costume before saving the day?
It works.
Branding.
But it takes like an extra ten seconds for you to change outfit. If there's a big fight going on, that probably costs lives.
What costs lives is people not being aware of Superman.
As long as all people, criminal or otherwise, are aware that an all-powerful man, beloved by all authority figures, is watching at all times, society is better off.
I can spare a few lives at the margin as long as I am certain that whenever people sub-consciously stray into thoughts of disobedience, they instantly visualize a bright primary-colored "S", and the slogan "Truth, Justice, and the American way.
That strikes me as vaguely fascist.
You know, just a little -
Are you thinking of slandering a beloved public figure?
This sounds like a job for Super-
Nevermind! Nevermind!
comics.hoverText: The best part about considering myself a brand is that even my most potentially honorable acts have been sullied by PR considerations!
comics.voteyText: I can tell by the way you've soiled yourself that you love justice.

comics.title: Perpetual Motion
comics.comicText:
GOD, WHY'D YOU CREATE CONSERVATION OF ENERGY? WHY CAN'T YOU GET SOMETHING FOR NOTHING?
BUT YOU CAN.
YOU MEAN LIKE... HOW WE GAIN FROM INTANGIBLE THINGS, LIKE FRIENDSHIP, LOVE, COMPASSION?
NO, LIKE FROM MAGNETS.
WATCH, YOU JUST TAKE MAGNETS AND PUT THEM IN A CIRCLE. DROP IN A PIECE OF IRON AND WHAM! IT GOES AROUND FOREVER. FREE ENERGY.
HONESTLY, HOW DID YOU GUYS MISS THIS?
WE HAVE TO KILL ALL THE PHYSICISTS.
comics.hoverText: Also, have you tried shining a flashlight into a solar panel?
comics.voteyText: With an infinity-powered laser.

comics.title: Family Vote
comics.comicText:
Ooh, tough luck, kids. One vote for vacation at Disneyland. Two votes for spending summer reading the dictionary and not talking back.
Oh? Democracy isn't fair?!
But that's not fair!
Parenting became a lot easier after we gerrymandered the house.
comics.hoverText: Let's be clear, kids. It's not *just*. It's potentially fair.
comics.voteyText: Just wait ten years for redistricting
comics.descriptionText: Father (a man with glasses and a red shirt, holding a tablet/device, seated on a couch next to a woman).

comics.title: A Bar Joke
comics.comicText:
AN AMERICAN, AN ENGLISHMAN, AND IRISHMAN ENTER A BAR
CONCERNED THAT THEY ARE THE INHABITANTS OF A JOKE, THEY BECOME WARY.
KNOWING THAT BAR JOKES OFTEN END IN HUMILIATION OR DEATH, EACH MAN IMPROVISES A WEAPON.
SEEING EACH OTHER MAN'S WEAPON, EACH ELECTS TO ATTACK ANOTHER.
THE AMERICAN SUFFERS A BLOW TO THE SKULL WITH AN IRON BAR. THE ENGLISHMAN AND IRISHMAN ARE SO REVOLTED THEY STAND SILENT AS THE WATCH HIM FLOP AND GIBBER AND DIE.
LATER, THE IRISHMAN AND ENGLISHMAN ARE INTERROGATED BY THE POLICE.
FORTUNATELY, THE PUNCHLINE COMES BEFORE THEY ARE SENT TO JAIL.
WHAT HAPPENED TO THE AMERICAN?! ANSWER ME!
HE... HE WALKED INTO A BAR... AND SAID "OUCH!
THIS BONUS COMIC COURTESY OF "SOONISH" PRE-ORDERERS. FOR GOD'S SAKE, CLICK TO BY IT NOW!
comics.hoverText: 'Why the long face?' 'Because I'm a murderer.'
comics.voteyText: It was the one day the American went out unarmed.

comics.title: Philosophy of Sandwiches
comics.comicText:
Can I have a bite of your sandwich?
But, it's the same sandwich. We ordered the same sandwich.
Impossible! Sandwiches are not platonic entities.
The tomato in your BLT came from a different seed! Your lettuce a different field! Your bacon a different pig! You cannot taste the same mayonnaise twice!
Gimme a bite of your sandwich, you half-wit!
It tastes about the same.
Can I have a bite of yours?
Nah.
comics.hoverText: In Postmodernism, everything is a sandwich.
comics.voteyText: I hate Aristotelian sandwiches.
comics.descriptionText: Man (holding sandwich, no dialogue).

comics.title: Kidproof
comics.comicText:
I have kidnapped my office!
You... what?
Well, I jailproofed the kitchen!
Suppose I'm the strangest, most dextrous member of the household...
Behold!
Cost to enter: $20/hour, or harbor thereof.
Toll free even if I say I go in for a vault?!
And no discount for vacation? Hahahahahaha!!
Trapped! Trapped!
comics.hoverText: You can also 'dad-prone' an area by introducing inexpensive 3-packs of plain white underwear into the environment.
comics.voteyText: I suppose this is death.
