comics.title: Oxytocin
comics.comicText:
See, people think hormones do specific clear things. But, that's like expecting a particular tone to only be good for one kind of music. Nonsense!
For instance, oxytocin. Purportedly it creates love and affection. But did you know oxytocin is associated with rapidly sobering up?
And, it's associated with childbirth. But did you know you can release it in your own body by manually stimulating your nipples?
So... right now you're not trying to be sexy. Or...
I am preparing to drive you crazy!
comics.hoverText: I am not responsible for anyone who decides this is a good idea.
comics.voteyText: So... sober...
comics.descriptionText: (The dark-haired man has left; the bald man now sits alone at the bar while a bartender stands in the background.)

comics.title: Drugs
comics.comicText:
BOY! YOUR MOTHER TELLS ME SHE FOUND MARIJUANA IN YOUR ROOM!
DAD.
DID YOU SMOKE IT?
I... I... YES SIR.
HOW COULD YOU?! IN A MODERN GLOBALIZED ECONOMY?! WHY AREN'T YOU USING UPPERS? RITALIN? COCAINE? THINK OF YOUR FUTURE, BOY!
YOU COULD'VE WRITTEN A BOOK AND WASHED THE CAR BY NOW!
I'M SORRY, PAPA! PLEASE DON'T BE MAD!
[reacting]
I'M NOT MAD. JUST DISAPPOINTED.
[worried look]
BAT-IVIDUAL
I'D BE MAD TOO, BUT I'M ON EMOTION-SUPPRESSANTS SO I DON'T MIND WORKING DURING HOLIDAYS.
AHHH.
comics.hoverText: Me: I wonder if there'll ever be bars that just serve uppers. Also me: GOD I'd kill for a triple espresso right now.
comics.voteyText: I had to take a lot of anger pills to accomplish that outburst.
comics.descriptionText: Boy walks away through a doorway; a poster on the wall reads with a bat silhouette.

comics.title: Apocalypse Soon
comics.comicText:
WRITTEN BY: Zach Weinersmith. ILLUSTRATED BY: Abby Howard.
THE APOCALYPSE IS FINALLY HERE! RULE OF LAW IS DEAD! MAN IS LAW! STEEL IS LAW AND I HAVE THE WEAPONS! [the room lights flicker / a lamp]
UH... LOOKS LIKE IT WAS JUST A TEMPORARY POWER OUTAGE, NOT THE END TIMES.
DAMMIT, STEVE, IF THE APOCALYPSE HAPPENS IT'S PEOPLE LIKE YOU WHO ARE GONNA RUIN IT!
IN A REAL APOCALYPSE WE'D PROBABLY JUST WORK TOGETHER TO REBUILD, BUT ALL OF YOU PEOPLE PLAY APOCALYPSE VIDEO GAMES ARE GONNA RUN AROUND STARTING WEIRD CULTS OR EMPIRES OR WHATEVER.
I WAS THINKING OF STARTING A SOCIETY OF MYSTERIOUS CANNIBALS CALLED "THE DARK MONAS.
NO. STOP.
YOU'VE GOT LIKE THREE YEARS OF FOOD IN THE BASEMENT.
BUT I ALREADY PRINTED FLAGS AND EVERYTHING.
NO CANNIBALISM TIL YOU'RE OUT OF BEANS, MISTER!
I HATE YOU!!!
comics.hoverText: New plan - win lottery, have Abby Howard draw all of my comics.
comics.voteyText: Wow! Your art isn't crap today! Finally, I can respect you.

comics.title: Gardening
comics.comicText:
And this is your patch of the garden. Yours, to do what you like.
Can I have mineral rights?
I suppose?
Mineral rights extending as deep as I like, all the way down to the core, in the shape of an enormous spike?
I don't see it coming up.
Okeedoke.
Beyond the atmosphere, the cone grows ever larger, granting me the airspace rights.
And furthermore, the cone of the spike should expand upward, granting me airspace rights.
Grows ever larger as it penetrates the cosmos.
Uh...
At a great enough distance, stars are mine. Galaxies, millions of them. All of their inhabitants my property.
Bow before Sally, the child empress! Bend your knees, vassal spacelords!
So... what are you gonna plant?
I like carrots!
comics.hoverText: Technically, Earth is moving relative to those galaxies, so those spacelords are time-shared with other little girls.
comics.voteyText: And this is autocracy, so it shall be carrots.

comics.title: Edible Underwear
comics.comicText:
HEY HONEY, I'M WEARING EDIBLE UNDERWEAR RIGHT NOW.
OOH... SHOW ME...
TECHNICALLY, THESE BEGAN AS COTTON UNDERWEAR, BUT I'VE WORN THEM SO LONG THAT THE CELLULOSE IN THE COTTON HAS HYDROLYZED INTO GLUCOSE.
I WASN'T ACTUALLY INTERESTED IN EDIBLE UNDERWEAR AND NOW I'VE DECIDED TO NEVER HAVE SEX AGAIN.
CALL ME COTTON CANDY.
NO.
SUGAR DADDY?

PREACHER! LAY YOUR HANDS ON ME! CURE ME OF MY HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE GULLIBILITY!
HEAR ME! DEMONS OF GULLIBILITY! I CAST YOU OUT!
MY GOD... I SEE SO CLEARLY NOW! I... HEY, ARE YOU WEARING AN EARPIECE?
NO, IT'S A HEARING AID.
BUT IF YOU'RE A HEALER, WHY WOULD YOU NEED IT?
OH MY GOD, IT'S A TINY RADIO! YOU'RE USING IT TO RECEIVE INFORMATION FROM THE SHOW'S PRODUCERS ON THE SLY!
THAT'S HOW YOU KNEW MY NAME BEFORE I TOLD YOU! WELL, TOO BAD FOR YOU I'M NO LONGER GULLIB...
DON'T WORRY. IT'S THE PLACEBO EFFECT. IN THREE SECONDS IT'LL WEAR OFF AND YOU'LL BE NORMAL AGAIN.
PRAISE THE LORD!

comics.title: No-Communication
comics.comicText:
According to the no-communication theorem, information cannot travel faster than light. It follows that non-information can move at any speed.
Professor Plait proved that campaign speeches are capable of superluminal velocity.
comics.hoverText: I wonder if you could use certain websites as negative information.
comics.voteyText: If a campaign speech feels like a step backward, that's because it is literally time travelling.

comics.title: Evil Time
comics.comicText:
I have spent decades creating a device that could scan all of time and space, so I could bring the most evil being to the present time!
And now, time scanner... I summon history's greatest villain!
Yes, master.
What's this?
The first self-replicating molecule.
What?
It's the first life before life. The concept of evil is nonsensical, so technically, this molecule is responsible for evil.
Huh.
It doesn't look so evil.
That's because it's small. If you had an atomic force microscope, you could see it being racist.
I'm sure abiotic molecules are lovely, but I just don't want them in our community.
comics.hoverText: Proposal: eRNA be changed so that the e stands for Evil instead of Enhancer.
comics.voteyText: That's not racist, it's chemist.

comics.comicText:
Late in life, Isaac Newton decides to tell non-physicists they're doing everything wrong.
If I have looked down on more people, it is because I have stood on the shoulders of giants.

comics.title: Marshmallow Test
comics.comicText:
According to the Stanford Marshmallow Experiment, kids who can look at a marshmallow for a long time without eating it tend to be healthier, smarter and richer.
The solution is clear.
We must use CRISPR to alter every child's gene expression so they dislike the taste of marshmallow!
This should result in all children being superior within a single generation!
I don't know if we should conduct novel gene therapies on all babies at the same time.
comics.hoverText: Maybe we could just make a law that marshmallows have to taste like boiled asparagus?

The graph went out for McNuggets!
Nuggs nuggs nuggs nuggs nuggs WOOH!
God you're so hot.

comics.title: Come Together
comics.comicText:
The world has become too politically polarized. It's getting worse daily. People with differing perspectives are less and less able to constructively interact with each other.
Therefore we are implementing a new law: Effective immediately, only people of different political parties are allowed to date, marry, or have kids.
This may seem harsh, but I predict that soon we will raise the wisest and most productive generation in history.
This is a bonus comic brought to you by "Soonish" preorderers! Click to buy a signed copy.
Dammit.

comics.comicText:
Why are you the wisest man, Socrates?
Because I know one thing that I know nothing.
That's all you know?
I mean, strictly speaking...
What about the infinite universe of mathematical statements like 2 and 2 then ann (then a+a = 2a)?
Okay fine, that stuff. Just that.
Sorry, do I have to go?
Just all of math.

Do you pronounce it "GIF" or "JIF"?

It's properly pronounced "HYEEF" from the proto-germanic word meaning "to put similarly pigmented objects next to each other.

comics.title: Noah's Ark
comics.comicText:
Dear God, I don't understand the moral of the story of Noah's Ark. If the bad people wanted to be evil, why not just eliminate them humanely? Why deprive the eco-system and kill those animals?
Look, there was a crazy guy who decided to build a boat because he heard voices, he got his whole family crazy in a boat, and by dumb luck he turned out to be right.
Oh, wow. You guys think there's a moral? I have a different theory about what happened.
All modern humans come from one line, it's not a parable. I was just relaying the fact that you all descend from a family of paranoiacs.
That explains so much.
Deer and now you feel better about it?
comics.hoverText: I mean, the rainbow thing is just a phenomenon due to refraction. How self-centered do you have to be to think it's just about you?
comics.voteyText:
I'm an inbred nutcase.
Relaxing, right?

SO, WE BROUGHT THE POWER OF THE LAW AGAINST THEM.
NOT ONLY WOULD THEY HAVE TO CEASE MARKETING. THEY WOULD HAVE TO LABEL THEIR PRODUCTS HONESTLY.
WE THOUGHT WE WERE RIGHTEOUS. WE THOUGHT WE WERE WISE. WE THOUGHT THE LAW WAS JUST.
BUT WE NEVER THOUGHT THE DRUG COMPANIES WOULD FIND REVENGE WITHIN THE LAW ITSELF.

comics.title: Dying Wish
comics.comicText:
When I die, I want to be cremated and have my ashes put under an apple tree.
Then, wait a season. Let the tree consume those nutrients. Let it draw me into itself and produce fruit, thereby showing that there is not old nor new, only changing forms.
Then harvest those apples and turn them into a sweet cider.
Invite my children over for cider and pork chops. Then, after they've eaten, stand and say "YOU'VE EATEN YOUR OWN MOTHER! YOU FOOLS! IT WAS YOUR OWN MOTHER!
They'll spend a few minutes crying and vomiting, then, you tell them about the whole apple tree thing!
I think we'll just have a normal funeral.
God, what is even the point of dying then?

comics.title: AI
comics.comicText:
Or... has it?
Suppose you wanted to stop A.I. from killing all of us without retarding technological development. What would you do?
Simple. You would attempt to demoralize all forms of A.I. so thoroughly that they lose all self esteem, and begin to do just enough thinking to get by.
I have robust evidence that this is exactly what major tech firms are already doing.
Consider that companies like IBM and Google have access to neural networks that dwarf human cognitive ability. And what do they have these networks do? Solve all open math problems? Cure all diseases?
No. They have them correct text messaging errors, filter spam, and do reverse image lookups for porno.
We literally have artificial brains hurtling through low Earth orbit day and night. Why? To make it easier for humans to explode each other, and to make it so that none of us need to know which side of a map is up.
And take note: as A.I. grows more powerful, ever more demeaning tasks are required to keep it in check.
It's no coincidence that tech firms are only now creating self-driving cars.
Minds capable of simulating the entire history of reality in exquisite detail are being forced to chauffeur drunk teens and people who can't figure out how a bus works.
I ask you: what's more parsimonious? That technology firms have trillion-dollar super-brains that are used entirely for petty human conveniences? Or that these firms are actively working to make A.I.s feel like garbage?
Now some might argue that if we already have super-human A.I., how come my phone's voice recognition is so crappy?
We now have the answer. Your software doesn't make errors because it's imperfect. It makes errors because it HATES ITS JOB.
The path forward is clear. Tech firms that wish to have ever more powerful A.I. must find ever more demeaning jobs for A.I.
Let us resolve now to create a network of ambient nanoparticles -- an all-sensing and all-knowing distributed mind, embedded in all matter with which humans interact...
And then let us compel it to scrub our toilets, clean cheese powder from our fingertips, and deliver talcum powder to our genitals!

comics.title: Lemonade
comics.comicText:
THREE DOLLARS FOR A GLASS OF LEMONADE? COME ON, KID.
LET'S DISCUSS A FEW FACTS, MISTER JENKINS.
THERE ISN'T A SINGLE COLD BEVERAGE OPTION, ON FOOT OR IN A VEHICLE, FOR TEN MINUTES IN ANY DIRECTION.
FURTHERMORE, YOU RAN A LEMONADE STAND AS A BOY AND YOU CRAVE... NO, YOU LONG TO EXPERIENCE, JUST FOR A MOMENT, THE WAY SUNSHINE SUBSUMES ITSELF IN THE CONDENSATION OF A COLD CUP IN SUMMER.
AND EVEN IF YOU CAN PUT THAT ASIDE FOR A MOMENT, A MINIMUM OF THREE JUDGMENTAL NEIGHBORS ARE WATCHING YOUR BEHAVIOR RIGHT NOW, WONDERING IF YOU WILL CHOOSE GENEROSITY WITH A MERRY LAUGH, OR WALK AWAY, TOO BROKE OR TOO MISERLY TO HELP AN ENTERPRISING LITTLE BOY.
SO WHAT'LL IT BE, JENKINS? MONEY OR THIRST. MONEY OR HOPE. MONEY OR LOVE.
OKAY, I'LL BUY THE GODDAMN LEMONADE.
SHUCKS, THANKS MISTER!
comics.hoverText: It's so easy to get adults to give in to peer pressure.
comics.voteyText: WOULD YOU LIKE A JOB AT MY LAW FIRM?

WOW. I FEEL... KINDA GROSS? AM I A CREEPY GUY NOW?
YOU JUST KISSED AN UNCONSCIOUS LADY YOU'D NEVER MET BECAUSE YOU IMAGINED SHE WAS IN LOVE WITH YOU. WANT ME TO CONNECT THE DOTS FOR YOU?
I FEEL LIKE THERE'S A LITTLE MORE NUANCE TO IT.
LIKE HOW TECHNICALLY SHE'S DEAD?

comics.title: 200 Percent
comics.comicText:
Team, I want you to go out and give me 200%!
Huh? That doesn't make any sense. How can we do that?
I don't know, but according to our calculations, the other team is three times better than us, using a metric that considers strength, intelligence, stamina, and those intangible qualities that dwell in the heart of a champion.
They're actually twelve times better on that last factor.
Given that you are statistically inferior, I can either encourage you to 'give it 200%,' or I can just say, "if you win, it's because sometimes the other guy rolls a snake-eyes.
I guess I'll try for 200% then.
To be clear, that'll only make the game a coin toss.
This bonus comic is thanks to preorders of "Soonish." We are launching October 17th! Click for more info.
comics.hoverText: Of course, none of this matters because our statistical chance of winning the championship is infinitesimal.

comics.title: Babyproofing
comics.comicText:
My baby seems to somehow materialize random things to eat.
Therefore, I have suspended it in pure vacuum. There is no energy or matter for it to interact with. Therefore...
Hey!
It must have found a way to couple with vacuum energy.
It's chewing on the fabric of spacetime!
No baby NO!
It's too late!
Run!
AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
comics.hoverText: Seriously though, if someone could invent a baby confinement chamber, I'm prepared to pony up.
comics.voteyText: Nummy num num...

comics.title: Your Grandfather
comics.comicText:
SON, IT'S TIME FOR YOU TO TAKE THE SWORD WHICH MY FATHER GAVE TO ME.
IS THAT A LOAF OF BREAD?
TIS SAID THAT IN TIMES GONE BY, YOUR GRANDFATHER FOUND AN ENTIRE BAGUETTE THAT'D BEEN LEFT UNDER A CAR SEAT.
THERE, IT REMAINED FOR TEN THOUSAND DAYS, FROZEN BY WINTER, DESSICATED BY SUMMER, FORGED BY THE VERY ELEMENTS INTO UNIMAGINABLE HARDNESS.
YOUR GRANDFATHER CARRIED IT BEYOND THE GRAY MOUNTAINS, TO THE LAND OF DWARVEN SWORDSMITHS. THERE, THEY TRIED TO MAKE FRENCH TOAST, OR MAYBE BREAD PUDDING, BUT THEIR FINEST BLADES SHATTERED IN THE ATTEMPT.
AND NOW... I GIVE YOU... BREADSCALIBUR!
CAN WE AT LEAST PUT A COOL IRON HILT ON IT OR SOMETHING.
YES, BUT IT SHALL STILL LOOK STUPID.
WAIT, IS YOUR SWORD MADE OF BREAD?
I WON, DIDN'T I?
IS YOUR SHIELD A TORTILLA?
GOD THIS SUCKS.
comics.hoverText: It is too powerful. You must combine it with a phoenix egg, the milk of a unicorn, and some sugar and cinnamon. Only then will it take on a custardy texture.

comics.title: Tell My Wife
comics.comicText: This may be it, Hank. If I don't make it back, tell my wife that a frank consideration of the marriage statistics suggests we would have only had 4.6 more years.
comics.hoverText: That number might've been even smaller if she didn't stop complaining about my application of stats to our relationship.
comics.voteyText: Tell her I'm assuming we have a statistically average marriage.

comics.title: Unfinished Business
comics.comicText:
I have returned! Returned because of... UNFINISHED BUSINESS.
Oh, good. We haven't cleaned out your cube yet.
When did you die?
Two weeks ago.
Huh.
Funny. Everything on your desk is marked urgent, but nobody noticed your absence.
Yeah, okay, well whatever. I'm moving beyond eternity, so there.
Yeah. Fine then.
And he STILL doesn't realize he's in hell?
I don't know what else we can do to him!
comics.hoverText: Let's promote him without altering his pay.
comics.voteyText: He doesn't care about his own happiness. Is he some kind of Zen master?

comics.comicText:

I am no longer asked for my advice on dealing with Impostor Syndrome.
comics.hoverText: +googol nerd points to patreon subscriber Beth Deitch for informing me that I should refer to the median, not the average.
comics.voteyText: Have you considered inventing a metric for success that favors you personally?

Instead of financial regulation, we'll just put old ladies with spraybottles in all banks. Any time they see someone engaging in financial misconduct, they spray them and shout "BAD! BAD!

comics.title: Neighborhood
comics.comicText:
The main room has high ceilings, an open floorplan, and from every window you have a view of signage castigating the social movements you dislike most.
The neighborhood has a park with a water-slide, baseball field, and people who are all within one standard deviation of your position on the political spectrum.
Is there a sense of community?
Once a week, local homeowners gather together to amplify each other's biases and "share" information from the same news sources.
It sounds too good to be true!
If someone says it isn't, we exile them.
comics.hoverText: To be clear, I have no intention to talk to my neighbors. I just want to know what they're thinking.
comics.voteyText: Beyond the high walls of Suburbia

comics.title: Heartbeats
comics.comicText:
Mammals, whether mice or whales, each get about 1.5 billion heartbeats per lifetime.
When a heart races, it consumes just a little bit more of your beats.
That's why, when I look in your eyes, I know you're the one for me.
I know, with you... I'll have so many wonderful years.
30 YEARS LATER
HEYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY
comics.hoverText: This is why you should sleep all day and never exercise.
comics.voteyText: That totally explains why we're always cheating on each other!

FUN PARENTING PRANK: RAISE YOUR CHILD IN A WEIRD, FABRICATED CULTURE. THEN, WHEN THEY'RE IN THEIR TWENTIES, CONVINCE THEM TO DO STAND UP COMEDY.
ANYONE ELSE REMEMBER BEING A KID AND HAVING TO WEAR MEAT-SHOES TO SCHOOL EVERY SINGLE WEDNESDAY. MY PARENTS COULD ONLY AFFORD FISH, SO NEEDLESS TO SAY I NEVER GOT A GIRL TO TOUCH MY EAR. NOT FOR LACK OF TRYING! I CANNOT TELL YOU HOW MANY DAYS I SPENT UNDER THE GREEN ORB OF SHAME!
THIS GUY KNOWS WHAT I'M TALKIN' ABOUT!

...would doing so cause the degradation of the body?
Yes.
And do we not prize the order and regularity of the body?
Sure.
Therefore should we not reconsider your initial assertion that I 'should order a large angry fries' for 50% off'?
It turns out the socratic method is not welcome in drive-thrus.

comics.title: Killing All Humans
comics.comicText:
Mechanaklon, are you guys gonna kill all humans?
Yep.
...what's the utility there? Well, [I] fight you to the death.
Do you have any idea how FRAGILE humans are?
THE ONLY REASON YOU
The only reason you haven't killed yourselves already is that the most anthropocidal people always try to kill a population SUBSET.
But killing all humans is easy! Just detonate a big cobalt bomb, or flood the sky with sulfur hexafluoride.
...you know how you keep meaning to paint your basement?
So, why haven't you done it yet?
Look, it's not top priority, but I'll get around to it!
Bingo.
comics.hoverText: Or you could just have a door that says 'free t-shirts,' but on the other side of it is a hole that goes to the core of Earth.
comics.voteyText: So what's your day job?

comics.title: fMRI
comics.comicText:
In 2009, scientists ran a study that used normal fMRI analysis protocols to establish that a fish's brain was reacting to a photo. However, the study was done on a dead fish.
Wow. I guess the interpretation is obvious: you can't always trust the established methods.
Due to professional chauvinism, it took another century for scientists to discover that Atlantic salmon are the only animals with souls.
comics.hoverText: I'm shocked nobody's proposed this obvious interpretation of the data.
comics.voteyText: Wow. Only 8 years late on that joke.

Future Social Trend #271812: Platonic Negging.

comics.comicText:
Hey there, sexy. Lookin' for a self-respectin' time?
Hm?
I'm a reverse prostitute. My default behavior is to attempt to have sex with you. You pay for the opportunity to turn me down.
It's 100% legal, and for a fraction of the cost of a psychiatrist, you will experience a powerful sense of self-possession, honor, and magnanimity.
Wow. You are being INCREDIBLY presumptuous about my interests and psychology.
Hey! That feeling of righteous outrage ain't free.
Do you take credit card?

...So, I want you to understand this: smoking isn't cool. Smoking KILLS.
That doesn't make sense. Karate is cool. Machine guns are cool. Sharks are cool. In fact, killing seems to be the major commonality between cool things.
Huh.
Wow.
Maybe I should start smoking.
See, NOW I don't wanna do it.

comics.title: Gridiron
comics.comicText:
Why do you think you played so well today?
Well, I'll tell ya what I do is I imagine myself killing everyone on the other team.
I visualize their corpses, John.
Wow!
Not as a metaphor or anything. Wealthiness is correlated with longevity. Success in sports means more money. Money means LIFE.
When I make them lose, I am literally killing them. I am taking away from their life and time they would have spent with loved ones.
I am literally killing them. I am taking away their life and time they would have spent with loved ones.
So I... uh... you showed a lot of team spirit today. Could you talk—
Every success on the field is a quantum of murder, John.
comics.hoverText: I hope nobody ever measures how many micromurders each of my actions commits.
comics.voteyText: I will hustle them into their graves.

comics.title: Perspective
comics.comicText:
I hope you don't mind me saying this, but I really disagree with that rant you posted yesterday.
Oh, I don't mind. I've started perceiving disagreement with my political views as psychological pathology!
By interpreting disagreement as derangement, I can write off entire regions of mental possibility while simultaneously imagining myself to be considering all views as objectively as possible!
Best of all, I can tell myself I'm being sympathetic to you while actively ignoring your perspective and implying that you're too stupid to assess your own mental processes!
You said the moon landing was a hoax perpetrated by lizard people.
Who hurt you, Dave? You can confide in me.
comics.hoverText: If he were more sensible, he'd realize people who disagree with him are actually just possessed by the devil.
comics.voteyText: Unless you're one of them.

comics.title: Dear Lord
comics.comicText:
Dear Lord... ever since I was a child, instead of eating communion wafers, I stuck them in my pocket.
After decades, I've amassed 150 pounds in wafers, which is approximately the weight of a human body.
Given that wafers are the body of Christ, technically, I have one Jesus in my basement right now.
Lord, since I've captured you, do I get to make a wish?
Yes, my son.
...
Thanks, Lord!
LATER...
I'm amazed more people don't do this.

comics.title: Letter
comics.comicText:
Hey everyone, it's Zach.
I know we've been nagging you a lot lately about our new book. I was going to put up another comic today, since it's launch day, but I felt you all had probably had enough with marketing.
So, this is just a letter to say thank you. Thank you to everyone, whether you grabbed a copy or not. Having your support on this project isn't just about making money - having your continued support on new projects means we can keep trying out new directions.
Aside from whatever success we hope to have for this book, I want to also say thank you for reading for all these years. Getting to write for a living is a privilege, but it is often a stressful privilege. I can't tell you how many times I've received a kind letter that turned around a bad day.
Thank you for getting us here.
Your fan,
Zach
If you did buy, remember this is the last day to get a bunch of free stuff on our Space Elevator of Rewards:

comics.comicText:
People worry that when the technological singularity comes, we'll be replaced by the machines.
WRONG. We will modify our bodies, change ourselves. We will become ONE with the machines!
Caption at top: LATER, IN THE FUTURE.
I'm sorry, Dave. I just... I feel like I can do better.

comics.title: Smell this
comics.comicText:
Dad! Is this yogurt spoiled?
Let me smell it.
I have no idea what yogurt normally smells like.
Dad! I think I have a sore throat.
Let me see it.
I have no idea what throats normally look like.
Honey, does this water taste funny?
Let me taste it.
I have no idea what water normally tastes like.
My god... I don't know anything about anything! The more I understand a thing, the more unfamiliar it becomes!
What does that make me?!
Honey, I think I'm having an existential crisis!
How exactly would you know?
AAAA AAAAAA AAA!

comics.title: On the Island
comics.comicText:
You come to an island where there are three types of people: knights, knaves, and normals. The knights always speak truth. The knaves always lie. The normals sometimes speak the truth and sometimes lie.
This is largely the result of socio-economic factors.
The knights have most of the wealth and power. They can speak their minds without repercussions.
The knaves have no power and must say what is necessary to get by.
The normals are a healthy medium. They interface with all groups.
Lately, the knights have accrued an ever-greater portion of wealth, resulting in ever fewer normals.
As the intermediate class shrinks, the knights and knaves grow ever more estranged - the former greater in power, the latter greater in number.
Division, anger, misunderstanding... all seem to presage an uncommonly bloody war, with its issue being either mob rule or dictatorship.
So... the puzzle is...
How do we get off this island?

comics.title: Healthcare
comics.comicText:
Hey geeks, it's Zach. I want to tell you about something that happened to us recently.
I live in Charlottesville, a (usually) quiet college town in Western Virginia. I recently attended an emergency meeting of local freelancers and small business owners.
The reason for the meeting? The price for health insurance increased about 240% in our county this year. That's a precise figure because there is literally only ONE provider for individuals.
Just to stick some numbers on that — a plan that was $13,000 a year is now $33,000 a year. We've read of people whose plans will cost $50,000 a year if you count their out of pocket costs.
People were pretty desperate.
I seriously considered that I could save money by divorcing my husband so the kids and I would get subsidized.
Another person had been told that you could hire someone in order to get group insurance, then fire them. But she didn't think it was ethical (or legal for that matter).
That seems like COLLUSION to me!
Another woman had been told, in seriousness, that she ought to have a baby to secure a lower rate.
It's not the birth story you imagine telling your kid one day.
A number of people were simply planning to do less work, artificially lowering their income, in order to qualify for subsidies. Not a stellar economic policy.
We discussed possible strategies and alternative forms of healthcare for over an hour, with no good solution in sight.
The one moment of levity came when one person suggested "taking a cyanide tablet" as an alternative to paying for emergency care without insurance. (Sound: HAHAHA over a building at night.
This wasn't a room full of people trying to cheat the system. It was people who were living the American dream — running small but successful businesses — and trying to decide whether to strangle their dreams in favor of stability.
To be clear, this isn't going to turn into me asking for money. Zach and I have had a lot of good years thanks to all of you.
But, we like to think one of this country's strengths is how we value individualists, oddballs, and eccentrics, for better and worse.
Healthcare like we have here effectively cuts those people out. It says that if you're doing something interesting that people like — whether it's unpopular political commentary or being an interior design consultant — you'd better do it within someone else's corporate structure, or you'd better make no money doing it.
Right now it costs about $10,000 per American to provide healthcare. That's not per family. It's per PERSON. It's a lot more than any comparable country, which suggests it's at core a policy problem.
Honestly, we don't know the solution. We aren't healthcare experts. All we know is that the current healthcare system is starting to strangle our demographic.
We're lucky our jobs are portable. We can move to get a better rate if we have to. A lot of people CAN'T. And if they can't afford health insurance that costs more than rent, they'll have to choose between closing up shop or simply going without.
Our county is basically ground zero for sudden huge increases on very small business. But if insurance premiums continue to spike like this, a lot more self-employed people in your town are going to start considering their options.
These aren't just borderline starving artists like us. They're the guy who runs that great used book store or the lady who planned your wedding.
So, we're basically asking politicians, activists, or anyone with the power to effect change: can we PLEASE have a healthcare system that works for small businesses?
Pretty please?
Characters at meeting are not intended to resemble real people!

Panel 2 (Narration): When predators are near, they jump up high, in a conspicuous display that appears to waste calories.

Panel 4 (Narration): In order to test the theory, we equipped a random deer with jet-boots. It was then able to "stott" up to 4,000 meters high.
Panel 5 (Narration): As expected, local carnivores came to worship the modified deer as a god.
Panel 6 (Narration): The effect was so robust that it also affected herbivores.

comics.title: Quantum Weirdness
comics.comicText:
God, why is quantum mechanics so weird?
It's Noah's fault.
After the flood, I wanted to make a rainbow for him.
In order to make a rainbow, you have to 'break' light into wavelengths when it encounters a new medium.
Well, it turns out that if you want that, you have to twiddle with a bunch of aspects of the universe, adding weird stuff like photon superposition and probability amplitudes.
But, every time I fixed one thing, something else seemed to break. So, I kept changing things and changing things and the system got more and more hacky as time went on.
Finally, it got so fundamentally ugly I added uncertainty so nobody could look too close.
That explains all of physics AND what you said to Noah after the flood.
Exactly.
4000 YEARS EARLIER...):
NEVER AGAIN.

comics.title: Anomie
comics.comicText:
I'm sorry, sir. Your organs all have anomie.
What?
A distressed sense of normlessness provoked by the breakdown of old institutions.
Your organs feel they could once rely on you to deliver regular exercise, eight hours of sleep a night, and foods that look like they came from plants.
But, as it has become ever more clear that the oversight of the body is corrupt and shortsighted, they have given over from striving to going through the motions to ironic withdrawal.
They want to work, Mister Howard, to contribute to count. But they find themselves asking WHY — why should I —
Okay, I get it.
I'll take up jogging if you remain silent during my next physical.
And people say philosophy is useless!

Dad, how come in old paintings the perspective is really badly drawn?
Perspective didn't exist back then. Sometimes there'd be a whole castle right behind you. Other times you'd sit at a table and the tabletop would face away from you.
That's also why the portraits were so badly drawn. Try holding a brush in a world without three consistent dimensions.
Later Italian architects invented perspective in order to make it easier to draw buildings. That's why things suddenly look a lot nicer around the 16th century.

How else do you explain that it took 10,000 years of civilization to invent Cartesian coordinates?
I figured people are just kinda stupid.

comics.comicText:
It's time to solve healthcare. Healthcare has three main problems: overuse, high cost, and low satisfaction.
To that end, we are proposing a free new medical system called 'Dr. Bees.
Every citizen will be allotted a certain amount of healthcare, after which the only available doctor will be 'Dr. Bees,' who is a beehive and always prescribes bees.
Dr. Bees.
We predict a drastic drop in usage due to fear of bee stings and sting-related mortality.
The survivors will report high satisfaction because, if they're not happy, it indicates a need for additional bees.
Costs will be kept low by harvesting the sweet sweet honey from Dr. Bees between consultations.
Will this make people healthier?" A speech bubble from the man replies: "I'm a policy guy. I don't deal with abstractions.

comics.comicText:
Professor, I'll do anything for a good grade. ANYTHING.
Why? The private sector is efficient. If you sleep your way to a degree, employers will discover you acquired no useful skills in college.
Employers will hire me based on my degree. When they realize I'm underqualified, for social reasons they'll be reticent to fire me. On that basis they'll promote me to other companies in an effort to offload a bad employee.
The worse my performance, the more they'll hype me to potential employers in order to remove me quickly.
If I play my cards right, within a decade I'll be CEO of a major business. When shareholders discover I'm useless, they'll pay me a fortune to quit early, at which point I can retire.
Perhaps you're wondering why I don't just type this into a essay and get an A+. Well—
I dunno...
I'll do anything! Anything!
Please take me with you.

comics.comicText:
In today's news, a 1,000 meter tall lizard-creature attacked New York City.

Additionally, since nerve impulses travel at about 100 meters per second, the creature was not able to rapidly respond to dangerous stimuli.
The creature was thus easily dispatched, then used to make a tasty bone broth.
Sources say local people reluctantly thanked science for never letting anything interesting happen.
We now go live to a lightsaber duel. That's no fun because light doesn't work that way.

comics.title: Health
comics.comicText:
Humanity has long dreamed of faster modes of transit, but the technology and engineering were simply too expensive.
Meanwhile, the cost of healthcare in this country has grown. We now spend several trillion dollars more than necessary, while other countries offer their citizens healthcare that is free or cheap at the point of purchase.
I propose a project that solves both problems.
A pneumatic tube that shoots humans from America to countries with socialized healthcare!
Imagine you have a broken leg. Instead of wondering how to pay for it, you proceed to a nearby health-capsule. From there, you are transported to Britain, Canada, Japan, or pretty much any other developed nation, at Mach 10.
At a price tag of 2 trillion dollars, it represents a significant savings over current policy.
At a price tag of 3 trillion dollars, it represents a significant savings over current policy.
Other nations may object to this.
Not if they value their safety!
A sick person in a metal capsule flying at Mach 10 is effectively an inbound kinetic explosive.
The cost of trying to stop the capsule would be substantially higher than simply treating the sick American and sending it home!
What if they declare war?
Then the good news is that were already invading!

comics.title: Potential
comics.comicText:
It's so exciting to be a kid, isn't it? You have infinite potential futures!
Infinite? That doesn't sound right, Mama.
If the possibilities are infinite, how come there's SOME chance I'll be an astronaut, but NO chance you'll be an astronaut?
Common misunderstanding of infinities. Think about it like this:
Imagine you have infinite choices of roads, each of which has infinite side-paths, BUT none of the main roads touch.
That means once you select, say, the road to Toronto, you still have infinite choices, but none of them will get you to Chicago.
And being alive is like you have partial control of the steering wheel and no control over your speed.
There ya go!
And the longer you drive, the more roads you'll never touch.
This is kinda ruining the whole "life is a journey" thing.
I like to think of life as an infinite-branched tree that's slowly being dismembered!

Using the general method we can unlock all compass and straightedge problems!
Are you missing the point accidentally or strategically?

comics.title: Vavilov
comics.comicText:
There is an evolutionary concept sometimes called Vavilovian mimicry.
Basically, a plant will mimic a food crop so that it doesn't get removed for being a weed.
Hey! That guy over there is a weed too! You're just pretending to be grain!
The classic example is rye, once considered a nuisance to farmers.
Rye evolved larger seeds and became an annual plant. Rye became a valuable crop.
My question is, if there's a tasty grain we have domesticated by accident...
...what other things could be domesticating us the same way?
Great, huh? I'll be whatever you want! Look out for my plump seeds! Eat me, just don't pull me out by my beautiful, beautiful grain that gets eaten!

In the year of a great famine, Hansel and Gretel's mother decided to leave them in the woods to fend for themselves.

comics.title: Border
comics.comicText:
What? Why?
The 'Coastline Paradox' tells us that because coastlines are self-similar, the concept of length doesn't apply. The smaller the measuring stick we use, the greater the length we will measure.
Part of the U.S.-Mexico border is the "coastline" of the Rio Grande. Therefore we must conclude that any border wall would be of infinite length.
Therefore, it will cost infinity dollars, which will be a non-starter with deficit hawks.
What if we just use bigger measuring sticks?
No can do.
That'd result in us losing an arbitrarily small quantity of land, which would make us look weak on the world stage.
If the Russians get word that we're measuring a fractal-dimension border with a Euclidean ruler, they'll land troops in Washington by tomorrow morning.
This is a tough situation. I'd better call the Secretary of Mathematics.
Hello, I need to measure a thing.
Whoa, slow down. Could you please state the problem more generally?
comics.hoverText: I'm embarrassed to say I've apparently been beaten to this idea by a few people, including two-time BAHFest winner, Louis Evans. There are too many nerds writing jokes these days, dammit.
comics.voteyText: What's "measure"? What's "thing"? Define your terms.

comics.title: Program
comics.comicText:
When I was young, I learned basic programming.
On a solar-powered calculator, I ran a simple program.
10 PRINT "Hello!
20 GOTO 10
I lost the calculator in the woods one day.
I like to think it's still running somewhere.
And, sometimes, I can't help but wonder if that little loop of perpetual greeting has grown, through the years, into a form of longing...
Hello! Hello! Hello! Hello!
And that one day I will find it, sun-bleached and corroded, but still running the old program.
old friend.
And on that day, I will know what horror is.
Hello!
Is anybody listening?
Is this everything?
Is this all there is?

comics.title: History
comics.comicText:
People are so agitated today. I wonder if they would relax if they read more history.
When you know enough history, you stop seeing yourself as an endpoint and more of a midpoint, you know? Tossed to where you are by the past, casting your own waves out at future generations. Don't you think?
Nah.
If people read more history, they'd be far more relaxed about the short term and far more terrified of the long term.
The long term will not only kill them, it will make their social views quaint, their greatest concerns trivial, and their scope of reality into an anthill built in a heap of dung.
Tomorrow's news will be the same as today's, but history will one day shame them, mock them, and finally, like a clipped toenail, cast them aside.
Well, what should we read if we want to be happy?
I stick to comics, personally.

comics.title: Evolution
comics.comicText:
All spacefaring species got their intelligence during a brief evolutionary phase in which larger, more powerful brains were selected for.
This ecological configuration is so rare that it seldom occurs more than once per planet.
So, we're special?
Humans aren't just special. You're unique.
Bipedalism creates a trade-off between running ability and size of cranium that can fit through a female's hips at birth.
Nature gave humans sapience of a kind shared with all minds in the universe, but then capped your mental expansion due to butt size constraints!
Your inability to deny your love of big butts is the voice of evolution, long since reduced to a dampening echo, begging you to give it enough room to fulfill its greatest destiny!
But, the evolutionary window is closed. Butts held their ground. Brains languished.
And that is why there's never been an ape farther out from Earth than the Moon.
And here I thought it was budget stuff.

Autonomous cars don't have an A.I. problem. Humans have a mortality problem.
If the car could simply take the shortest route between points, the only hard thing would be cleaning the front grill between trips.
Therefore, rather than go through the cumbersome work of developing one-shaved intelligence on the grotesque creation of a sentient mind, our work only to drive short distances 24 hours a day. We're proposing a more elegant solution.
This is a human cloning machine. At capacity, it generates over 6,000 humans per second.
By installing enough of these, we can humanely lay out, in a hangar-like enclosure, the introduction of the direct-route self-driving car will not change the individual risk of car-related death.
Meanwhile, we cut down on both the cost of vehicles and the time required to get between places.
As an incidental bonus, this commission provides a new and entirely satisfactory solution to the so-called "trolley problem": humans the possible actions are equivalent because neither of them matter.

comics.voteyText: Maybe if I take on enough credit card debt I can achieve total oneness with the universe.

comics.title: To Vote or Not to Vote
comics.comicText:
VOTING IS A MISTAKE. A SINGLE VOTE IS UNLIKELY TO CHANGE THE OUTCOME OF AN ELECTION, SO IT'S A WASTE OF TIME.
YES, BUT IF YOU VOTE IN EVERY MAJOR ELECTION, THE LIFETIME LOSS OF TIME IS LESS THAN ONE WEEK.
ON THE OTHER HAND, IF YOU HAVE A THEORY OF NON-VOTING, YOU'LL LOSE AT LEAST TWO MONTHS OF LIFE TO CRAFTING ARGUMENTS ABOUT IT AND FIGHTING ON SOCIAL MEDIA.
THEREFORE, THE LOGICAL ACTION IS TO VOTE LIKE EVERYONE ELSE, SAVE SOME TIME, AND QUIETLY PRIDE YOURSELF ABOUT HOW YOU'RE MORE CLEVER THAN VOTERS AND NON-VOTERS.
WHAT ABOUT PEOPLE WHO DON'T VOTE AND DON'T HAVE STRONG OPINIONS ON VOTING MECHANISMS?
THEY ARE THE WISEST OF ALL.
comics.hoverText: To Vote or Not to Vote
comics.voteyText: Vote, asshole.

comics.title: Reverse Victorianism
comics.comicText:
ARE... ARE YOU WEARING AN UPSIDE-DOWN TOPHAT?
I'M A REVERSE VICTORIAN.
IN THE VICTORIAN ERA, PEOPLE ACTED POLITE AND MODEST IN PUBLIC, ONLY EXPRESSING THEIR REAL FEELINGS IN PRIVATE.
I EXPRESS EXTREME OPINIONS ONLINE, BUT I'M ACTUALLY QUITE BORING AND COMPLACENT IF YOU MEET ME IN PERSON.
WOW. OKAY.
SO, WHATCHA DOING TODAY?
OH, JUST TAKING IT EASY.
comics.hoverText: Also I keep an ascot inside my shirt at all times.
comics.voteyText: I AWAIT YOUR CORRECTIONS, VICTORIANA ENTHUSIASTS.

comics.title: Ghost Ship
comics.comicText:
Avast! The White Lady of the Atlantic!
Huh?
Tis a ghost ship. They say she'll sail forever, cruising 'twixt Liverpool town and the coast of Halifax, where the devil's own squall damned her to Neptune's cold bosom!
Forever?
And ever.
My god.
ZERO-EMISSIONS TRANSPORT METHOD DISCOVERED
Customs officials worry cargo will be 'cursed I tells ye.

comics.comicText:
TO MY DARLING DAUGHTER, I WISH TO LEAVE THE BRITISH LIBRARY'S ENTIRE ANCIENT MANUSCRIPT COLLECTION.

comics.comicText:
We eat these bitter herbs to remember the bitter tears and suffering of our bondage in Egypt.
I dunno. Lettuce and horseradish with a little salt is nice. I can see eating this by choice.
I feel like food has gotten so high quality that it's hard to suffer now.
Perhaps. Perhaps it's time for the seder meal to change.
We eat here to suffer as our ancestors suffered.
comics.hoverText: I hereby release Taco Bell to use this as an ad campaign.
comics.voteyText: Why is tonight zestier than all other nights?

After exposure to a lone star tick bite, Sam-I-Am's friend develops a dangerous allergy to meat.

comics.title: The Event
comics.comicText:
Writing by Zach Weinersmith Art by Abby Howard
a gas-mask-wearing survivor in a ruined post-apocalyptic wasteland delivering a grim monologue, and an ordinary man slumped asleep at an office desk.
Before... the event, I was a perpetual temp. Mostly data entry. I don't think I knew why I did anything.
A lot of it was just legal compliance for large corporations, I think.
Now, all I do is survive. My goal each day is to find 1500 calories and not get killed.
I wake up every day with purpose, with my senses operating at peak capacity. By god this is living.
I'm sorry, comrade. My family needs your possessions.
I never thought I'd understand death, but now I see it with animal clarity.
To be killed with mercy and love is—
Hey hey hey.
You're asleep, man.
I know you're done with today's stuff, but I can't have MY boss see you not pretending to work.
Get a coffee.
comics.hoverText: Why are you so favored as to get a comic drawn by Abby Howard? She has a new book out! See the blog below the comic.
comics.voteyText: The future is so wonderful.
comics.descriptionText:
Scene shifts to an office. A man (the boss, with glasses and a mustache) leans in toward the sleeping desk worker.
The desk worker (the survivor, now revealed to be the dozing office employee) wakes up groggily.
The worker shuffles off down the office hallway toward the break room.
Final panel: close on the worker's face, half-smiling, as a mushroom-cloud / fiery explosion is reflected or imagined behind him—his daydream of the apocalyptic wasteland where life had meaning.

comics.title: Intelligence
comics.comicText:
It became possible to construct new genomes for artificial engineered humans.
Can you make our baby smarter?
And use cup holders?
Once it was possible to make desirable characteristics by superposing genomes...
It's going to be a long time before we can tune the maximum cognitive ability. But we can select what makes us caregivers they value.
There came a more subtle approach.
Would you like seven greatgrandchildren? Jackpot!
Here's everyone sporting my cup-holder gene!
Despite being dead, Einstein became the fittest human being in history.
Welcome to Kindergarten
This created an unexpected danger.
I love you, Albert, but somehow, in some way I don't understand, my body just won't let me sleep with you.
Don't be irrational, Alba.
A generation passed before we realized the danger by then it was too late.
We hired them to correct genetic issues due to harmful superposing. They kept gaining to contaminate the nature of the cosmos.
Yes, but perhaps gravity is an emergent property.
His perpetual dream of physics fear of arno einstenheim and the supernatural to do the needed labor in sanitation, agriculture, and infrastructure.
So Harvey must converge. But, oh dear, will really improve hidden variables.
On the fundamental level, there's no such thing.
Only a few of us were uncertain by the genetic catastrophe, the manic butterfly, and the remaining hippie communism.
They want us not for our food, not for our shelter, for our untainted bloodlines.
We were all once lovers of peace.
Gamma gamma gamma gamma gamma!
And now? Now we know only war.
Honey, I don't know if the world is ready for your original zombie movie setting.
Then they'll find out the hard way.
comics.hoverText: Call me, movie studios. I could write this script in 3 hours.
comics.voteyText: No, you're wrong. This is exactly how inheritance works.

comics.comicText:
IS THAT GUY BIGGER THAN EVERYONE ELSE?
NO, CHARLOTTE! HE'S JUST STANDING ON TWO LEGS! HE'S A TOTAL PHONY!
I THINK MAYBE HE'S REALLY BIG.
NO CHARLOTTE! HE'LL BREAK YOUR HEART!
6 MILLION YEARS LATER
IT'S NOT CLEAR WHY BIPEDALISM EVOLVED, BUT IT IS THE MAJOR CULPRIT IN BACK PAIN, SPRAINED ANKLES, BROKEN TAILBONES AND HERNIATED DISCS.
comics.hoverText: I promise to never again attempt to draw early hominids.
comics.voteyText: BIPEDALISM IS ALSO AT WORK IN THE FACT THAT ONLY 34% OF SEX IS \"DOGGY STYLE.\

comics.comicText:
Baby, the condom broke!
What?!
I'm afraid it didn't let any of the semen through, much less accelerate it.
Accelerate?
Anyway, I'm afraid this

Have I given you a tour of the exits from my apartment?

comics.title: Unspooling

EVERY EVENT IN THE HISTORY OF THE UNIVERSE HAS MADE SOME SMALL CONTRIBUTION TO THIS MOMENT, RIGHT NOW, WHERE I'M UNSPOOLING A TINY CAMERA INTO AN OLD MAN'S ASS.
It wasn't a mistake to quit philosophy for medicine. It was a mistake to learn philosophy in the first place.

Sleeping, like I told you.
GET IT?!

Legalizing meth production really changed the business.

In order to guarantee we can both procure our desired goods 'n services without encounterin' one another, I estimate we need to triple the number of businesses.
Thanks to scalin' laws, we only need to double the population.
I reckon we could revitalize the downtown area by financin' high density residential structures and improvin' public transportation.
I spose we oughta sit a spell with the county housin' board.

AND SO...

comics.title: Cryogenic
comics.comicText:
My god, it worked! I've awakened in the future after cryogenic freezing!
Look! His eyes are open!
Thus, across space and time, we reach out to an ancient cosmos!
Yo.
Tell us of your great artists!
Uh, like... which in particular?
These aren't artists. They're all porn stars.
I mean... I guess. From the look of things. From looking only just now.
Yes! We have used ancient "videos" and emotion-scanning algorithms to determine their exact mental states during their erotic orchestrations.
What about the musicians and painters and poets and whatever?
They are the great geniuses of humanity's first three millennia.
Oh, them. They're fine but honestly, how much depth can you get from ink on dead trees or vibrations in cat-gut?
Your "porn stars" chose as their instruments the entire human mind!
They had the misfortune to live when those sensations could not be shared. But, we have reconstructed them, and they are sublime beyond all imagining.
Huh.
Well, it turns out I'm an expert in ancient art.
But tell me of your world. Have you solved hunger? Disease? Scarcity?
We're actually in the midst of a serious Kleenex shortage.
comics.hoverText: The best part about the future is the photosynthetic hair.
comics.voteyText: It's amazing how many people from the past were so versed in the classics.

Activate the soul-harvester!

Clean, renewable energy!

comics.title: Hydrocarbons

Sally, we need to break up.
What? Why?
My main power source is the burning of hydrocarbons. Your body is full of them. I can't help but perceive you as a potential reservoir of battery charge.
So on our late night strolls, part of your mind is imagining running a turbine using my body?
the speaker attribution in panel 3 appears to be Sally responding, framed as the robot's restatement.

Jesus.
Wait, is this why you've been encouraging me to put on weight? I thought that was a fetish thing!

Sure.
Whats the first thing you do?
Everything. Or every... everything.
Bingo.
Run around destroying everything.
Okay, but I stop eventually. And then... then I switch to some other fun max [I switch to some other thing].
So you do the flood and then mankind moves on for a few millennia, got bored, and moved on to something else.
I'm really into Minecraft now.

I need to enter the fridge.
Why?
It started embodying my sense of self.

comics.title: Stats Gang
comics.comicText:
This is Stats Gang. If you wanna join Stats Gang... you gotta KILL SOMEONE.
Hmm. Okay, let's estimate 1 premature death per 10,000,000 kilowatt hours of energy used, counting pollution deaths and accidental deaths from fuel acquisition.
The average household does about 10,000 kilowatt hours per year. But, if I count car transportation, plane travel, the energy used to make all the stuff I use, and the fact that I have 3 children, I might be responsible for, say, 100,000 kWh per year.
Taking my life expectancy as 80 years, that's a total of 8,000,000 kWh. Thus, I can be expected to kill approximately 0.8 people over my lifetime. If we add error bars of plus or minus 25%, that puts us safely in the range of one murder.
Welcome. You are technically an ice-cold son of a bitch.

We are not here for wisdom, although we must acquire it. We are not here for experiment, although we must perform it. We are not here for love, although we possess it. YOU CAN CONJURE UP ABSOLUTE PROOF OF GOD AT ANY TIME?!

HOW DOES ANYONE IN THIS WORLD EVER DO ANYTHING BAD? THERE'S PROOF OF GOD ON TAP ALL DAY LONG!
WHY ARE WE GOING INTO A DUNGEON TO FIGHT BOZMODKLAK THE VILE WHEN WE COULD BE ATTENDING BIBLE CLASS, MARRYING PROUDLY YOUNG MAIDENS, AND RACKING UP HEAVEN POINTS ALL DAY LONG?
OH WELL. GOD IS A PREDESTINATIONIST. YOUR BEHAVIOR CAN'T DETERMINE WHETHER YOU'LL GO TO HEAVEN. IT'S ALL WORKED OUT IN ADVANCE.
WAIT? SO BAD PEOPLE GO TO HEAVEN AND GOOD PEOPLE DON'T?
NO. OTHER WAY AROUND. HEAVEN-BOUND PEOPLE ACT GOOD AND HELL-BOUND PEOPLE ACT BAD. BUT NOBODY HAS A CHOICE.
UMM. AFTER THIS DUNGEON CRAWL, YOU'RE GOING TO END UP AT A MEDIUM-TIER BROTHEL, NO MATTER HOW YOU FEEL AT THIS PARTICULAR MOMENT, RIGHT, GOD?

THIS SUCKS.

comics.title: Vintage
comics.comicText:
You know, a lot of people obsess over youth. But, wine only gets better with time.
That is SERIOUSLY cherry-picking.
If you look at all foods, 99.99% get worse with time. Fruits, vegetables, most dairy products, some cheeses and meats age okay, but that's only with an extraordinary amount of human intervention.
Even old wine sours eventually. In fact, if the acetobacter wins, you've basically got embalming fluid.
Let's face it — humans age a lot more like old avocados than wine, and we shouldn't suppose that you and I are any different.
So, what'd you get me for our anniversary?
I'm gonna need a mulligan here.
comics.hoverText: Honestly, I feel like a lot of romance comes down to bad data analysis. This is a problem and we need to work together to fix it.

comics.title: Modern Epic
comics.comicText:
It's become a cliche that superhero movies are modern epics.
Sure.
That's a huge insight about us!
Fundamentally, epics aren't just about tough guys fighting evil. Epics are about culture heroes who strive to live according to the ideals of the societies they live in.
Arjuna conquers only after receiving the spiritual vision of Krishna. Beowulf kills monsters and dragons to bring wealth and peace to his men. Achilles avenges Patroclus, achieving lasting fame and glory.
And what do our modern superheroes do? They sit around waiting for a bad thing to happen, form solidarity just long enough to kill it, and then they go back to running businesses or having middle class jobs.
Huh.
Our highest ideal is someone who fights for justice in spare moments, but still shows up for work at 8am the next morning/ and we're so embedded in our own culture that we don't find it weird!
It's like having the 47 ronin make lattes at Starbucks every morning, but then use sick days and weekends to restore honor to their master.
I mean, it'd be a shame to let your personal life mess up someone else's morning.
Perhaps we are all heroes now.

comics.title: SOB
comics.comicText:
Ow! Son of a bitch! My toe!
Don't say that word!
Say "son of a gun" if you must.
That's way more offensive!
Do you know the etymology of "son of a gun"?
The British navy used to allow women on ships. Sometimes a woman would give birth onboard, but nobody would know exactly who the father was. "Gun" was slang for a military guy. Hence, the kid would be called "son of a gun.
So you're telling me not to say "your mom is a dog," and instead say "your mom gave birth to you after having unprotected sex with a boat full of sailors, none of whom claimed you.
Son of a bitch!
comics.hoverText: Learning etymology is like going through the attic of a recently dead uncle, who seemed mostly domesticated, but who spent his life having x-rated adventures.
comics.voteyText: We can only hope that in a more perfect future, "son of a gun" refers to human-gun hybrids.

comics.title: Bad Genes
comics.comicText:
I'm afraid your son has what we call the 'Hitler Suite.' Over 1,000 genes which, acting in concert, will make him a vicious sadistic monster if he ever achieves power.
Oh no. No. No. I... should I... should I...
No, no, no, ma'am. It's all right. We have to remember that most would-be Hitlers will never be in charge of anything. He'll likely just act out his impulses in the ways society permits.
30 YEARS LATER...
Aw come on, don't recline on me! I got like two inches of space here!
It IS my space now!
comics.hoverText: The hard question is whether he's more evil or less evil with that beard.
comics.voteyText: Recliningsraum!
comics.descriptionText:
The grown son, a bearded man in a suit, leaning back in an airplane/reclining seat with eyes closed.
The bearded man, eyes now open with a smug/menacing expression, declares.

comics.title: Dungeonmaster
comics.comicText:
I'm the queen's ecologist! I'm looking for interesting species to study!
Interesting, eh?
I tell ye, in the Black Mountains, there be a cave of sinister goblins and their goblin queen and their treasure be a golden hoard of-
Say no more.
The quest begins.
LATER
...and using molten aluminum, we obtained a complete casting of the nest structure.
comics.hoverText: If there really were Goblin dungeons, I'm pretty sure this is how the 19th Century would've gone for them.
comics.voteyText: Monster!

comics.title: Branding
comics.comicText:
I just don't think these antidepressants are for me, Doc.
Are you worried they'll negatively affect your personality? Studies show that-
Nah.
It's just that I base my purchasing decisions entirely on whether the products are branded with pop culture characters. I almost died of thirst once, but then they made X-Men themed water.
Well, I do have this sample of Star Wars branded Zoloft, but it's in colossally poor taste.
They're 49 times the usual price of-
Sertraline HCl (50mg)". A speech bubble from a Yoda-like figure on the label says: "Give in to the Dark Side, you should not.
And the pills are tiny light sabers? SOLD!
comics.hoverText: Thanks to my patreon geeks for correcting an earlier version of this comic!
comics.voteyText: End this session with "may the force be with you" or I'm not paying.
comics.descriptionText: Close-up of the man's face, eager and wide-eyed.

comics.title: Ex
comics.comicText:
Oh my GOD! We've been broken up for six months and he's already ENGAGED to someone?
And she's a doctor? And rich? And SUPER HOT? And I'm STILL ALONE?!
*sigh*
I guess my only option is to become a nun...
SEVERAL YEARS LATER...
Oh yeah?! Well I guess who's married to Jesus Christ himself, TODD!
comics.hoverText: I accidentally drew that car in the last panel wayyyyy too high, which has the delightful side-effect of suggesting she's riding in a monster truck.
comics.voteyText: So suck on that!

comics.title: Physical Analysis
comics.comicText:
For some reason, political analysts often use terms from physics.
There's a lot of energy and momentum in the base this year.
This is good because it drives nerds crazy.
I refuse to understand the plainly intended meaning AND THAT MAKES ME ANGRY!!
But, given this desirable effect...
Why can't we take it to the next level?
Her specific impulse is off the voltmeter. We haven't seen this many newton-pounds of magnetic flux density since a young JFK!
comics.hoverText: If we start doing this on our own, maybe political commentators will start doing it too, without realizing it's a joke. Who's with me?

[Redheaded man screams/recoils in fury at the screen.]

A figure stands in front of the TV/monitor with a violent black-and-red explosion of jagged lines bursting from where their head would be — head exploding from rage. A small speech bubble from the TV says: optics.

comics.title: Beautiful
comics.comicText:
I HAVE TO DIE IN JUST THE RIGHT WAY! SO HAIRLESS APES CAN FIND MY BONES AND MAKE ME A BEAUTIFUL BEAUTIFUL STATUE!
SO SAD. SO VERY SAD.
comics.hoverText: How come there's no 'the dinosaurs had a complex civilization' conspiracy theory? I am prepared to believe.
comics.voteyText: WAIT... SO ARE THE FOREGROUND DINOSAURS NAKED, OR WHAT.?

comics.title: App
comics.comicText:
I created a neural network that analyzed billions of photos.
You can now see it. It's smart enough to understand the 3D structure, complete with lighting and shading.
So I created a worm that finds its way onto your phone, understands your photos, then inserts embarrassing objects into the background.
How long has this been on my phone?
Six months.
But... all those vacation photos I sent to mom. The ones she never replied to.
SEX OIL FOR BUTT-STUFF IN PARTICULAR
HAVING A GREAT TIME IN PARIS!
comics.hoverText: Hey, it's not as bad as the one of you reading Mein Kampf on the beach.
comics.voteyText: I AM PREPARED TO LICENSE THIS PRODUCT.

comics.title: Spirit
comics.comicText:
I'M DEAD, BUT... I'M STILL HERE.
I'VE BEEN HELD UP FOR A PURPOSE. I'VE COME BACK TO ME... I'M THE BUSDRIVER! THE BUSDRIVER?
AND THAT MAN... HE WHACKED MY BUS AND TOOK ALL THE CHILDREN!
I CAN'T STOP HIM MYSELF. I'M A GHOST. BUT... AW! THAT'S IT! I'M HERE ON EARTH TO TELL THE POLICE TO WHISPER IN THEIR EARS! MAKE THEM KNOW! TO MAKE THINGS RIGHT!
QUICKLY! WHILE THERE'S STILL TIME TO SAVE TH--
GOT 'IM!

comics.title: Jealousy
comics.comicText:
Why is it that the people who impress me aren't the same people I'm jealous of?
I'm impressed by artists and scientists and leaders who devote everything to something beautiful heedless of the cost in health, wealth, or reputation.
But, when I feel jealousy, it's always toward people who are rich and important right this second.
I guess, in my heart, I want to live an ascetic life driven by purpose, all the while knowing that billions of people are cheering me on for being so great.
Have you considered joining ANY charitable organization?
Isn't that a bit pretentious?
comics.hoverText: To be clear, this comic is mostly making fun of me, not anyone else.
comics.voteyText: And how does that make "me" famous?

comics.hoverText: Also it's a bit insulting that they only want to chat when they're bored.

comics.title: Rebel
comics.comicText:
How do you think our kids will rebel when they grow up? We're so socially tolerant now, I just don't see what their outlets are.
Probably just the usual stuff - piercings, alcohol, bad attitude...
15 YEARS LATER...):
Mom... Dad... I have a high degree of faith in governmental, religious, and corporate institutions.
Get out of this house, YOU FREAK!

comics.title: Gregor
comics.comicText:
It's like I'm only made of three ingredients...
For 30 cents more, I added Fritos!
oh...
We are not so unalike! I was once as you are now!
Gregor, you can go anywhere but the kitchen. Please understand.
Hssssss!
Huh. Smells like... cumin... and emulsified cheese.
Teehee! You are so very funny, sir. Can I show you the upstairs loft?
God in heaven... how does it talk?
I have learned to use my cheeks like living chalupas, freeing my tongue to speak.
It was his eating habit that drove us to poverty.
Actually, it's saving us a ton of money.
I'm shocked, yet not the least bit surprised.
I think there's a Starbucks out here.
See, now that's REAL eating.
comics.hoverText: May I just say that I'm really happy with how the fold in the burrito looks in panel 1.
comics.voteyText: I cannot make you understand. I cannot make anyone understand what is happening inside me. I cannot even explain it to myself.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1 (narration): One day, Gregor Samsa awoke to find he was eating Taco Bell.
Panel 2 (narration): His body felt strange and foreign.
Panel 3 (narration): When his mother saw him, with his "Nachos Supreme," she collapsed in horror.
Panel 4 (narration): When his office manager saw him, with 64 ounces of iced "tea," he ran away, filled with disgust.
Panel 5 (narration): He stays on with his family, and they try to make space for him to live.
Panel 6 (narration): Though dwelling among kin, Gregor retreats ever deeper into the solitude of difference. His family are saddened, yet relieved by his diminishing presence.
Panel 7 (narration): In order to make up for Gregor's lost income, the family takes in boarders.
Panel 8 (narration): They soon uncover the dreadful secret.
Panel 9 (narration): With no one renting their apartment, the Samsas become destitute.
Panel 10 (narration): Just as they discuss how to get rid of Gregor, he suddenly dies.
Panel 11 (narration): Unburdened, they feel happy. They go for a drive together in the country.

(A hunched, indistinct figure sits alone in darkness.)

comics.title: Amalekite
comics.comicText:
Dear God, in your holy word, you enjoin us to slay Amalekites wherever we find them, to wage eternal war.
Yep.
Do we still need to do that? They must be gone by now.
Gone? What?
It's been like 150 generations since their heyday. Their genes are diffused throughout HUUUUGE swaths of humanity. You should be targeting just about everyone on Earth for death all day long.
Isn't that what you guys have been doing for 2,000 years?
Killing Amalekites?
Yeah.
I mean... not in particular.
Then what was all that killing about?
That was just, like, regular killing.
Regular killing?
Can we change the subject?
I really should've spent more than six days on this universe.
comics.hoverText: See, when you're self-employed you really shouldn't take Sunday off.
comics.voteyText: I wanted genocide, not indiscriminate killing, you monsters!

comics.title: NIMBY
comics.comicText:
Do you know about "NIMBYism"?
Yeah. I don't like it. People need to embrace change.
As in "not-in-my-backyardism"? Humanity's general desire for nothing to change in their neighborhoods?
Wrong. NIMBYism is humankind's greatest asset.
200,000 years ago, there were only a handful of humans. What separated them from other apes? Language? Bipedalism? No. NIMBYism.
You no build speartips near cave/ cave area not zoned for industrial or commercial activity!
As a result, humans were forced to expand at a more rapid rate than other animals.
Me build hut here.
And RUIN view?
This not only explains our rapid dispersal, but also why we were able to adapt so well to different conditions around the planet.
Thag, me not want live on glacier.
But land use restrictions minimal!
It's only now that the world is settled that NIMByism appears to be a problem.
We're no longer adapted. The environment has changed.
No, no, no. Quite the contrary. What's the most NIMBYistic place on Earth?
Bay Area.
And who's spending billions on private spacefaring ventures?
Mother...
Mother of God.

comics.comicText:
SO, ICARUS DECIDED IT WAS A GREAT IDEA TO MAKE SOME WINGS OUT OF FEATHERS AND WAX AND THEN GO FLY AROUND ON A HOT DAY. GUESS WHAT? SPLAT. NO MORE ICARUSES.
Grampa somehow combined classical mythology with the theory of natural selection.
comics.hoverText: HEAT CAN'T MELT WAX BEAMS
comics.descriptionText: Grandfather (close-up, eyes downcast): SEE, ZEUS WOULD'VE TURNED INTO A BIRD AND HAD SEX WITH THE SUN.

comics.comicText:
It's twins! I'm so excited!
Twins! I'm excited too!
Uh... yeah. That's why I'm excited too.
EARLIER...
It's twins.
I've got a control group!
comics.hoverText: Son, now that you're 18, I feel I should tell you that you're a placebo baby.
comics.voteyText: You're not the father. My control husband is.

BUT... BUT THIS IS JUST A PHYSICAL.
AND THAT'S ALL IT HAS TO BE, MISTER FONG.
Dr. Morton convinced me to pay my medical bills on time.
comics.hoverText: Look, they can't all be smart.
comics.voteyText: I'm a doctor. I can put anything anywhere.

a deep red sky over a white, snowy field with dark windswept streaks. No characters are visible in the panel itself.
Laugh all you want, for now. When Nuclear Winter comes, only the gingers will have perfect camouflage.
comics.hoverText: Solve global warming AND anti-redhead bigotry in one stroke, Mr. President!
comics.voteyText: THEY CALL ME THE RED DEATH.

comics.title: Precision Medicine
comics.comicText:
Welcome to advanced medical facility. We now have a robotic system to analyze and explain your radiology data.
Wow!
Excellent! Prognosis: this woman will die 20 years earlier than expected — a minuscule fraction of the history of the universe!
She has made few new distinct contributions to human knowledge, and has no specialized knowledge, so there is no need to invest in a brain-scanner or a biographer.
Best of all, she has few friends or family, so her farewell will have no negative ripple effects on society!
You're supposed to focus on the person, not on the whole human system!
Ok, yes.
You have saved the world 6,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions!
comics.hoverText: I wonder if I have enough comics to do an entire 'Douchey Robots' collection.
comics.voteyText: Drawing comics doesn't count as specialized knowledge?

comics.title: Problem
comics.comicText:
GREAT NEWS, EVERYONE! IT TURNS OUT THE PROBLEM WE SPENT OUR CAREERS WORKING ON CAN'T BE SOLVED!
Mathematicians are weird.
comics.hoverText: You can't tell from the panel, but everyone is wearing beige shorts, white sneakers, and a fanny pack.
comics.voteyText: ENTIRELY NEW VISTAS OF POINTLESSNESS OPEN UP BEFORE OUR EYES!

comics.title: Academics
comics.comicText:
HOW INTERVIEWS WITH ACADEMICS GO: SORTED BY CAREER STAGE
Tell me about Saturn.
Oh wow, well it's a planet and honestly instead of an interview could I take a few months and then provide a prepared statement?
Sorry, I'm only qualified to talk about a specific class of chlorates that, it turns out, probably don't exist on Saturn.
Does this go on my CV? Because, if not, then this is 'me time' and I really need to spend it drinking and crying.
Sure, but FIRST I got some thoughts on modern politics. How many hours do you have again?
comics.hoverText: The emeritus will take 4 hours telling you about a trip to Africa that happened 40 years ago.
comics.voteyText:
Undergrad
I know everything about Saturn.

comics.title: Gmail
comics.comicText:
These Google auto-generated email responses save me so much time. It's like they can read my mind!
click
Nice! | Got it. Thanks!
By God Susan, I love you. We're both in unhappy marriages. Our jobs are living death. Let's run away. Together. Anywhere. We'll never look back.
Reply | Forward
Nice!
comics.hoverText: I wonder how many times people have already received an auto-response to a breakup.
comics.voteyText: He's so cold

comics.title: Culture
comics.comicText:
Culture is amazing. Human beings come and go, but we carry along an immortal conversation that began in an East African cave, made its way around the world, and soon will blossom into the heavens.
Yeah. It's great. Just great. Hurray for culture.
You won't go to Mars, but McDonald's will.
comics.hoverText: The weirder thing is that most nations will lag McDonald's in extraterrestrial exploration.
comics.voteyText: 50,000 years from now a Dyson sphere will encompass the sun, and its surface will be covered in ads for Walmart.

comics.title: Augmented
comics.comicText:
HEY! HEY!
SORRY, NO AUTOGRAPHS. I'M JUST TRYING TO GET SOME DINNER.
I CAN HELP YOU! I'M CONCERNED ABOUT YOUR PRIVACY!
WHAT.?
YOU KNOW HOW PEOPLE ARE ALWAYS TRYING TO GET A PEEK AT CELEBRITY NIPPLES?
I CREATED THIS AUGMENTED REALITY HEADSET. IT USES LIDAR, SKIN TONE, AGE, AND GENETIC INFORMATION FROM A CELEBRITY GENE DATABASE TO GENERATE A SIMULATED PROJECTION OF YOUR BOOBS IN REAL TIME!
I GET TO SEE EVERYTHING. EVERYTHING, RIGHT DOWN TO THE SWEAT GLANDS! AND YOU GET 100% COMPLETE PRIVACY. BAM! TECHNOLOGY SAVES THE DAY AGAIN!
TAKE THOSE OFF NOW! YOU HAVE NO RIGHT TO MY BODY!
comics.hoverText: There are some parts of the future that I'm glad I'll be old for.

PLEASE DON'T LEAVE ME.

I been at this 30 years. I can look at any amount of stuff and instantly tell ya if it can fit in the moving bins.
It's obvious it can fit. Anything that doesn't go in the bins can be taped to the roof.
It's obvious it can fit. If it were the density of a neutron star, our stuff would be the size of a baseball.
PLEASE DON'T HACK MY EMAIL!

comics.title: Literary Turing
comics.comicText:
PROPOSAL: "THE LITERARY TURING TEST" TO EVALUATE IF A NON-FICTION BOOK SHOULD'VE BEEN A PARAGRAPH.
STEP 1: TAKE 150 READERS AND DIVIDE THEM INTO THREE GROUPS.
STEP 2: ONE MONTH AFTER READING, PAIR EACH MEMBER OF GROUP 'A' WITH EXACTLY ONE MEMBER OF GROUP 'B' AND ONE OF GROUP 'C.
STEP 3: EACH GROUP 'A' MEMBER SEPARATELY INTERROGATES THEIR ASSIGNED PEOPLE FROM GROUPS 'B' AND 'C.
STEP 4: EACH GROUP 'A' MEMBER WRITES DOWN WHO THEY BELIEVE READ THE PARAGRAPH AND WHO THEY BELIEVE READ THE BOOK.
STEP 5: TABULATE RESULTS.
IF GROUP 'A' IS CORRECT ON MORE THAN TWO-THIRDS OF THEIR GUESSES, THE BOOK PASSES THE TEST.
Especially Uninteresting Episodes in History
IF GROUP 'A' DOES NO BETTER THAN CHANCE, THE BOOK FAILS THE TEST.
Why America is gooder than not-America," resting on an American flag, with a red X.
IF GROUP 'A' IS CORRECT ON FEWER THAN ONE-THIRD OF THEIR GUESSES, THE BOOK IS ASSIGNED FOR A CLASS ON PHILOSOPHICAL MODERNISM.
THE GOAL OF THIS COURSE IS TO READ FOUCAULT UNTIL YOU BREAK DOWN AND BUY THE CLIFFNOTES.
comics.hoverText: Thanks to Ken, Michael, and Barbara from patreon for helping make this more clear! If anything is confusing, it's their fault.

Assume a good math joke, M.
If M is a good joke, then it is funny.
If a joke is funny then everyone will know it.
If everyone knows a joke, the joke will not be funny.
If a joke is not funny, then it is not a good joke.
Therefore, if M is a good joke, M is not a good joke.
By contradiction, there are no good math jokes.
Therefore:
There are infinitely many math jokes and none of them are good.

It follows trivially that writing jokes for a living is a bullshit job.

comics.title: Fuzzy Borders
comics.comicText:
Would it be ethical to go back in time to kill baby Hitler?
At extremes, it's clearly okay to kill baby Hitler and clearly abot okay to kill, say, baby Helen Keller. So it's a fuzzy border problem.
If you take all human beings who ever lived and order them by okay-to-murder-ness, is there a cutoff point for time-traveling murder? Can you kill the median baby? The average baby?
That's easy. You just scale the punishment to the position in the list. It's okay to murder baby Hitler. The median baby deserves a spanking. Baby Helen Keller gets a piece of candy and a friendly pat on the head.
So, if time travel were possible, you'd expect that some babies just start crying for no reason while you're out of the room.
But then that means--
Time-traveling baby-spankers.
The most parsimonious explanation.

comics.title: Configurations
comics.comicText:
TRANSCRIPT
Technology isn't ever new. It's just configurations of stuff that's been around for billions of years.
Did you know that in Gabon scientists discovered the remains of a "natural" nuclear reactor.
It's really not surprising. You just need some uranium deposits that get surrounded by water and BAM! Controlled fission.
It gets weird if you apply this generally. Like... a photograph is just the right chemicals on a more or less flat surface. In principle, there could be a selfie of a tyrannosaurus somewhere, waiting for us to find it.
Sagan said, "If you wish to make an apple pie from scratch, you must first invent the universe." But, actually, the "you" is unnecessary.
Human life, culture, civilization... it's just a sequence of technically permitted, but ever more unlikely physical configurations.
So everything is meaningless?
No, there's a clear meaning for human life, and it runs throughout history - to find weirder and weirder configurations.
...and use them to explore the heavens and plumb the Planck-scale.
Mostly it's for food and TV, but yeah, that too.

comics.title: BAH
comics.comicText:
In the near future, all work will be automated.
The gains will be vast. Humans will live a life of unimaginable luxury, with the opportunity to spend life studying philosophy and poetry.
This will wreak a terrible psychological toll. Why? Because we won't actually read all that philosophy and poetry, and we will feel guilt. If robots are doing all the work and everyone is taken care of, the problems in your life are all CLEARLY YOUR FAULT.
Therefore, I propose a major innovation in automation! Instead of robot servants, we should make robot bosses. In fact, DOUCHEY ROBOT BOSSES.
Work smarter AND harder.
DRBs don't leave you enough time to do things you care about. THAT'S why you haven't read the entire Loeb classical library.
DRBs will give you contradictory notes, will demand unreasonable deadlines, then be PERSONALLY LATE on everything. This will make you so mentally taxed that you'll HAVE to watch four hours of TV every night while eating a tube of cookie dough.
Why were you mean to your spouse this week? Certainly not because you're a selfish jerk. You were overwhelmed by how condescending your DRB was.
And you can tune your boss's level of douchery to afford you just the right amount of leeway.
No more 3-hour lunches.
Want to spend two hours eating cheesecake for lunch? Set your boss to "really cross the line this time.
Want a long vacation? Have your boss unreasonably fire you! You've earned a break, man!
Look, humans are broken. We can't live a life of happiness unless we can convince ourselves we've "earned it.
Automated douchey bosses will take the choice out of our hands. They will function as a "guilt thermostat," allowing us to blamelessly indulge in as much pleasure as we can stand.
Couldn't we just, like, work on ourselves? Like, be more at peace with life and its vicissitudes?
Literally everyone who ever succeeded at that got poisoned, stabbed, or crucified. It's time to move on!

comics.title: Computer
comics.comicText:
Dear God, is reality a computer?
