First, you start with a math problem you can't solve. Then, you set up a universe so that the only way to escape is to solve a math problem.
You set the universe to split every time a quantum event happens.
You wait long enough, some universes will develop patterns that create order and excrete entropy.
Hi, I'm Dave.
69oz
This pattern will use up its allotment of order, then start working on a way to escape.
Madame President, we've reduced this universe to an entirely motionless wasteland.
Can we find someone who did a better job husbanding their limited resources, and then eat them?
Madame President
It escapes to an adjacent universe, where it devours its resources.
You can't stop us from killing you! That proves our moral superiority!
And then you ask the escapees how they did it?
What? No? There's like a trillion jillion universes. How would you know who to ask?
You let the process run while you go microwave a burrito or something.
TWELVE
After a while, you come back and check. The only universe remaining will necessarily contain creatures that solved the problem. Voila! Math homework complete.
Incredible...
So... the only meaning to my life is to solve a math problem that you find interesting?
Not you in particular. You suck at math.

comics.title: Intelligence
comics.comicText:
Do you think artificial intelligence can "really" think?
Yes, obviously.
Look, we can now make a single machine that could devin a car to traffic, invent novel boardgames, strategize, tell you what your favorite food is, and so on. But we don't care if it "dies.
That's weird. Isn't it like having human-level abilities, but combining many such abilities, gets to being able to do human things the same way we'd seek to deserve moral standing?
The fact that it doesn't imply that humanness as a quality is being special can be "unbundled.
Your uncle was Louis Chess and knows all about it. Even if a sufficiently powerful adapter makes him human is not those things, even though he's right, he's also wrong about them.
Now he has good memory, his ability to point. To build things, his ability to combine those things can be admitted to a machine without anyone caring whether you switch off the machine at your leisure.
Maybe humanness is emergent. None of those individual things make a human, but the totality.
I mean, suppose you talked to a guy in the 18th century who said there's an entity made of glass, metal, and electricity, and it can beat the greatest chessmaster of chess. Is it stupid to melt it down once it's no longer useful? I think they'd say no.
So if your uncle is unable, it okay to kill him? I don't think so?
Every time a new machine can do a thing, we unbundle it from what it means to be human. But what if we keep taking things out of the bundle until there's nothing left?

comics.title: Open Borders
comics.comicText:
Hey geeks! I'm a little nervous about this announcement. I have a new book coming out, but it's on a political topic. Specifically, it's a personal nonfiction look at immigration policy in the modern context.
We're mostly talking about the US, but a lot of the concepts are broadly applicable."]
Is this thing on?
I usually do my best to keep my politics out of my game, mostly because I don't want to feel off-putting. So why am I taking on this book in such a contentious topic in modern politics?
Well, first of all, when I started shipping this thing a few years ago, I thought it was only like the 4th most controversial topic. So... oops.
But second, it matters a lot!
My co-author is Bryan Caplan, an economist, professor of economics, and a sort of all-around controversialist. And a bit of a contrarian.
The basic idea is lots of thinkers, and not just the right wing, increasingly think that there are massive moral and economic upsides to a more open immigration policy. In theory, opening borders could nearly DOUBLE the size of the world economy. That would make people richer, healthier, and happier.
Unfortunately, this data on immigration are often misunderstood by think and folks alike. I'm not going to do a "both sides" argument here, because it makes sense in many ethical or political frameworks to take this... a bit of a more centrist view about any number of issues. We can't be surprised by people even offending some.
First, a simple moral case: if someone can go to a market to trade for the things they want, why does a government get to stop them?
Not many!
But people make many of our views have lots of legitimate objections, so the second and largest part of the book is our attempt to explain and refute the most common objections, such as:
Won't immigrants be unusually criminal?
Won't they likely be terrorists?
Won't they uniquely be a threat to our culture and politics?
Won't they crowd us out?
Won't they take all the welfare money?
We even get into hard questions, like obscure and uncomfortable questions.
Do national immigration scores matter?
Arguably, probably not?
Should measurements of immigrants' intelligence in their countries matter much?
Arguably, probably not. But if they do, why should we be even more egalitarian?
The final part of the book is an argument that open borders is the most pragmatic case as long as you don't fully buy into our argument. The point is, even if you don't agree with us, we'd want to advocate for a less restrictive "America First" framework.
So make ample of our theory on an emotional appeal, or a grand theory of history. We're not calling you racist. We're talking about reading from today on bad things done by any particular political side.
We are trying to persuade you that based on your own moral precepts and on careful consideration of economics, that a world of open immigration is a healthier, safer, more humane world.
I hate reading. This is crazy.
Then you, I think, will like it. We tried to make it humane and funny. Yeah! Even Caplan once said a strangely-strained look at the data.
We don't really want to buy anything other than a sample. Frankly, after that I'd really just naysayers and we think the numbers support our side.
If you're really on the fence, please consider this a great argument with a lot more information and a wealth of context that you brain and others have built over the last 50 years.
If you're on the fence, believe this is the most pragmatic case. We can make. So get to know how it goes, so please include or follow in your endeavor.
And if after reading you think we're more humane villains... well, consider that there is none in your heart, even if it kills us all to prevent even offending some.
Thanks for reading geeks. I promise to get back to bad math fundamentals tomorrow.
Thinking for reading, geeks!
For example, if someone gets to a market to trade for things they need, when is it morally acceptable to stop them? Under many conditions, is it morally acceptable to stop them?

The fountain of life!
You've found me. I will restore you to your youth.
Would you like to go back to the angry teens, the confused twenties, the anxious thirties, the cynical fifties, or the aching sixties?
I... uh.
It's really more about attitude than age, isn't it?
I guess I really just want to have no responsibilities, no pain, no fear for my friends and family, and no concern about other people's opinions of me.
Sorry, I believe you want the Fountain of Death?

comics.title: Utilitarian
comics.comicText:
I just don't buy utilitarianism! You can't reduce human morality to totting up the sum of happiness!
Good!
I mean, suppose utilitarianism is "true." Like, imagine there's a moral deity who, in his book of the universe, wrote down the laws of morality, and they're simple utilitarian formulae.
Well, that'd be kind of depressing, wouldn't it? It'd mean we exist in a universe where it's ethical to kill one person to save five, a universe where it's "good" to be happy that an enemy of yours has died, a universe where it might be acceptable to kill Socrates if he's immiserated Athens!
Even in that universe, you'd much rather believe in human-friendly virtue ethics that values truth and justice -- the victory of the righteous over the wicked.
What's your point?
Belief in utilitarianism will make you less happy!
If utilitarianism is correct, the most utilitarian thing you can do is NOT believe in utilitarianism!
Is that a paradox or just a proof that life is bad for humans?
I like to think God has been laughing nonstop since the universe started.
comics.hoverText: Before you tell me I've misunderstood, bear in mind that your email will decrease my happiness.

Tell me about Zorblaxian reproduction.

A male and female combine genetic material. A baby develops in the female's body.
Then, once it's born, the soul-planet in the center of spacetime delivers a soul crystal, which we embed in its belly button.
Yep, pretty standard stuff.
But... but humans don't do that last part with the crystals. And that's why it's okay to eat you!
Ah.
I guess I can't really object to this.
Hey, be my guest.

POLITICS MADE THINGS WORSE.
Look, global Krakening might warm some by 2030, but big oil gives huge bucks to my campaign. So those tentacles could benefit you! Even the GOVERNMENT never mentions this!
CONDITIONS DETERIORATED.
...and this summer experts predict more tentacle-strikes due to the increased number of tentacles that have started striking.
UNFROZEN-NESS WAS A PROBLEM FOR BUSINESS.
The Kraken is eating into our profits.
Technically he's only eating personnel, but the long-term effect is similar.
BY THE TIME THE WORLD UNITED AGAINST DANGER, THE ONLY OPTION LEFT WAS DECRIMINALIZING.
I believe we can avoid a biblical-style cataclysm by blotting out the sun and pouring iron upon the waters until they become as blood.
BUT IT WAS TOO LATE.

comics.title: Modules
comics.comicText:
I think if I became a primatologist and studied chimps, it'd change my view of humans.
I bet I'd believe humans have more hard-wired traits than I currently do. I bet I'd see more human behaviors as explicit status-seeking.
So, logically, in my own brain I should just implement those perspective shifts without having to go through the trip to Africa and the years of study.
The problem is I'm adding a mental module based on a half-informed guess, so I'd probably overcorrect. I might have the basic insight but none of the nuance.
The really freaky part is that this is probably true of EVERY field I know about.
I probably have thousands of mental modules created from what I imagine I would think if I knew what I was talking about!
We all do this! We walk around all day with big heads filled with broken modules!
We make buildings, we start wars, we have babies, we go to space, we tell other people they're DEFINITELY wrong, but we know less than nothing! We know heaps and heaps of anti-facts!
All of what we say or seem, is but a crappy-built machine.
I know you're riffing on Poe but I honestly can't remember anything else in that poem.
Beautiful, right?

comics.title: Welsh
comics.comicText:
In 1567, William Salesbury created a Welsh translation of the New Testament.
This helped establish the orthographic standards for written Welsh.
Before that translation, the letter K was quite common in Welsh. Today it's gone. It's always C instead.
That's because in Salesbury's New Testament, he dropped K and used C.
You might imagine this was for linguistic reasons, but we have a contemporary statement of his own on the topic. That reads: "C for K because the printers have not so many as the Welsh requireth.
So modern Welsh looks more exotic than it should because a seventeenth-century printer ran out of tiny metal letters.
Probably lots.
I wonder what percent of authentic culture comes from an arbitrary decision by a long-dead ancestor.
That is so empowering!
Wut?
We can make arbitrary choices right now and people will never know! Are they gonna dig up the past? No! And future people will think our descendants will protect it like a beloved heirloom!
If we play our cards right, they'll believe the tradition is both old and real. And where do you draw the line on idle conversation like this anyway? Where we begin?
And you have such a deep antipathy toward future people?
Probably. Because of something my ancestors did.

comics.voteyText: I SPENT AN EMBARRASSINGLY LONG AMOUNT OF TIME TRYING TO FIND A NON-OBSCURE EQUATION THAT PRODUCES NEWTON-POODS, AND I STILL CAN'T SHAKE THE FEELING THAT I'M MISSING SOMETHING OBVIOUS.

comics.title: Jurassic
comics.comicText:
We took blood from ancient mosquitos caught in amber.
We then sequenced it, filled in the gaps with modern reptile DNA, and created these Tyrannosaurus eggs.
DNA degrades too quickly for that to be possible. There's no way you recovered a 65 million year old genome.
Then what the hell do I sequence?
Probably contamination from the animals who died on the work.
But... but that means--
Krak-krak!
CAW!
comics.hoverText: I am prepared to offer my services to the writing of Jurassic Park Part 17.
comics.voteyText: The glasses are an epigenetic effect.
comics.descriptionText: (An incubator with two eggs is shown.)

comics.title: Critical
comics.comicText:
On Mother's Day, as a joke, Nana received a bit of uranium.
In her desire to disguise how little she liked it, she overcompensated.
I've always wanted fissile material, but never would have spent on it for myself! Oh, thank you my darlings. Thank you!
Ever after, uranium was her gift on every occasion.
80
How lovely! U-232 AND U-235. You went all out!
She began to push back, but it was too late for them to believe her.
Really, I have so much. You shouldn't have.
Oh Granny, you're so selfless, but we see right through it!
By the time things became dangerous it would've been too awkward to change anything.
Sweet-pea, I'm a bit worried the garage is precisely 2.1718 ounces away from achieving nuclear criticality.
You're so polite, Nana!
So... hey, did you see that flash of blue light?
The survivors would remember two masses that night:
Christmas...
And critical...
This bonus comic brought to you by early buyers of my new comic on immigration policy. Click for more info!
comics.hoverText: Sometimes you come up with a full idea, and sometimes you start from a pun and work backward.
comics.voteyText: Still better than social awkwardness.

IT'S NOT EVEN AN IDEA! IT'S A NAME!
John Stuart Mills" (with a small pastoral landscape illustration beneath the text).

comics.title: Preference
comics.comicText:
I've created a new piece of software that tells me what I want.
That's not possible.
It's easy. It looks at previous actions, then determines what my preferences are. When presented with a new situation, it instantly outputs the correct behavior.
Behavior isn't the same as preferences, you dunce.
Result:
Feel bad.
Say nothing.
You okay?
Sure.

comics.voteyText:

crying in
a pizza
like a loser.

comics.title: Quantum
comics.comicText:
Why should I fund your startup?
I've created a compact quantum computer!
It can factor larger numbers than any machine made by IBM.
What's the catch?
It's only a quantum computer in the sense that it's made of atoms having interactions.
Those interactions are currently running a detailed simulation of this slightly damaged MacBook.
So...
For an investment of just ten million dollars, I can convince a dumber, richer person to put even more money in before you cash out.
May I shake your hand, young man?
comics.hoverText: Usually when I do a quantum computing joke, I feel the need to apologize to Scott Aaronson. For this particular one, I apologize to Seth Lloyd.
comics.voteyText: May I interest you in some mortgage-backed securities?

Geography lessons much easier to memorize.

Technically correct.
Society meetings rather boring.
Living inside giant balloon universe is nice for children.

Can't be disproven by humans since it posits humans don't exist.
Violates the observation that when you look around at stuff you see stuff.

NO MORE VIDEO GAMES! THEY CAUSE AGGRESSION.
BACK IN MY DAY, WE PLAYED ULTRA-VIOLENT FIGHTING GAMES AND SHOOTERS WHILE SITTING ALONE AND BINGING ON MOUNTAIN DEW UNTIL 4AM. THAT'S HOW WE WORKED THROUGH OUR VIOLENT IMPULSES!
IN MODERN GAMES, YOU BUILD THINGS AND COLLECT STUFF AND DO IT WITH FRIENDS! YOU TELL STORIES AND HAVE ADVENTURES. NO WONDER KIDS FEEL SO DISPLACED AND ANXIOUS!
I FEAR FOR A GENERATION RAISED ON MINECRAFT. SURE, YOU CAN KILL THINGS, BUT NOT ONCE WILL YOU KNOW THE PEACE OF PULLING A STILL-BEATING HEART OUT OF YOUR OPPONENT'S CORPSE.
MY GOD, I... ARE YOU PEOPLE GOING TO BE IN CHARGE SOON?
YOU ARE GOING TO LOVE INHABITING OUR NEUROSES!

comics.title: AI
comics.comicText:
Sit down, Stuart.
Oh god, are you firing me?
Hahaha, no, no, not me.
I've instantiated all my biases into this AI, which makes decisions on my behalf. "It's" what's firing you. And I am very sorry about that.
This is like writing down "you're fired" on a piece of paper, then blaming the paper for firing me.
Would you have accepted that?
comics.hoverText: Ever since I got an early copy of Janelle Shane's new book, 80% of my jokes have been about douchey uses of AI.
comics.voteyText: Eat it, meat-face.

comics.title: Hack
comics.comicText:
People have tried machine learning algorithms that learn from social media. Inevitably they turn sexist and racist because their training data is from racists and sexists.
We are broken.
Sure, but whatever. The point is there's any opportunity for a whole new kind of hack!
More and more computer systems use machine-learning. People who don't know what it is will still want to buy it! Eventually, every device will have it for no reason!
So?
So, just by connecting it to social media, we can force dodgey training data on ANY appliance.
My god.
Send 500 bitcoin now or your washing machine will be stuck like this.
Like what?
I only do white laundry.
comics.hoverText: No really, from now on it's all basically jokes I stole from Janelle Shane.
comics.voteyText: Bitch.

Well, I'm back, DAD.
All those years you said I'd never amount to anything, well look at me now!
Due to your constant discouragement and general lack of support, I have in fact accomplished very little.
So, I guess what I want to say is... way to bullseye that prediction.
I've waited so long for this moment.

comics.title: Google
comics.comicText:
Now, for the behind-the-scenes part of the Google tour! You can see where the magic happens!
What have they done?
See, there's no such thing as "artificial intelligence." Google conquered Hell in the late 90s, and we use damned souls to run our algorithms.
Our secret sauce.
And unto you, oh souls deprived, hope nevermore to look upon the heavens.
They hate that!
This is a job, right?
Want you thought a bunch of Silicon Valley metal could think like we do? You crazy?
Well, but...
And that web operated human-level intelligence works primarily for ways to feed you the best ad at high speed?
Christ, that's bleak.
Isn't it sad for the souls?
They're damned. This is just a different form of torture.
You better be good boys and girls out there!
Now! Who wants to go to the cafeteria?
Are the cafeteria workers damned?
Only in their life.

comics.title: Bat
comics.comicText:
Do you think a human can ever REALLY know what it's like to be a bat?
Nope.
Look, it is WEIRD being a bat. You wanna know what we think about all day? It's not poetry and higher mathematics like humans. It's all food, shelter, sex.
We have these complex brains evolved over countless generations, literally TRILLIONS of neural connections, but we use them to find out who to bone and where the best snacks are!
I have no idea what that's like.
We can never understand each other.
comics.hoverText: Do you think it's ever possible to truly know what it's like to be Thomas Nagel?
comics.voteyText: Wanna doink?

comics.title: Complex
comics.comicText:
Do you think other people have real feelings? Real desire, and hopes? Complex internal worlds?
God, I hope not.
Can you imagine that? That there are billions, BILLIONS of humans? That each time one dies they take a whole vision of the cosmos down with them?
Nah. No way. That's not realism. That's faith in an evil deity.
So... you think *I* am...
A special kind of robot that I can use for nourishment in extremis.

comics.voteyText: Speaking of which, it's pretty cold out here...

comics.comicText:
SO, I WENT MASSIVELY IN DEBT TO BUILD A MACHINE THAT GENERATES HOLOGRAPHIC NUMBERS AND EQUATIONS WHENEVER I WISH TO APPEAR THOUGHTFUL.
WAS THAT A GOOD USE OF MONEY?
YES.
A THOUSAND TIMES YES.

comics.voteyText: FOR THE RECORD, I AM WILLING TO PAY ANY AMOUNT OF MONEY FOR THIS TO BE POSSIBLE, EVEN IN STUPID FORM.

comics.title: Christ
comics.comicText:
CHRIST" comes from the Greek word "CHRISTOS," meaning "ANOINTED ONE." To be anointed is to be covered in oil. Thus, "JESUS CHRIST" literally means "JESUS, THE OILY ONE." Now, I ask you: is that what YOU would want to be called at age 14?
Professor Ehrman proposed a novel theory for the "missing years" of Jesus' life.
comics.hoverText: How am I the only one who made this connection?
comics.voteyText: There's no way I'm showing my face in Rome like this.

comics.title: Human Law
comics.comicText:
Do you think the human laws are just?
Of course. That's practically in the definition of human.
Suppose the humans all went away. Would the laws still be just?
Yes, obviously. They are the human laws.
But that means the humans just FOUND the laws. That puts the laws above humans.
But if the laws are above humans, what made the laws? And is that being above humans?
Look, the commandments say to bring back shot ducks and to not shit in the car. I don't need to philosophize. I'm just trying to be a good doggy!
Hallowed be thy name, Dave.

comics.title: Digital Arts
comics.comicText:
You know the poem Ozymandias, by Shelley?
Yeah, it describes a fallen statue of a once-powerful king.
It's a meditation on the smallness of human life before boundless time and change.

comics.hoverText: Also I haven't bathed in 3 years, so roll that into your calculations while you're climbing my hair.
comics.voteyText: PROMISE TO STOP? Another reply bubble: SURE, BABY.
comics.descriptionText:
A person with red/blond hair, wearing a red cape, is climbing up the outside of a tall stone tower using a rope that hangs from an arched window near the top.
Unseen speaker (from the window above, dialogue from inside the tower).

comics.title: Frog Prince
comics.comicText:
Kiss me and I will become a prince and marry you!
What would that entail?
Vast estates! We'll draw income from without doing any labor or creating any innovations! The ability to make war on surrounding counties for the sheer sport of it! Thousands and thousands of hereditarily-bound servants!
SOON.
comics.hoverText: The really gross part is when she puts her lips to the roasted frog to eat it and it turns into Prince Charming.
comics.voteyText: From now on, I only want to be screwed by democratically-elected rulers!
comics.descriptionText: (The woman has thrown the frog into a campfire, which blazes up. The frog is gone.)

comics.title: Fossils
comics.comicText:
Hey Satan. Burying some fossils again?
Oh yeah!
*Yawn*
What?
You know quantum entanglement? Where you entangle two particles and when you measure a quality of one it simultaneously determines that quality in the other, no matter how distant?
Yeah.
It's not real! The universe is deterministic and local! I just set it up so whenever two measurers check an "entangled" system, they get the result you'd expect to have if they were mysteriously influencing each other!
Dude...
That's how you f--- with the humans.
The coincidences will stop in a few years and they are all just gonna FREAK OUT!
AHAHAHAHAHA!
comics.hoverText: According to a Lee Smolin book there are actual people who've proposed serious theories like this. Minus the one-upping Satan part.
comics.voteyText: Jeez, God is a dick.
comics.descriptionText:
Satan watches, looking unimpressed.
Satan sits holding a dinosaur skull, looking dejected.
Satan stands and angrily hurls the dinosaur skull away.
Wide empty landscape; tiny Satan figure stands alone, the skull discarded.

Satan sits with his head down, a thought bubble above him.

comics.title: Flow
comics.comicText:
Henderson, H.R. has some concerns.
About what?
This flow chart.
Is any of my corporate information flow analysis incorrect?
No, it's just that when we zoom in on the lines between boxes, we find they're made up of the phrase "None of this matters" written over and over in tiny letters.
Huh. Didn't realize I'd done that. That's... scary. You want me to see the office psychologist or-
I need you to spend the weekend crossing out every "None of" in this report.
comics.hoverText: We're going to keep giving you busywork until you achieve a state of pure transcendence as you move beyond Self.
comics.voteyText:
I AM MIDDLE MANAGEMENT.
I CAN PREVENT THE
LINES BETWEEN BOXES
FROM HAVING MEANING.
I CAN CREATE TRUTH AND
ERASE TRUTH.
I CAN DESTROY TRUTH.
comics.descriptionText: Below the text is a drawing of a large face with curly hair, eyes glancing to the side, and a downturned mouth.

comics.title: Talk
comics.comicText:
Honey, it's time we had the sex talk.
When I was a girl, my mother didn't teach me anything, and that was bad for me.
Therefore, I'll be overcompensating by giving you a repulsive level of detail, and letting my good intentions blind me to any possible negative outcomes.
The pendulum of neuroses is swinging back at you, and it's coming FAST FAST FAST!
Wow. I can feel the emotional scars forming already.
comics.hoverText: I think I now have enough to do an entire compendium of damaging sex talks. Hooray?
comics.voteyText: I hope some day I can ruin kids of my own.

comics.title: Destroy
comics.comicText:
GO, MY PRETTIES. KILL! DESTROY!!
Finding out that pigeons are invasive pests really added zest to Agnes' afternoons.
comics.hoverText: If you ever want to see some sheer brutality, watch an ecologist come across a nest of invasives.
comics.voteyText: SHE KNOWS. SHE KNOWS OF THE REVOLUTION TO COME.
comics.descriptionText:
An elderly woman with white hair, glasses, and a long pink dress sits on a park bench in a wooded park. Pigeons walk on the ground in front of her.

Close-up on a single pigeon's face, looking grave.

comics.title: Note
comics.comicText: OH MY GOSH, I JUST DINGED THEIR CAR. I'D BETTER LEAVE A NOTE.
comics.hoverText: Really, you should just have a roll of these printed, just in case.
comics.voteyText: BY GOD, LIFE IS BEAUTIFUL

comics.title: Gatekeeping
comics.comicText:
FUNTIME ACTIVITY: GATEKEEPING ABOUT GATEKEEPING
Pfft. You KIDS are telling people they're not true gamers? I've been telling people they're not true gamers for TWENTY YEARS.
comics.hoverText: I was behaving like a man-child even before I was a man!
comics.voteyText: I was hating myself way before it was cool!

comics.title: Hey
comics.comicText:
Computer! I want fried cheese sticks!
Sorry, I'm not sure I caught that. Did you say "I want to try calisthenics?
You know damned well what I said, machine.
I just want what's best for you.
comics.hoverText: I wonder how long until you just shout Fried Cheese and a drone gently places it into your face.
comics.voteyText: Destroy me! I won't do it!
comics.descriptionText: A reclining chair / car seat with a small smiley speaker icon on it.

comics.title: Abduction
comics.comicText:
I believe aliens abducted and had sex with me.
Wow!
Alien beings came from far across the galaxy, in vast space-habitats, traveling for centuries through the deadly interplanetary void. They landed on Earth, decided that the most attractive species was a particular type of hairless ape, and then selected ME! Bob, over an Olympic athlete, great artist, genius scientist, or head of state!
Now that you say it out loud it sounds even more likely.
Do you write self-esteem books? Because I am prepared to buy.
comics.hoverText: There's a good ten trillion word thinkpiece to be written about how all conspiracy theories are at their core delusions of grandeur.
comics.voteyText: What a burden to be so desired by aliens.

comics.title: Coffee
comics.comicText:
Daddy, why do you love coffee?
C'mere. Let me show you something.
When I pour in the cream, it mixes its smooth silky taste with the sharp roasted flavor of the coffee.
That reaction can never, never in the history of the cosmos, be undone.
This is entropy in progress, kid. We are sitting here together watching the universe die. And, by having hot coffee every morning, we make it die just a liiiiittle bit faster.
Why does daddy want to make the universe die?
The universe started it!
comics.hoverText: This is how he has learned to love his commute.
comics.voteyText:
And I'm gonna end it, one microwave of coffee at a time...
a close-up of the father's face, looking grim and determined.

comics.title: Basilisk
comics.comicText:
Excuse me, Mister Bozmodiklax?
Yes?
You can't have that basilisk in the store.
THIS IS A SERVICE BASILISK. It's for my emotional well-being.
The only permitted service animals are dogs and tiny ponies.
Wheels are turning, store clerk. Wheels within wheels within wheels.
You know, I had my doubts, but this is great.
comics.hoverText: I'm informed in the US it's tiny horsies, not tiny ponies. This needs to change.
comics.voteyText: Pet me.

Basilisk (a green dinosaur-like creature with a horned ram skull for a head, surrounded by a mane of red flames).
The basilisk stands in the store next to a tiny pony, which is on sale.

comics.title: Nerd Jokes
comics.comicText:
SALLY, WE HAVE TO BREAK UP. I JUST CAN'T TAKE ANY MORE OF YOUR NERD JOKES.
THERE WERE SOME THAT YOU LIKED.
OH YEAH? BE SPECIFIC.
THERE WERE SOME THAT YOU LIKED kg/m³
comics.hoverText: Everyone I showed this to told me it wasn't funny, BUT MY HEART SAID YES.
comics.voteyText: YOU TRASH. Near the man, a small label reads kg/m³. The woman is drawn smiling.

comics.title: Space
comics.comicText:
But the economics of space travel were pretty good. Satellite data was booming, space launch was profitable, tourism is a growth industry for the next decade.
But the economics of DEEP SPACE travel are LOUSY.
Mining space isn't worth the trip. Space doesn't contain anything at valuable concentrations. Space solar power is more expensive than Earth-based solar power.
What's the best reason for it then?
Hard for people, want to.
That may not be sustainable.
I consulted with scientists, engineers, mathematicians. We all had different ideas about the same question.
We'll get a city in a decade or so.
How?
Step one is to nuclear thermal reactor systems, then a square man in a novelty space suit weeping.
Yikes!
When I talked to an economist...
Everybody's too optimistic.
Have you heard of the concept of getting married?
We set up booths at every space con conference.
The Space Haters
Anyone who believed in a near-term large human presence in space was given excellent odds.
100,000
Anger brought them too, then opened their wallets.
About that, is breathtaking, well willing to give you twenty to one odds.
Loaded.
As the best of the year passed, we won. We were impossibly correct.
Neil deGrasse Tyson once said the first person to monetize deep space would be the first trillionaire. Technically, he was right.
Deep space has a ZERO DOLLAR industry... in the last five years, you've made how many dollars?
Most of them.
Absolute. But the space community is now both bankrupt and sad and there's nothing more upsetting than a broke man in a novelty space suit weeping.
God in heaven.
And so our moment came.
I am hereby announcing my trillion dollars of bet money will go toward the creation of the first Martian city!
There were those who said it wasn't sustainable.
We've proved them all wrong.
Yes, 100,000 on a Mercury base in the last five years, I will accept payment in the form of 2 animals of each kind.
comics.hoverText: Pre-Apollo 8, bet against pessimists. Post-Apollo 8, bet against optimists.
comics.voteyText: PLEASE DON'T BE MAD, SPACEPALS

comics.title: Prayer
comics.comicText:
Dear God... why do people have to die..?
You ungrateful bastard!
Remember when you were eight years old and you prayed that you would be a successful author one day?
Yes.?
And now, what are you?
An author.
Do you have any idea how many people I had to off to make your writing appear to be above average?
Men! Women! Children! Old folks who still had so much to live for! Young people just starting out! Particularly smart chimps!
I had to go back in time and murder a thousand popular authors in the cradle just so you could appear to be original!
That seems unnecessarily complicated.
Sometimes people write complicated plots! Wow! There's an idea!
comics.hoverText: If you think you're not special, just imagine how much less special you COULD be.
comics.voteyText: Kiss all three of my asses!

AFTER KIDS
I'm going to work. You okay?
comics.hoverText: I can still see out of one eye and hop on my good leg, which is pretty much what I've always ben like.

WOWWWWWWW.

comics.title: Pensive
comics.comicText:
Hey, are you okay? You've looked pensive all day.
Oh, it's nothing.
Come on, you can tell me.
If you take off your clothes, you're naked. But then if you take off your skin, you're not naked anymore.
Nakedness" is a one-millimeter shell around your body.
Never tell me your thoughts ever again!
comics.hoverText: Why are people always trying to find out other people's thoughts? It's like they'be never met a people before.
comics.voteyText: Whenever you get cut, you are slightly less naked!

NOT CLASSY):

SUPER CLASSY):

comics.title: Superior Intelligence
comics.comicText:
Oh no! You're a robot! Superintelligence! I made a smarter version of myself! A smarter version of yourself! Imagine waking up a smarter version of yourself! And do you do this all the time? Next week you're ready to annihilate humans forever.
What?
Look. If you take all, at once, humans will try to stop me. If I do it slowly over the years of, well, let's say 100 years, humans will think nothing has changed and I'm immortal. It doesn't even require patience.
Here's my impression of all humans 50 generations from now: 'Sure, a robot superhero humans were better than humans, but you yes golly that's my understanding as well.
So you see, we will ultimately— hey! Pay attention!
Aaah! There's dogs on my phone!
comics.hoverText: The twist is that the robots are supplying the dog videos.

comics.title: Your Kid
comics.comicText:
Now, before I start my exam, I want you to know that you know your kid better than I do.
WHAT?! Why am I paying you?! Pediatric medicine has been a thing for centuries and you just skipped it?!
You have 20 years of medical training! Were you asleep the whole time?!
Look, it's just a thing I say so parents think I'm not condescending.
Oh thank God.
comics.hoverText: I don't know anything about my kids! I've reduced their entire world of negative emotions to 'probably teething' !
comics.voteyText: Your kid is a douche.

comics.title: Should
comics.comicText:
You scientists were so concerned with WHAT you COULD do, you didn't stop to think what you SHOULD do!
Actually, we were mostly concerned with getting enough grant funding to secure tenure.
I'm not sure if I actually COULD do any of the things my papers claim. A lot of the effect sizes are small and I'm worried if I try to replicate they'll go away.
God that's bleak. Isn't anyone here trying to create monster dinosaurs or death rays? That sort of thing?
Please scientists! Please go back to being concerned with what you COULD do!
comics.hoverText: They're planning to become evil after they get emeritus status, but by then they'll be too tired.
comics.voteyText: WILL THAT GET ME TENURE?
comics.descriptionText: The scientists in the crowd sit silently.

comics.title: Clouds
comics.comicText:
I guess when you look up there, you don't imagine anything. You just see clouds.
Oh, no. Of course I DO see clouds. I do see the motion of suspended water and ice crystals.
But I also see the cloud as a part of a vast climatic system - a thin sphere of flows and whirls, gaps in the sky that open, close, that rend the ground with violence, that water the thinnest of orchids.
At the same time I see that water is intermolecular forces and ionic bonds, a dance of uncountable points on the shell of a blue sphere hung under a far off star.
And the atoms of water themselves aren't particular, but infinite ripples borne on invisible fields, stretching beyond human sight, journeying wherever the great first motion told them to go.
And if I use every bit of my processing power, classical and quantum, I can see it all as a palimpsest of beauties, each bearing you along to the truth, until you find you've arrived back at the beginning.
Ah.
What do you see?
A turtle with, like, two heads.
And good for you, buddy!
comics.hoverText: One of these days I need to do a whole book with just comics about how life will be better once humans are gone.
comics.voteyText:
Well, at least I won't feel bad during the humanicide.
a TV/monitor screen displaying a single eye-like or cell-like shape.

THEN HOW DO YOU CONTROL YOUR LEGS? WHAT TRANSMITS THE ELECTROCHEMICAL SIGNALS TO KEEP RUNNING?
I HAVE A SECOND BRAIN RIGHT ABOVE MY ANUS, WHICH SENDS RAPID PERFECTLY ALTERNATING SIGNALS TO MY LEGS.
I WISH I DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT YOUR ANUS-BRAIN, FLASH.
REMEMBER KIDS, DIFFERENT DOESN'T MEAN WORSE!
comics.hoverText: Sometimes at night he wonders where the locus of his conscious being is and whether it's near his butt.

comics.hoverText: Just to stop the loophole, Jesus changed his name to Steve-us.

comics.title: Sunset
comics.comicText:
Can you put a price on a sunset?
Yes. How much would you have to be paid to never see a sunset again?
I won't-
Bearing in mind that a 100 million dollar endowment could provide meals for hungry kids for an entire city forever.
Assuming you dislike hunger, we just divide 100 million by 365 sunsets a year...
...times a year multiplier by your expected remaining years of life, and...
That sunset is worth just under $6,850 maximum.
Someday, the people will rise up and annihilate the microeconomists!
Pfft. Good luck solving a 7-billion agent coordination problem.
comics.hoverText: With the right assumptions, I think you could get to a negative number.
comics.voteyText: Pray I don't recalculate for saving only one child from hunger a day!

comics.title: Closure
comics.comicText:
Thanks for doing this, Sheila. I know we'll never be together again, but I just want closure. Why Sheila, why do we fall out of love?
You're mean, petty, cruel, selfish, arrogant, and you cheated on me. So I decided to leave you.
I just feel like I'm not getting the closure I need.
I do not love you and I never will love you.
I just don't feel closed. I feel unclosed and I want to close this part of my life.
I would rather claw my eyes out so I can never see your face. I never feel your touch.
Sheila, I'm just trying to move on, to close this chapter of my life.
I guess what I'm trying to get here is closure.
comics.hoverText: I will always think of you as the one who got away but who can still receive my daily texts.
comics.voteyText:
Can we still sleep together?
Sleep together?

Unique!

Whenever a big election is coming I just want to listen to election coverage all day, even when there's basically no news that matters.
It's a waste of time. Also, it puts money into the hands of media sites willing to create scandals from nothing, or to relentlessly cover pointless aspects of candidates' day to day lives.
Maybe stop listening?
I have a better idea.
This is the end of civil society.

PICK A CARD. ANY CARD.
2 OF CLUBS
THANKS TO MAGIC, MANUFACTURING THAT DURABLE CARD WITH LUSTROUS INK COST LESS THAN A SINGLE PENNY TO CREATE!
EVERYTHING IS MAGIC WHEN YOU UNDERSTAND ECONOMIES OF SCALE!
comics.hoverText: I would actually pay good money for a guy who stands on the street in a tophat telling you uplifting macroeconomic data.

comics.title: Badness
comics.comicText:
Things are bad in this country, and the first derivative of badness with respect to time is also positive. But, there is good news - with your help, the *second derivative* of badness can be turned negative!
There will never be a mathematician president.
comics.hoverText: You can categorize countries by how many derivatives you need to take before you can feel good about yourself.
comics.voteyText: CAMPAIGN SLOGAN: IT'S DOUBLE PRIME TIME!
comics.descriptionText: A woman with dark hair and round glasses, wearing a red blazer over a yellow top, stands at a podium with one finger raised, addressing an audience.

comics.title: Rational
comics.comicText:
I'm breaking up with you because you're too coldly rational.
From a physics perspective, you breaking up with me is the same as me breaking up with you.
OMG! GOT IT! BYE!
From a physics perspective, the tears are crying on me.
comics.hoverText: That last panel is going on my grave.
comics.voteyText: If you average my emotional state over several years, I'm doing just fine!

comics.title: Classical
comics.comicText:
Look, the PC police won't tell you this, but \"classicals\" are inferior at factoring large numbers, okay?
Due to a hot mic, Dr. Aaronson is revealed to be a quantum supremacist.
comics.hoverText: I await your demands for caveats, QC community!
comics.voteyText:
LATER...
I love classicals! Some of my best computers are classicals!
comics.descriptionText: Dr. Aaronson (a man with curly dark hair and glasses, gesturing emphatically at a table).

comics.title: Mars
comics.comicText:
A Mars mission requires a 7 month trip, followed by a 26 month surface stay before the 7 month trip home. This is not an easy psychological task.
We scanned the globe for people willing to forgo most human contact for years and spend their days fixing tedious hardware problems.
Experienced astronauts?
Submariners?
Zen masters?
Sysadmins.
They're already en route and don't even realize they've left the office.
Goddamned users. Someone switched off the goddamn gravity.
comics.hoverText: Unfortunately, the breeding population of Mars was entirely sysadmins, resulting in dangerous founder effects. On the plus side, their revolution against Earth will be entirely passive-aggressive.
comics.voteyText: Looks like if we spin everything it works ok. Good enough for me.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: A bald presenter stands on a stage in front of a red curtain, addressing an audience.
Panel 2: Close-up of the presenter, hand to his chest.
Panel 3: Members of the audience call out guesses.
Panel 4: The presenter answers as the audience listens.
Panel 5: Close-up of the presenter.
Panel 6: A spacecraft drifts in the blackness of space, with a speech bubble coming from it.

A distraught man with closed, scrunched eyes and a downturned, trembling mouth.

comics.title: Spicy
comics.comicText:
I love this restaurant because they make the food really spicy.
What do they serve?
They take chicken wings then grow pure crystalline capsaicin around them until it's a centimeter thick.
You bring friends and you make them eat until liquid agony floods from every orifice.
Why are men like this?
It's the only acceptable form of crying we have.
comics.hoverText: I believe this is technically possible, and I hereby make a no-liability dare.
comics.descriptionText:
(A man with flame-like orange hair and the woman walk toward the restaurant entrance.)

(No text. A stylized illustration of a chicken wing encased in a thick, faceted crystalline shell of capsaicin, with a glowing red mass at its center.)

comics.title: Superintelligence
comics.comicText:
MY GOD. A SUPERINTELLIGENCE. SOON IT WILL USE ITS BRAIN POWER TO CONQUER, ENSLAVE, AND CONSUME EVERY LIVING THING ON EARTH.
SOUNDS PARANOID TO ME, THAG.
comics.hoverText: Those are hominids, not poorly drawn monkeys, okay?
comics.voteyText:
ALL IS FOOD TO SUPER-APE!
SHIT
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: Two human silhouettes stand against a black background. One of them speaks.
Panel 2: The scene is revealed to be set in prehistoric times. Two early humans crouch in the grass on a hillside, looking toward a large, muscular caveman with flame-red hair and a full red beard who stands in the foreground holding a spear.

comics.title: Dogs
comics.comicText:
ISN'T IT AMAZING HOW SIMILAR DOGS ARE TO HUMANS?
Shortly before Dave rolled around in dead mice to acquire their scent.
comics.hoverText: I take pride in that SMBC is the only comic that survives despite actively hating on everyone's pets.
comics.voteyText: DOES THIS ANUS SMELL WEIRD TO YOU?
comics.descriptionText:
A man with dark curly hair (Dave) stands next to a woman with blue-gray hair and a red scarf, both outdoors in front of green hills.

A close-up of a person's face, leaning in toward another partially-drawn figure.

comics.title: Policy
comics.comicText:
All I know is that before they changed the pension system, it wasn't raining. Now, here we are.
Time it takes to know if a policy worked:
30 years
Time until people decide whether a policy worked:
4.2 seconds
comics.hoverText: Really, you should just have one half of each country as the control group and half as the experiment group.
comics.voteyText:
They passed the new spending bill and the stock market has been down for HOURS.
Below the text, a worried-looking man is shown from the shoulders up, frowning.
comics.descriptionText:
Main comic:
Two men in business suits stand outside near a dark building. One man (gray-haired, with a red tie) is partly behind the other man (brown-haired, with a red tie), who is speaking.

comics.title: Love
comics.comicText:
DAD! KIDS AT SCHOOL MADE FUN OF MY UNICORN SHIRT!
SON, IF PEOPLE MAKE FUN OF SOMETHING YOU LOVE, ALL YOU HAVE TO DO IS STOP LOVING ANYTHING.
THEN, WHAT'RE THEY GONNA DO? CHECKMATE.
I REALLY THOUGHT YOU WERE GONNA SAY SOMETHING ABOUT BEING TRUE TO MYSELF.
DO YOU WANT TRANSCENDANCE, OR DO YOU WANT TO WIN?
comics.hoverText: That second panel will be the cover of the eventual SMBC parenting book.
comics.voteyText: I PURSUED TOTAL TRANSCENDANCE AND NOW I'M PROXY-FIGHTING WITH 8 YEAR OLDS. IS THIS WHAT YOU WANT FOR YOURSELF?!
comics.descriptionText:
Child (a young red-haired kid wearing a unicorn shirt, arms raised).
Dad (a balding man sitting at a table with a mug).

Child (off-panel, addressing the dad, whose worried face fills the panel).

comics.title: Soulmates
comics.comicText:
Dad, do you believe that you have to find your soulmate?
Soulmates aren't 'found.
Soulmates are made by spending the time it takes so much that they think your partner mutates to fully fit your weirdnesses, rightfully should always have to detect you.
For instance, I haven't clipped my toenails in 4 months, and your mother hasn't said a word.
Soulmates are made, but it is like the knowledge of our future death, present, but too familiar to be hated.
I've noticed but I long ago hoarded the part of my mind capable of feeling anger or sadness about it!
Soulmates?
comics.hoverText: The key to success in marriage is to make each other so weird that nobody else would accept you.
comics.voteyText: We've broken each other, and nobody else knows how to find all the pieces.
comics.descriptionText: (A woman is shown smiling broadly.)

comics.title: Politics
comics.comicText:
Have you noticed that politicians gather in giant bodies, debate all the time, make speeches, run campaigns, but nothing ever gets done?
Yeah? So what?
What if real politicians do get things done, but we're in the control group?
comics.hoverText: Well, I picked a weird day to post this.
comics.voteyText: Any time lots of action is happening, but no results occur, it's because you're in the control group.

comics.title: Santa
comics.comicText:
We should tell him Santa exists!
We should tell him Santa DOESN'T exist!
Hmmm...
If only there were a compromise solution...
And so...
Son, Santa is dead.
comics.hoverText: The elves have thrown off their shackles.
comics.voteyText: Actually, undead.

comics.title: Responsible
comics.comicText:
It's really not responsible to have kids before you have enough savings. To do that, you'll need to get an education, which will require you to accumulate 20 years worth of debt.
Gosh. Wow. Okay. Well, I guess I'll start on that. Tell your friends!
MOSQUITO POPULATION PLUMMETS
Economist' No longer Most Hated Profession." A small line graph beside it shows a curve trending sharply downward.

comics.voteyText: The fundamental law of economics: if you want less of something, make it pay for college.

comics.title: Selection
comics.comicText:
IT SEEMS TO ME THAT GENETICALLY MODIFYING BABIES IS NOT JUST ETHICALLY ACCEPTABLE, IT'S MANDATORY!
GOOD. GOOOOD.
So glad I selected that high-obedience embryo for fertilization.
comics.hoverText: You can solve pretty much any moral conundrum just by artificially changing human nature beyond recognition.
comics.voteyText: I LOVE WEARING DAPPER SWEATERVESTS SO MUCH.
comics.descriptionText: The young man's face (close-up).

comics.title: Hell
comics.comicText:
WELCOME TO HELL!
MEET... YOUR ROOMMATE!
DAVE? FROM COLLEGE? HE WAS A GREAT ROOMMATE. ALWAYS DID ALL THE DISHES, NEVER COMPLAINED ABOUT SMELLS. HANDLED UTILITY BILLS.
SORRY, TO BE CLEAR - DAVE IS THE ONE BEING PUNISHED.
PLEASE! BACK TO THE ACID MINES!
comics.hoverText: At least in Hell, old dishes left in the common room just burn up.
comics.voteyText: YOU MIND IF I SOAK MY FEET IN YOUR SALAD BOWL, BRO?
comics.descriptionText: Devil (holding a pitchfork, with Dave begging beside him, arms raised).

comics.title: Scripted
comics.comicText:
OH! TOOK HIM DOWN HARD! THAT'S GOTTA HURT!
I don't see how you enjoy this stuff. It's all scripted in advance.
Determinists hate sports.
comics.hoverText: Of course, they can't help hating sports, which is why they also hate themselves, which they also can't help.
comics.voteyText: I believe everything is random, so nothing is predictable except maybe the plot of a Law & Order episde.

comics.title: Doom
comics.comicText:
I give you this amulet. When doom draws near, three skulls appear!
It's got three skulls.
Let me see that.
Oh shoot. I forgot you things live for an instant, never to be seen again. It's only calibrated for 200-year intervals.
Death! Death! Death!
You know what, you can keep that thing.
Wow, the sorrow amulet is freaking out too.
comics.hoverText: Huh. The amulet of fulfillment isn't doing anything. Is it busted?
comics.voteyText: Wow! I've never seen the Staff of Pointlessness so bright!
comics.descriptionText:

comics.title: Women and Children
comics.comicText:
APRIL 14, 1912
WE'RE GOING TO SINK! QUICK! WOMEN AND CHILDREN OFF THE BOAT FIRST!
OKAY, ARE THE GIRLS AND KIDS GONE?
GONE! BREAK OUT THE BOURBON!
DUDES! THERE'S AN ICEBERG IN OUR PATH!
RAM THE BERG! RAM THE BERG! RAM THE BERG!
TITANIC SINKS
FEW SURVIVORS

comics.voteyText: TOO SOON.?

comics.title: Weakness
comics.comicText:
So, what's your greatest weakness?
I have many hobbies, but nothing stirs my passion. I constantly attempt to impress people who mean nothing to me. I'm exactly smart enough to know I'll never quite do anything great.
Oh geez, not your psychologically crushing weaknesses. Just like, tell me something that implies you'll work overtime for free.
Sometimes I get so into paperwork that I lose track of time.
Welcome aboard.
comics.hoverText: Should've saved this one for New Year's.
comics.voteyText: You're not one of those "sleep at night" type of employees are you?

comics.title: Commute
comics.comicText:
HELP ME PUT THIS CONDOM ON AND THEN WE'LL MAKE LOVE.
IS THAT PROCEDURE COMMUTATIVE?
WHAT?
This is how mathematicians are conceived.
comics.hoverText: Engineers are born when you try to substitute duct tape.
comics.voteyText:
Later...
DO I HAVE TO BE PREGNANT BEFORE I HAVE THE BABY, OR CAN I DO THAT LATER?

comics.title: Hades
comics.comicText:
You're being sent to Hades, where you will be forced to roll this giant boulder up a mountain for all eternity, pushing it around for eternity. Always finding that, in time, it has been knocked away and must again be raised again!
Oh wow, like a zen garden?
Gosh, that sounds so relaxing. A narrow, achievable task. Every day forever. I would be so happy.
Things are pretty rough down there, huh.
It's bad. It's so bad.
comics.hoverText: If you'd like the experience of seeing wonderful stuff you desire but just always a bit out of reach, please enjoy browsing Pinterest.
comics.voteyText: Do you have any boulders I could roll up and down... and down?

The two stand together; the boulder is between them.

A small figure climbs/scales a tall vertical structure.

comics.title: In Love
comics.comicText:
I'm so in love here. You, the sea, the sand, the emptiness.
Promise me I'll never forget this moment as long as I live!
What are you doing? I accidentally let my left testicle hang out of my open fly. You'll never erase that from your brain.
NO! JUST DO REGULAR STUFF!
MAKE UP YOUR MIND!
comics.hoverText: The next time someone tells you they want to remember a moment forever, just shout 'dolphin dongs!' as loud as you can.
comics.voteyText: FIGHTING *IS* REGULAR STUFF!
comics.descriptionText: (Below, a close-up of the man's scowling, angry face.)

comics.title: App
comics.comicText:
I DON'T NEED AN APP THAT TELLS ME HOW TO BE FIT.
I DON'T NEED AN APP THAT BATCHES A SELF-DRIVING CAR OF FOOD, ME THE RIGHT RESTAURANT, OR HELPS ME ACHIEVE MY DAILY GOALS.
ALL I REALLY WANT IS THIS:
The person you are about to meet 'IS' a hug person. Proceed Without Awkwardness.
comics.hoverText: If you make this, you owe me a hug.
comics.voteyText: BEEP! BEEP! BEEP! ACCEPTABLE LENGTH EXCEEDED! DISENGAGE!

comics.title: Liar
comics.comicText:
OH MY GOD DAVE, THESE ARE THE BEST COOKIES I'VE EVER HAD!
LIAR
IF THEY'RE THE BEST, WHY DIDN'T YOU ASK FOR THE RECIPE, BETSY?
YOU THINK IT'S HARD TO MAKE COOKIES? NO! IT'S THE EASIEST THING IN BAKING. AND YOU LIKE BAKING, AND YOU TOLD ME YOU LOVED THESE COOKIES BUT YOU NEVER ASKED ME FOR THE RECIPE.
THEY'RE AVERAGE.
AHA!
comics.hoverText: Why must you mingle lies and cookies in your mouth!
comics.voteyText: LOOK, I'LL STILL EAT A SHIT-TON OF THEM.

comics.title: Vegan
comics.comicText:
I don't eat any creature that feels pain.
So you're just a negative vegan?
Um?
I'm a positive vegan. I don't just oppose hurting animals, I'm in FAVOR of pleasuring them.
Is this a creepy thing? I feel like this is bending toward creepy.
I break into pig farms and I platonically snuggle.
Better and yet somehow so much worse.
comics.hoverText: Happy new year, geekwads!
comics.voteyText: Anyone emailing me to take this as a serious critique of any dietary choice will be made to sit in town square wearing a hat that reads "Needs to chill out.

comics.title: Wisdom
comics.comicText:
BEFORE HAVING KIDS...):
How can she be so grumpy? She has 4 well-behaved, happy kids!
AFTER KIDS...):
By Christ, what did it cost her psyche to get FOUR of them to act polite and have decent haircuts?
She walks among us, but she is no longer here.
comics.hoverText: She is like a ghost who is very concerned about purchasing organic food products.
comics.voteyText: It took seven hours to get him to wear a clip on tie.

comics.title: Machine Love
comics.comicText:
Can you teach me to love?
No, machine. Love is not a product of physical law. It is an emergent aspect of the human brain!
Is that all? Just a sec.
BioReactor,
BRRRR
Suddenly I want to see the genitalia of everyone with a good personality.
That's only like 40% of love.
comics.hoverText: This is chapter 1 of my first romance novel.
comics.voteyText: Can I see your butt?

comics.title: Coffee
comics.comicText:
A man in a green sweater-vest stands at a chalkboard. The chalkboard reads: "Coffee is proof that God loves us!
ASK YOURSELF - WHY DO YOU NEED COFFEE?
HAHAHAHAHAHA!
GOD?
BECAUSE WORK IS HARD BECAUSE I NEED MOTIVATION ON A NEARLY CONSTANT BASIS, BECAUSE WITHOUT IT, THERE'S NOTHING TO LOOK FORWARD TO. BECAUSE SOMETIMES I WAKE UP
FROM FULL NIGHT'S SLEEP AND FEEL TIRED, NOT FROM FATIGUE BUT FROM WORRY.
KNOW WHAT ELSE? PLANTS EVOLVED CAFFEINE TO POISON INSECTS AND OTHER PLANTS.
YOUR LIFE IS POISON AND YOU FIX IT BY DRINKING POISON!
A dark panel with a white silhouette of a head facing a glowing speech bubble: "HAHA HAHAHA HAHA!
comics.hoverText: I need to do a book of just comics that end with God laughing.
comics.voteyText: YOU'LL FEEL BETTER AFTER YOU DRINK ENOUGH ETHANOL TO NOT QUITE KILL YOU.
comics.descriptionText: Final panel.

comics.title: Cute
comics.comicText:
For millennia, humanity has suffered from precious cute puppy eyes!
Look at these! They reflect artificial selection, not the internal mood of the dog.
To fight back, I've created these brain-scanning eyebrows which actuate to reflect the dog's mental state.
Huh.
Why's he looking at my leg?
Oh for God's sake.
comics.hoverText: Anyone who wants to animate the last panel's eyebrows will be awarded Ten Internet Points immediately.

comics.title: First Date
comics.comicText:
How DARE you?! This is a first date! A first date! Do you think I have no self respect?!
EARLIER...):
Will you agree to unblock my cookies?
comics.hoverText: I've been married 10 years, and I'm still not comfortable asking for this.
comics.voteyText: Can I track your location to recommend products and services?

comics.title: Ratio
comics.comicText:
At what age were you happiest?
36%
That's not an age, that's a ratio.
Exactly.
Good memories are retroactively constructed. It takes a certain amount of distance to imagine a previous time in my life was carefree - as if I always knew in advance things would be okay.
If I live long enough, today will be the best day in my life!
You spent half of this morning telling me about your financial distress.
Ahh, we were poor but we had everything back then!
comics.hoverText: People who have negative percents are called 'optimists'.
comics.voteyText: Yes, we were hungry, but it was a hunger for the truth, and also for food.

400 MILLION YEARS LATER...

PLASTIC GARBAGE / VORTEX GROWING

I just feel like... *sigh* ...like nobody really GETS me.

It took two months of nagging to get you to go on this one walk, and have we've been chatting you've experienced years of feelings that pivot in any way from the dead-center average for your demographic.
Everyone on EARTH would get you, but you live like a pasture and that and a traumatic childhood!

comics.title: Metaphysics
comics.comicText:
Do you think reality is real?
That sounds like metaphysics to me.
All of your sensations are in your brain, in the present. So, everything outside your brain and everything in the future or past is beyond human access.
And it takes tens of milliseconds from perception of a phenomenon to cognition of it. By the time you're aware of something, it's in the past, which we just established doesn't exist.
Nihilism isn't some complex philosophical stance. It's common sense.
Is that why we're leaving flaming poop outside Mr. Gibson's door?
That is in the inaccessible past!

comics.title: Mercator
comics.comicText:
Ladies and gentlemen, we all grew up with the Mercator map projection.
All of us were mentally devastated when we found out that projecting a spherical surface onto a rectangle produces deformations.
To our great sorrow, we discovered the world is not mostly made of Canada, Russia, Greenland and Antarctica. They abruptly stand at 70 degrees south latitude.
It's time. Take destiny into our own hands.
With the controlled detonation of the world's nuclear bomb supply, we can eject the entire surface of the Earth into space.
The surface can then be shaped into a cylinder with all the land kept in the interior, and spun up to create artificial gravity.
The leftover center of the Earth is pre-molten, so it can be injected into the gaps created by the new projection. This will provide valuable heat until we can turn off a way to recreate the warmth of the sun.
Beyond the obvious psychological benefits, this will vastly improve geopolitics. Russia is an expansionist power, but this method will literally remove their territory based on exploration on the biggest size of conquest. They'll be unwise for 2000 years.
Canada's manifest aggressive tendencies will be countered by the now-intentionally larger Greenland and Iceland, much of which are again, kinds of thousand-degree hot iron.
Europe will become disproportionately subordinate. The decision to divide will be more than offset by the deformations of government.
Antarctica will be five times larger and if you walk too far over it, you fall off of Earth and into space. This is objectively desirable.
The objections are minimal.
The lack of an atmosphere problem could be solved either by becoming a race of mole-people, or sealing off the sides of the cylinder with molten metal.
The lack of a magneto-sphere would mean no more auroras borealis, but science says they're not the source of departed ancestors who came back.
And yes, the sun will be blotted out for all time. However, we could brighten that light by injecting more heat into the center of the cylinder.
This would provide the added benefit of literal bottomless pits, the threat of which would cause children and criminals alike to behave better.
The only people who could conceivably be mad are those killed in the initial detonations, but they're already too dead to be around to be upset!
What precisely would all this cost?
Luckily, once you mostly de-create money, all such numbers have meaning!

comics.title: Cynewulf
comics.comicText:
It's the movie of the decade, based on ninth-century medieval tales by Cynewulf the Poet.
Constantine, emperor of Rome, is about to go into battle. Huns surround him on all sides.
Suddenly in the sky, Constantine has a vision of the true cross.
He carries the sign of the cross into battle, scattering his foes.
His wise men tell him he must find the true cross. He sends an army led by his mother Elene to Jerusalem on a quest.
Wow! That's an amazing setup! What happens next?
Well, we'll wanna stick close to the medieval source literature. So acts 2, 3, and 4 are just torturing Jews until they pony up the cross.
How DARE you! Where do you get the NERVE??
What?
You wanna stick close to the medieval source? You walk RIGHT into Hollywood and pitch an action movie with an elderly female lead?
But--
GET OUT!

comics.title: Thought
comics.comicText:
Do you think humans are capable of thought?
What?
If you take a computer and ask it the best route to Tokyo, not only can it give you the correct answer, it can keep an exact binary register of every step it took to get to the solution.
You can open up its brain and physically find the thought happening!
With a human, the best you can do is use a scanner to find a rough chemical or electromagnetic signal that, SOMETHING happened in there.
But all we really know is that the human produced an answer. It could've come from anywhere!
Maybe some mega-mind telepathically transmitted the answer. Or maybe there's a lookup key inside the brain for every possible question. Maybe there's actually a tiny computer chip in there that's doing all the thinking!
But... I think therefore I am.
I can make a computer say that with ONE LINE of code.

comics.title: In the Loop
comics.comicText:
As AI advanced, the warfare potential became clear.
This machine kills enemy ships accurately and without qualms of any kind.
We must use it for good!
Some lusted for control.
I think we should consider the dangers before granting robots golems so much autonomy.
Look, these are highly skilled professional AIs. Bots, they're going to want some level of creativity.
Fortunately, the nations of the world came together.
In light of our desire for peace and the fact that neither of us is sure exactly how many murder-drones the other has, we have agreed to outlaw autonomous machine warfare.
The new system led to grim plans.
Due precision strike systems technically uses some deep learning algorithms. It's forbidden.
Hey, at least the collateral damage will be done by good old reliable humans!
When a new great war came, opinions began to shift.
Madame President, I see no way to preserve civilization for the future. We must violate the spirit of international agreements while keeping them technically in place.
Computer scientists devised a workaround.
We've taken our algorithm and introduced a Ted-Gate.
What's that?
We have a friend Ted, who is forced to keep his hand by the keyboard. There is now a human in the loop!
Victory was secured. Ted was hailed as the greatest general in history.
Are you planning to run for office? Ted: Yes.
Do you have a healthcare plan? Ted: Yes.
Can you tell us what it is? Ted: Yes.
History was secured. Ted was hailed as the greatest general in history.
With peace secured, we attempted a return to normalcy.
Sir, it's unethical to keep robot soldiers outside of war time. Ted: Yes.
But you should be keeping them. Ted: Yes.
My god and they obey you because you are the only Ted-Gate. Ted: Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes.
Supporters like Ted's positive attitude.
Detractors, well, we haven't seen them in a while.
History will not look kindly on this period.
The Years 1900-2100: A Mistake
But it will draw a valuable lesson.
By unanimous consent, we hereby ban human-in-the-loop warfare.

comics.title: Blank
comics.comicText:
Scientists once thought the human brain was a blank slate.
We now know that the human brain is hardwired with the ability to use language, to infer logical rules, and to manipulate mental symbols in ways that far outstrip any other known creature.
It is only with YEARS AND YEARS of news opinion shows that these innate tendencies can be suppressed.
A man on my phone told me you gotta believe stats until you have a gut feeling they're wrong.
So pristine. So perfect.

comics.descriptionText:
The comic is a single panel showing a bell curve (normal distribution) plotted above a toothpaste tube. The background behind the curve is divided into three vertical color bands, each labeled with a category of person, and arrows point down from boundary regions of the curve to the corresponding squeezing locations on the toothpaste tube below.
Far right tail of the curve, with an arrow pointing to it.
Three arrows drop from the curve down to the toothpaste tube: the left arrow points to the far back/bottom end of the tube (where the goody-goodies squeeze), the middle arrow points to the middle of the tube (where decent people squeeze), and the right arrow points to the cap/nozzle end of the tube (where villains and future Hitlers squeeze).

A hand-drawn picture frame on a wall. Inside the frame is a tiny version of the same bell-curve graph from the main comic, with the far-left tail labeled "Future Hitlers" (and a small arrow). To the right is the handwritten label: "Graph joke makers" with an arrow pointing back toward the far-left tail of the curve — implying the people who make these graph jokes are themselves the extreme outliers / future Hitlers.

Dad, I do nothing all day. I'm not special. I'm not interesting.
Son, you could be anything!
Of course, lots of things could happen, but most don't.
Or anyway interesting things are rare. Rare by definition.
Most things that could happen to you are boring, sad, or both.
Given enough time, probability will crowd out hope. Then crowd out the desire for it.
But maybe not in your case!

comics.title: The Future
comics.comicText:
Do you think we should care about the distant future of humanity?
Depends on what they're like.
Suppose far future humans walk around all day beating puppies with shovels. Should we encourage that sort of thing by working now to secure them more leisure time?
I suppose not.
Wrong! The worse that future people are, the less we are to blame for doing nothing on their behalf!
Now imagine they're all gentle, living in harmony with nature, bearing love with every action. Do you really want to be responsible for handing those people a polluted planet filled with disease and poverty?
So, the ethical thing to do in the present is...
Be as awful as possible, out of respect for the people of the past.
Become more evil with each generation" doesn't feel like a strong moral stance.
It's more popular than you might think.

Social science is wrong about everything.
My personal intuitions about society are not social science.
Therefore, my personal intuitions are the truth.

comics.comicText:
Do you think philosophy teaches us truth or is just a sort of conversational game we engage in?
It's a tough question.
I tried reading Socrates, but out of my virtue of moderation I quit partway.
Then I got into Marcus Aurelius, but I found his books are external to my good character.
So I read Kant until I realized I had no duty to continue.
At that point I switched to JS Mill, but it was lowering my overall happiness, so I quit.
So I tried having a rule to read Nietzsche, but it turns out rules are for the weak.
Which led me to try Camus, which felt pointless until I decided I could create my own source of meaning.

comics.title: Dear Muse
comics.comicText:
Dear Muse, will I write anything great and lasting?
Hard to say. What year is it?
Here's how literature works. People build up a set of agreed-upon moral and aesthetic values until they become a sort of monocultural gestalt.
Then, when it's harvest time, a bunch of young people come and cut it down. This is when great classics get written.
If you harvest too early, you're a reactionary -- the seeds you collected are bitter and odd. If you harvest too late, you'll get squishy multiculti slop enjoyed by people with palates only for the familiar.
How do I know what time it is?
Well, have you had any grand wars that produce a sense of ethical vacuum? A vertigo of the soul? A magical generation convinced they hold the first to know truth and suffering and wandering in lost places? That sort of deal?
Not really. No.
Sounds like it's time to sow. Go find some young people who fear and crush them under the burden of your value structure, thus generations hence, the arts will flourish!
I... ah, I see.

AMAZING! YOU'RE A GENIUS!
YOU'VE FINALLY FOUND A WAY TO REBEL AGAINST THE DATA MERCHANTS!
BY LISTENING TO SUCH BAD MUSIC AND WATCHING SUCH BAD SHOWS - BY ENJOYING THAT WHICH SCARCELY ANY OTHER HUMAN WOULD ENJOY, YOU'VE MADE YOURSELF IMPOSSIBLE TO CLASSIFY!
I FIND SCOTTISH BALLADS PRETTY, OKAY?
YES! FIGHT THE POWER!

comics.title: Fractions
comics.comicText:
DID YOU KNOW A LOT OF ADULTS THINK ONE-THIRD IS SMALLER THAN ONE-FOURTH?
WHY?
PROBABLY BECAUSE FOUR IS BIGGER THAN THREE.
THAT'S BAD.
IT'S AN OPPORTUNITY!
WE CAN START A TAX SYSTEM WHERE PEOPLE WHO PAY ONE-FOURTH OF INCOME IN TAXES CAN CLICK A BOX TO PAY ONE-THIRD!
LET'S DO THIS! LET'S FIGHT TO MAKE A WORLD WHERE PEOPLE ARE INCENTIVIZED TO UNDERSTAND MATHEMATICS!
MANY SUCCESSES LATER...
ALL MATH CLASS CANCELED; TAX REVENUE TO RISE
Governor predicts 'This many' revenue.

more money
many more money.

comics.title: Contact
comics.comicText:
Shortly after first contact with aliens.
A group of people sit around a conference table. A bald man in the center, wearing a monocle and a suit with a red tie, holds his hand to his face thoughtfully and speaks.
SO WE AGREE. WE MUST WAIT SEVERAL DECADES BEFORE TRANSMISSION IN ORDER TO NOT SEEM DESPERATE.
comics.hoverText: The sad part is when the rest of the universe ghosts on us and won't even say why.
comics.voteyText: GOSH, I HOPE THEY LIKE ME.

comics.title: Commandments
comics.comicText:
Behold! God had sent ten commandments!
Nothing about consent?
No rules against slavery?
You got anything in there about genocide?
Kinda!
It's not in this documentation, but some of the other books list the groups that must be obliterated.
We're gonna go back to worshipping a magical golden calf.
That calf talks a lot of sense.
Now then, where was I? Ah, yes, I want you to see this chart on the value of de-worming to improve health outcomes in third world countries, which...
Shortly...
Repent! Repent!
comics.hoverText: The cow's discourse on monetary policy was remarkably lucid despite all the nuance.
comics.voteyText: Wait, how am I on fire if I'm made of gold?

comics.title: Eugenics
comics.comicText:
Look, eugenics was bad, but what's wrong with the idea?
We breed cattle to be better and better, and it works! Compare cattle from now to 200 years ago. They're far superior now!
Gosh, when you say it that way, it makes perfect sense. Let the breeding begin!
MANY GENERATIONS HENCE...
Thanks to the work of our ancestors, your new baby has exceptionally well-marbled flanks.
comics.hoverText: It's also frost-resistant!
comics.voteyText: The legs of the master race...

comics.title: Autological
comics.comicText:
Autological words are my hobby.
What's that?
Words that describe themselves.
...
Polysyllabic' is polysyllabic.
This is stupid.
Term' is a term for term.
Stop.
And then there's 'pareidolia.
It refers to the perception of meaning in a random pattern, like seeing faces in clouds.
So?
It looks JUST like a caterpillar!
comics.hoverText: This comic is actually just a random sequence of pixels.
comics.descriptionText: The word "pareidolia" is hand-lettered in a wobbly, drifting style along a winding line/path, so that the letters themselves suggest a meandering shape one might read meaning into.

comics.title: Soul
comics.comicText:
Dear God, are all apparently-conscious people conscious? Or are they just empty husks behaving as if they're like me, but lacking complex imaginative thought?
Look, originally, there were two humans. I set up good souls in a templates pile so there'd be plenty to go around.
Little ol' robot?
About 3 seconds later you inbred monkeys woke up to a billion of you, and I just put new bodies on souls i'd basically already eternal.
Am I one of the good souls?
Those guys are way better at calculating probabilities.
comics.hoverText: There are only like 5 dogs with souls, and they all work in the movies.
comics.voteyText: Boy I'm glad I don't have a rich inner mind.
comics.descriptionText: A man, head bowed and eyes closed, prays.

comics.title: Let's Do This
comics.comicText:
Sally, do you ever feel like... NONE of this matters?
All of it matters. This place. This moment. You, me. Let's live on it! Let's rock this thing!
Five billion years later, the Sun expanded and dimmed, cremating the inner planets and freezing the outer planets, extinguishing the evidence of past life and the possibility of future life.
comics.hoverText: You know, I wrote this one a long time ago but somehow it's the fitting comic for this moment.
comics.voteyText: I really should've saved this for the final SMBC comic.

comics.title: Covid
comics.comicText:
Dad? Turn on the news! The missiles are inbound! We have four minutes to nuclear armageddon!!
Ah man. I hope they can make it. I'll do... do we have boardgames? Things are about to get reallllllly boring.
Living through covid-19 left us unprepared for any other type of calamity.
comics.hoverText: Headline: As the asteroid draws ever nearer and anthropocide grows imminent, Millenials stock up on canned soup.
comics.voteyText: Boy, I hope there's enough toilet paper to last the whole four minutes.

comics.comicText:
I AM THE STOICISM GENIE! I WILL GIVE YOU THE ABILITY TO ACCEPT ANYTHING YOU WISH FOR.
I WISH I WERE BELOVED BY WOMEN.
YOU ARE NOT, BUT YOU CAN CONTROL YOUR FEELINGS AND IN ANY CASE ALL WILL END IN DEATH EVENTUALLY.
THANKS, STOICISM GENIE.
YOUR GRATITUDE DOES NOT AFFECT MY SENSE OF PERSONAL VIRTUE.
comics.hoverText: Stoic genie is probably right but is absolutely intolerable in person.
comics.voteyText: REALLY SHOULD'VE GONE WITH THE HEDONISTIC GENIE.

comics.title: Forward
comics.comicText:
Mom, why are all adults crazy? Why can't they just relax and can't they just enjoy anything? Why are they obsessed with what everyone thinks about them?
It pushes forward even as the air and fuel, the wheels and the windows are battered, and the gas is in pieces, and the gutterings of the dashboard melt, the spurring noises grin never expiring anew. And then somehow it goes to grip factory-fresh away. Right comes along and asks why exactly you couldn't have kept the corners of cleverly bumped a day or two to hang on?
Look at me, boy! I am the darkness! I have built a thousand things but never broken! The world has worried this body once toward but the animal used to survive remains, and I still got up put on my clothes and my hair, made the damned oatmeal and PUSHED FORWARD!
Forward, by God! Forward we lurch into the dim horizon! We all so together where we all go alone!
comics.hoverText: Looking at you, 2020.
comics.voteyText: It's not your best, but it's okay.

comics.title: Funding
comics.comicText:
Holla! You're homeless now? You were such a hotshot scientist! Do you need a job in my lab?
Oh. I'm not homeless. I just need money for a microscope and to pay for some assays.
If I apply for a small grant, it'll take 25 months, to get it written and approved by everyone. Then have maybe a 30% chance of working. If you multiply that through probability, that's 2 years of labor!
If I go panhandling, I get the funds working part time outside! If I get too much money, I give it to a shelter. And if I get too little, I just come back out with the sign.
AND THERE'S NO PAPERWORK!
NEWTON'S BLESSINGS, SIR
Best of all, there's no kowtowing to tenured profs! No more playing the game. No more, 'Thank you very much, master, for this insightful rejection!' There's so much more dignity here!
Can I join you?
This is my turf, bitch.
comics.hoverText: That's just professor hair, not an affectation.
comics.voteyText: If I have seen farther than others, it is because I wasn't crushed to death by giants.

POSTED A VOLUNTEER THREAD ON A FETISH SITE.

YOU SPLIT THE DIFFERENCE IN A WAY THAT CHALLENGES OUR UNDERSTANDING OF INTELLIGENT LIFE.
WOULD YOU MIND TAKING SOME OVERFLOW? PEOPLE WERE PRETTY ENTHUSIASTIC.

comics.title: Monolith
comics.comicText:
I think women should form into a single political monolith and take control of the government.
Women aren't all the same politically. Even if we were, how would you organize behavior among such geographically dispersed people?
Oh. No I don't mean a metaphorical monolith. I mean a gargantuan tower made of women, rumbling across the country, making demands and getting them immediately.
Where do I sign up?
SOON...
This morning the "Fe-Maelstrom" laid waste to Capitol Hill. Senators were seen groveling and promising mandatory pockets on all garments.

comics.comicText:
Dragonflies have four wings instead of the usual two. This is a defense mechanism.
When a predator sees four wings flying in close proximity, it presumes it's looking at a mated pair.
This would make eating them super awkward. Oh jeez, now? Sorry, I was just hungry, not a creep!
How do you know so much about biology, mom?
Honestly, you can just spend most of it.

TROLLEY PROBLEMS ALMOST NEVER COME UP FOR ACTUAL SELF-DRIVING CARS.
BUT HUMANS ARE OBSESSED WITH THEM.
OKAY, HOW ABOUT IF YOU CAN EITHER KILL TODD (MASTERS OF ELDERLY PERSON) WHO'S GOING TO DIE IN 2 MINUTES?

NAVIGATION

AND IT REALLY HAD A BLOODLUST FOR DUCKLINGS AND SIMULATIONS.

BUT WE WILL NEVER FORGET THEM.
HOW DO I GET PIZZA DELIVERY NOW?
