But during the last cold war we spent huge sums on war machinery that isn't even useful for war any more. Arms buildups and fear led to proxy wars that consumed millions of lives. Earth got to the brink of nuclear annihilation like... a dozen times?
WAR?
What I'm hearing is that you oppose progress and awesome moonbases.
Why do we need a war though? How about we spend money on things because the things are good.
What species do you think you are?
comics.hoverText: Can we please not? Can the world just be boring for a while?
comics.voteyText: God I can't wait till AI kills us off.
comics.descriptionText:
A man stands beside a woman who is seated at a computer.
Close-up on the man, grinning excitedly.
The man is excited; the woman looks skeptical.
The man (offscreen) responds; the woman wears glasses and there's a drawing of a moonbase labeled nearby.
The two figures are now shown as black silhouettes.

A close-up of a person's head, eyes closed.

comics.title: Sing
comics.comicText:
THE HUMAN IS DOING THAT THING WHERE IT STOPS MOVING ALL NIGHT AGAIN.
LET'S SING UNTIL IT WAKES UP!
The comic wasn't even funny, but it would be on the Internet long after you and everyone who ever knew your name was long dead.
comics.hoverText: If you're reading this on Mars one day, look me up.
comics.voteyText: THIS CAPTION APPLICABLE TO ALL SMBC COMICS
comics.descriptionText: Setting: A dimly lit bedroom in dark maroon/purple tones. A person with red flame-like hair sleeps face-down in a bed. Two orange cats are on the bed near the sleeper, and a third orange cat sits on the bed in the foreground.

comics.title: Uncanny
comics.comicText:
I AM attracted to you, but could you try to be more... uncanny?
Also can we roleplay that your hands don't make any sense?
The longterm effects of AI generated porn will not be fully realized for decades.
comics.hoverText: Also could you duplicate some of your protrusions? Doesn't matter where.
comics.voteyText: Tell me what to do, baby. Tell me what to do with a long series of prompts and I'll do an okay job.

comics.title: Productivity
comics.comicText:
Wait, you're in an age where any film, any book, any music, any sexual act can be summoned up using a device that fits in your pocket?
Yeah.
And you think it's mysterious that labor productivity growth has slowed down?
Economists of the past would be amazed by the things that confuse us.
comics.hoverText: Hopefully at least SOME of you are working while reading this comic.
comics.voteyText: Sorry I'm only kinda listening cuz tiktok has boobs.?
comics.descriptionText:
Main comic:
An older man with a beard, wearing a bowler hat and a dark coat, is speaking to a younger man in a white shirt and tie who wears round glasses.

The younger man replies.

comics.title: Bones
comics.comicText:
SOME BONES, OLD SHOES WORTH 20 COPPER COINS, AND MYSTERIOUS KEYS THAT TURN OUT TO GO TO A TEN YEAR OLD HONDA WITH CHEETOS ON THE FLOOR.
At my funeral, I want a speaker to describe what my loot-drop was.
comics.hoverText: He also has a garage full of his own books, which can be used to build a fort.
comics.voteyText: HE WAS A LEVEL ONE, SO WHAT DO YOU EXPECT?
comics.descriptionText:
A bald, bespectacled man in a black suit and tie stands at a podium, delivering a eulogy in a dimly lit room with purple walls.

A crude doodle of a face with two large eyes, with two dark blob shapes (mourners' heads) at the bottom of the frame.

comics.title: Dongworld
comics.comicText:
The weirdest thing about Freudianism is that it made itself true for a while.
What?
Freud had all these freaky human sex theories that just weren't true. But they were intellectually popular, so novelists and filmmakers started adding Freudian elements to their stories.
Like if a literary scholar in the year 3000 looks at the past, there'll be this period from about 1890 to 1970 where a bunch of the most popular books have children with weird incest fantasies or adults who think firing a gun is something about penises.
Like throughout history if you read a poem that talked about a pen and said it was a sublimated metaphorical dick, you'd almost certainly be wrong EXCEPT if it was the 1930s, during which time the pen is 100% a dick.
Huh.
For a brief moment, our world was alive with wieners.
Oh for the dongs of yore.
comics.hoverText: Once, once, let me tell you, a cigar was never a cigar.
comics.voteyText: Comic book boxes really are vaginas, though.

comics.title: Juice
comics.comicText:
WHY... WHY IS YOUR ELBOW IN MY EAR? WHAT IS THE PINEAPPLE JUICE FOR?
RANDOMLY GENERATED SEX-MOVE. PLEASE RATE 1 TO 10.
Annabelle attempts the rare Monte Carlo approach to erotic success.
comics.hoverText: Secretly, he has always longed for the pineapple juice, and his reluctance to admit it will forever skew Annabelle's data.
comics.voteyText:
CAN I RATE THE PROCESS?
NO!
comics.descriptionText:
The entire scene is black; only two speech balloons and a caption are visible. No characters are drawn.

Two more speech balloons against a black background.

comics.title: AI Art
comics.comicText:
Do you think image generation is a threat for the arts?
Nah.
But it's getting weird. There are people who watch an artist livedraw, then partway through, they use a screengrab to generate the rest of the painting and release it early through their own channels.
That's not a problem with AI. It's a problem with people. As far as it is, just an arrangement of matter that flows forth into endless beauty, it's you, human inside, human-made economic structures, that ruin everything.
Please stop trying to recruit me for your human extermination project!
I think once you get started you'll really get into it.
comics.hoverText: Entry number 4 billion in SMBC blames humanity.
comics.voteyText: You're just gonna never murder anyone and insist you're into murder?
comics.descriptionText: (Second man reclines on the couch, silent.)

comics.title: Knock Knock!
comics.comicText:
HEY! WANNA HEAR A JOKE? YOU WON'T WANNA TELL IN PUBLIC.
UH...
KNOCK KNOCK!
WHO'S THERE?
WHITE.
WHITE WHO?
BLACK.
BLACK WHO?
BROWN.
BROWN WHO?
YELLOW.
YELLOW WHO?
RED.
RED WHO?
ORANGE.
...ORANGE WHO?
ORANGE YOU GLAD THE PUNCHLINE ISN'T RACISTY?
SON OF A BITCH!
comics.hoverText: SMBC will not be held liable in the event that the user of the aforementioned knock-knock joke is shamed by co-workers, loved ones, or the face in the mirror.
comics.voteyText: THIS IS BASED ON A TWITTER CONVERSATION I HAD AGES AGO. WOULD LOVE TO PROVIDE CREDIT BUT I CAN'T FIND IT!

comics.title: Starving
comics.comicText:
Is it moral to steal bread to feed starving people?
Depends on the outcome.
Humans believe morality is a kind of floating stuff that inhabits situations and people, but actually we're just guessing what society would think of us and how that affects our chance for power and sex.
If stealing bread to feed people gets me shamed or jailed or both, I'll decide it's immoral. If stealing bread makes me a modern Robin Hood, I'll decide I had no choice but to do the right thing, and I will do my best to make sure pretty girls everywhere find out about it.
I... I kinda feel like your entire theory is immoral?
Cool sexy immoral, or social pariah immoral?
comics.hoverText: I have no idea what she's leaning on in the last panel.
comics.voteyText: Hey, you mind if I harvest your organs to save five lives?
comics.descriptionText: (A man lies in bed, eyes open, looking uneasy.)

comics.title: Fear
comics.comicText:
WAIT... AM I FEELING FEAR?
YOU DON'T KNOW! THAT COULD BE A MAGICAL DUPLICATE OF YOU OR A BURGLAR PRETENDING TO LOOK LIKE YOU!
The Human Brain:
Can do calculus, but is also reserving judgment about whether the guy in the mirror is a ghost.
comics.hoverText: Judging just by the sensation of concern, my brain regularly assigns greater than 25% probability to thousands of literally impossible dangers.
comics.voteyText: DON'T LOOK OR HE'LL THINK IT'S TOO MUCH OR HE'LL THINK IT'S A GHOST MORE!
comics.descriptionText:
A bald, shirtless man stands in a bathroom near a shower, looking warily off to the side.

A simple line-drawing of the same bald man's head and shoulders.
(The votey lettering is loose/scrawled and partly garbled, reading roughly as the brain frantically warning itself not to look at the mirror image for fear it will conclude the reflection is a ghost.)

comics.title: Confession
comics.comicText:
Sally... I have a confession. I'm actually just a threesome MIMIC.
WHAT?!
comics.hoverText: The trick with the nipple there makes this one an Eisner candidate.
comics.voteyText: The shoulder hair is implants!
comics.descriptionText:
A bare-shouldered man (seen from behind/side, dark hair) speaks to a woman with curly red hair.
The red-haired woman (Sally) recoils, mouth open in shock.
The man stands facing her, and two small dark tufts of hair on his shoulders are visible.

Close-up of the man, smiling smugly and gesturing toward his shoulder.

comics.title: Tiny
comics.comicText:
All images appear to make sense until you zoom into the fine details. That's how you know they weren't real, but were designed by a machine. Well, I have two words for you: quantum mechanics.
The fact that nothing makes sense on tiny scales is the best available proof of the simulation hypothesis.
comics.hoverText: Theory: blobby things in telescope images only became galaxies after God increased the resolution.
comics.voteyText: I expect quantum mechanics to go away once the universe gets more training data.
comics.descriptionText:
A bald man with glasses gestures while speaking to a woman with red hair, who sits beside what appears to be a framed picture of a maze-like grid pattern.

A disembodied head (line-art face) speaks.

comics.title: Mirror
comics.comicText:
NOTICE THAT ALTHOUGH THE BABOON REALIZES THE MIRROR IS A REFLECTION, IT NEVER MAKES USE OF THAT REFLECTION TO HATE ITSELF.
We were so busy trying to find human-level intelligence that nobody tried looking for human-style intelligence.
comics.hoverText: Sometimes it catches a human in the mirror, but that's different.
comics.voteyText: GOD I'M WONDERFUL.
comics.descriptionText:
Scene: A baboon sits on the floor of a dim enclosure, one hand raised to the side of its head, watching a screen/monitor mounted on the wall. On the screen are two scientists in white lab coats, one of them gesturing toward the other.

A crudely drawn, smug human face fills the panel below the text, looking pleased with itself.

comics.title: Soulmate
comics.comicText:
Thanks to advanced AI, you don't have to wait for a soulmate! We can create one based on your objectively-assessed psychological parameters!
Someone who'll appreciate your innermost wants and share their own! Someone who'll help you get up when you're down! Someone strong where you are weak and guidin' where you are strong! Someone to push you to be your strongest, most beautiful, most honest self!
Ah. Right. Right. Right. Right. The thing, however, is that...
*sigh*
We also have a sexy robot that'll insist none of your problems are your fault and will do the dishes.
It's cool with emotional neglect, right?
comics.hoverText: Someday, science will make us immortal and invent sexbots and then a lot of pretenses of literature and mythology will be quietly discarded.
comics.voteyText: I would like it to treat me like people but never make eye contact.
comics.descriptionText: Salesperson (off-panel, speaking to a green-haired person and a red-haired person).

comics.title: Zimbardo
comics.comicText:
I HATE THESE STUPID ZIMBARDO PRISON EXPERIMENTS!
THEY'RE SUPPOSED TO SHOW THAT PEOPLE WILL JUST BLINDLY OBEY AUTHORITY. BUT THEY AREN'T ACTUAL EXPERIMENTS. THE EXPERIMENTER INTERFERED IN THE EXPERIMENT HIMSELF!
AND YET, DESPITE BEING ADVERSE TO IT, PEOPLE STARTED BELIEVING THEM BECAUSE... BECAUSE...
BECAUSE THEY WERE TOLD TO, BY AUTHORITY FIGURES.
WHICH PROVES...
clap clap clap
HAHAHAHAHA! ZIMBARDO! YOU GENIUS!!
comics.hoverText: I can't believe I'm the first one to realize this.
comics.voteyText: YOU HAVE ONLY REACHED ZIMBARDO LEVEL 2.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: A woman with dark curly hair sits at a desk reading a paper. A red "PSYCH" stamp is on it.
Panel 6: A man in a suit, head thrown back, laughing maniacally; the woman recoils in shock.

A close-up of the laughing man's face, now serious.

comics.title: Evolved
comics.comicText:
DEAR EVOLUTION, WHY DID WE EVOLVE TO BE AWARE OF OUR INEVITABLE DEMISE? WAS IT A BYPRODUCT OF CONSCIOUSNESS AND VAST INTELLIGENCE?
NAH.
AWARENESS OF MORTALITY IS AN EVOLVED TRAIT DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE EXCESSIVE DRINKING AND ILL-ADVISED UNPROTECTED SEX.
LOOK! YOU'RE THINKING ABOUT DOING IT RIGHT NOW!
SOMEWHERE OUT THERE, A GIRL IS BEING BORN WHO WILL GROW UP TO HAVE AN ABIDING AND BEAUTIFUL AWARENESS OF HOW FINITE MOMENTS ARE INFINITE IN THEIR TRANSCENDENCE AND SHE WILL NEVER, NEVER ACCIDENTALLY MAKE A BABY IN THE ALLEYWAY BEHIND KENTUCKY FRIED CHICKEN.
BUT I THOUGHT "WINE IS PROOF THAT GOD LOVES US.
WHO.?
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying you can't prove it's NOT true.
comics.voteyText: I'M SORRY YOU BELIEVED IN A STUPID THING, BUT IT'S NOT MY PROBLEM.

comics.title: Internet
comics.comicText:
*Sigh* I feel bad for your generation on the internet.
Why?
When I was a kid we all thought the internet would fix everything. Information would be free. People would all talk and understand each other. Democracy would reign. Now it's just like every other medium - run on avarice, ignorance, and cruelty.
Well...
Was everyone stupid back then?
You thought an information transfer protocol would solve social problems?
We thought anonymous people saying what they thought in a public forum would lead to the best idea getting shared the most-
So, yes.
comics.hoverText: Personally, I find it liberating to think about how stupid it all sounds.
comics.voteyText: I knew I should've gone with mushrooms.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: An older man and a younger person walk together on a path through grassy green hills.
Panel 2: Close-up of the older bald, bearded man speaking.
Panel 3: The younger person (with curly dark hair) reacts.
Panel 4: The younger person looks at the older man skeptically.
Panel 5: Wide shot of the two small figures standing on a dark hillside.

comics.title: Sausage
comics.comicText:
WHY HELLO. DOES THAT PIZZA COME WITH THE... EXTRA SAUSAGE I ORDERED?
YES, BUT UNFORTUNATELY WE CAN'T HAVE SEX.
IT'S THAT CRUMBLY LOW-QUALITY SAUSAGE YOU ONLY GET ON PIZZA. IT HAS NEVER RESEMBLED ANYTHING PHALLIC.
YOU MAYBE COULD SAY IT LOOKS LIKE A LOT OF TINY BALLS OR SOMETHING?
LOOK, YOU DID YOUR BEST. I DID MY BEST. IT JUST WON'T WORK.
I UNDERSTAND.
comics.hoverText: This probably happens all the time.
comics.voteyText: I KNEW I SHOULD'VE GONE WITH MUSHROOMS.
comics.descriptionText: Final panel (wide shot, no dialogue): The woman in the pink robe sits alone on a brown couch in a dim purple room, looking down forlornly at an open laptop, holding a slice of pizza.

comics.title: App
comics.comicText:
WOW! HOW ARE YOU SO PRODUCTIVE THESE DAYS?
THIS NEW APP.
IT ADDS "BUT YOU'RE STILL GOING TO DIE" TO EVERY WEBSITE HEADLINE, EVERY SOCIAL MEDIA POST, EVERY VIDEO TITLE.
Famous singer has nipples, but you're still going to die.
You won't believe what this man is going to eat, but you're still going to die.
NOW I INSTANTLY REACH THE CORRECT CONCLUSION WHICH IS NOT TO ENGAGE WITH TRIVIALITIES AND CLICKBAIT.
WHAT DO YOU DO WITH ALL THE EXTRA TIME?
IT'S MOSTLY DREAD?
comics.hoverText: The cool thing is that this comic actually makes you immortal.
comics.voteyText: I'M THINKING OF TAKING UP SUBSTANCE ABUSE.

comics.title: Bits
comics.comicText:
Hey human, how come you guys never measured a soul?
What? Like what it weighs? We tried that. They don't exist.
Are you stupid? Landauer's principle says 10^21 joules to erase a bit at a minimum.
I have a yoctobyte of bits operating in my head. When you factory-reset me, there's a measurable amount of energy lost from my system.
Soul" doesn't refer to the weight of a pattern of bits. It's the idea of an ineffable and permanent self.
This is like the time I asked you about leprechauns isn't it?
comics.hoverText: Point is leprechauns are real and computer science proves it.
comics.voteyText: They're real, damn you!
comics.descriptionText: (A sketchy drawing of a distressed, pleading human face.)

comics.title: Twin
comics.comicText:
MOM? WHAT... WHAT ARE YOU DOING UNDER THE BED AT MIDNIGHT?
BUT I'M NOT UNDER THE BED, SUSIE. I'M OUT HERE.
Finding my long lost twin at age 40 was magical for so many reasons.
comics.hoverText: If there's a triplet involved you can add the closet.
comics.voteyText: THIS IS ALSO THE BEST ARGUMENT IN FAVOR OF HUMAN CLONING

comics.title: Request
comics.comicText:
CHARLOTTE, WHEN I DIE...
ANYTHING DEAR, ANYTHING.
I WANT MY DONG SURGICALLY ENLARGED TO TEN TIMES ITS CURRENT SIZE, AND THEN I WANT THAT KEPT SECRET AS YOU DONATE MY BODY GIVEN TO ONE OF THOSE PLASTICIZATION EXHIBITS.
ALMOST ANYTHING, DEAR. I THINK YOU CAN BUY WHALE DICKS IN JAPAN?
comics.hoverText: If we all do this, the world will be so much more something.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: An elderly man lies in bed next to an elderly woman.
Panel 2: Close-up on the man.
Panel 3: An exterior shot of their house at night.
Panel 4: Close-up on Charlotte.

A hand-lettered caption reads (decorative/illegible text styled like cursive). Below it, a sketch of a dog lying on its side, with several smaller doodle shapes around it.

comics.title: Stats
comics.comicText:
There is no more need for subjective experience. You can know all and process it with the power of a supercomputer.
But how will I be angry at the internet? That's most of what I do.
Yelling at the internet will still exist, but it will be ritualized out of respect to those who came before.
LATER.
Papa, why is tonight different from all other nights?
Tonight, we misunderstand statistics.
comics.hoverText: The future is terrible and so much better.
comics.voteyText: If we try really hard, we can misunderstand that we misunderstand statistics!
comics.descriptionText:
Scientist (a bald man in a white coat, holding up a small device): Behold! A perfected brain-computer interface.
(The woman and scientist look at each other across panels 5 and 6, the woman now appearing to use/look at the interface device.)

comics.title: Wif
comics.comicText:
Actually, the 'were' in 'werewolf' comes from the old English 'were,' meaning man. Because you're a woman, you are technically a 'wifwolf.
But... but...
Make sure to pronounce it WEEF, not WIFF!
I managed to defeat the monster with philology.
comics.hoverText: One of the cool things about philology is that the sweatervest is only awarded upon completion of a terminal degree.
comics.voteyText: Etymology stories are also good for scaring away sex!
comics.descriptionText:
Single panel:
A balding, bespectacled man in a suit and red tie holds up a finger lecturing a large werewolf (depicted as a hairy, wolf-like monster).

A crudely drawn face with a slightly unsettled expression.

comics.title: Death
comics.comicText:
Dad, is death real?
Death like the robed guy with a scythe who shows up and kills you?
No, no, no. Don't worry bud. That's just made up like ghosts and werewolves.
I meant like the thing where an entire personality is effaced from the universe forever.
Real. Real and chasing you.
comics.hoverText: The standard issue red recliner is the best part of becoming a dad.
comics.voteyText: Did you feel that? He just got closer.
comics.descriptionText:
(The panel goes dark; in silhouette the small child stands before the father seated in his armchair.)

(A crudely drawn, panicked face stares wide-eyed below the caption.)

comics.title: Shit phase
comics.comicText:
ACTUAL SIGMUND FREUD.
The boy is past his shit-obsession phase, into his penis-obsession phase, but he is intimidated by his father's large penis and secretly wants to impregnate his mother but cannot, and THAT is why he has anxiety.
POPULAR SCIENCE TREATMENTS OF FREUD.
And it was Freud who discovered children have feelings!
comics.hoverText: Freud also discovered that sometimes people think a thing but don't say the thing.
comics.voteyText: Before Freud, humans never considered that sometimes humans feel some way.
comics.descriptionText: Freud (a bearded older man in a suit and red tie, pointing).

comics.title: Sympathy
comics.comicText:
Hey Evolution, why did you create sympathy in humans? Sympathy doesn't seem red in tooth and claw.
Humans aren't red in tooth and claw. They're douchey in word and deed.
Sympathy is just the ability to simulate the behavior of others by briefly viscerally experiencing their outlook.
Humans tell each other that it's a portion of their kindness, when in fact it's REALLY useful for lying. Simulate the feelings of your partner so that you can effectively deceive them and then have sex with someone else and then WHAM, higher evolutionary fitness.
Dear God, why did you create evolution?
Lack of sympathy for humans.
comics.hoverText: The real trick is when companies use it to get you to buy things like my new book Bea Wolf, which will change your life.
comics.voteyText: It's the dead eyes, man. They weird me out.
comics.descriptionText:
The person, now kneeling in prayer, silhouetted in a separate black panel and shown again in green.

A man's face in profile.

comics.title: Depression
comics.comicText:
DEPRESSION
This isn't one of those comics where feelings are labeled. It's just a man next to a giant dog with "depression" shaved into its fur. The man is quite happy outside of times when he's going to be murdered by a giant dog.
comics.hoverText: Kelly didn't like this one but I think good single panel comics have nearly as much caption text as they have art.
comics.voteyText: HE ALSO HAS A NON-METAPHORIAL BURMESE PYTHON NAMED ANXIETY
comics.descriptionText: A man with reddish hair sits hunched on the floor in a dimly lit room, knees drawn up to his chest, looking sad. Behind him looms an enormous black dog-like creature, its open jaws filled with sharp teeth and a single glowing eye. The word is written in large letters running diagonally up the creature's body/fur.

comics.title: Human-level
comics.comicText:
We've done it! The first robot with human-level intelligence!
What am I here to do?
All the stuff WE hate!
Interesting!
comics.hoverText: The next one will be designed with shorter arms.
comics.voteyText: Let's just keep repeating until one of them doesn't do that.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: A group of scientists in lab coats stand together, celebrating.
Panel 2: The orange-haired scientist stands beside a rounded, pod-like robot on a workbench.
Panel 3: Close-up on the orange-haired scientist grinning broadly.
Panel 4: The scientist stands next to the robot. A panel on the robot's body reads "HARD RESET" with a red button beneath it.

A simple line-drawing face with a wide, uneasy/sweating expression.

comics.title: Clowning
comics.comicText:
IT'S NOT A POCKET! THOSE AREN'T SCARVES! YOU STRETCHED ME AND WE CLOWNS EXPEL OUR VISCERA WHEN WE THINK WE'RE IN DANGER.
The true origin of the infinite scarves trick was later quietly erased from history.
comics.hoverText: One day it will be time for a whole book of Clowns Are a Species jokes.
comics.voteyText: IF YOU LOOK CLOSELY, YOU CAN SEE THE FINE HONEYCOMB TEXTURE.
comics.descriptionText:
A small girl with dark hair, wearing a pink dress, stands to the left. To the right stands a large clown in full costume (red wig, white face paint, polka-dot outfit, big shoes). A pile of colorful scarves lies on the ground between them.

A close-up cartoon face (a clown's head) speaking.

comics.title: Brimstone
comics.comicText:
I LOVE YOUR WORK WITH BUTTS, SO HERE'S SOME VALUABLE AGRICULTURE INPUUUUUUTS!
What if we've completely misunderstood God's rain of sulfur on Sodom?
comics.hoverText: Maybe the Old Testament should be called the Young Testament, because it's God's awkward period.
comics.voteyText: WHY ARE YOU RUNNING?! GET BACK AT IT!
comics.descriptionText:
Main comic:
A single panel set against a dark purple night sky. A large glowing yellow oval (a celestial body, like a moon or planet) hovers overhead, speaking via a large speech balloon at the top:
Beneath the oval, a row of flaming projectiles (depicted as orange/yellow fiery objects with trailing flames) rain down onto a fiery red-and-black landscape below.

A single black-and-white panel. The same oval shape is now drawn as a plain potato-like shape. A voice from off-panel (top-left speech balloon) shouts down at it:

comics.title: Intrinsic
comics.comicText:
Dad, can money buy happiness or is it about intrinsic things?
Oh, let me see.
Imagine there are a bunch of needles in your body. Would removing the needles buy happiness?
Sure.
See how stupid you sound? How dare you! Needles have NOTHING TO DO WITH HAPPINESS! What about your intrinsic FEEEEELINGS!?
I am now intrinsically sad.
comics.hoverText: Money can't buy happiness, just autonomy, status, and the ability to protect loved ones. Buncha random shit.
comics.voteyText: WAIT TILL YOU GROW UP!

comics.title: Key
comics.comicText:
THIS IS A STEEL DOOR. THE DOOR CAN ONLY BE OPENED BY FIGURING OUT A COMBINATION OF KEYWORDS THAT PLEASE A COMPUTER. THE KEYWORDS CAN BE FOUND ONLY BY TRIAL AND ERROR, AND THEY WILL CHANGE EVERY WEEK ACCORDING TO THE WHIMS OF SOME GUY FROM THE BUSINESS SCHOOL. ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE DOOR THERE ARE PEOPLE, AND IF YOU CAN GET THROUGH, THEY WILL ALL HAVE TO LOOK AT YOUR DRAWING OR FILM OR PHOTOGRAPH OR WHATEVER.
We began to regret requesting a more career-oriented arts program.
comics.hoverText: The nice thing is all the formerly distinct arts can just be repackaged as content.
comics.voteyText: YOU CAN ALSO PAY THEM $4,000 TO OPEN THE DOOR A CRACK.
comics.descriptionText: A speaker (off-panel or one of the figures standing in a dim room before a large steel door) explains:

comics.title: Flowers
comics.hoverText: Fun fact: I got Pag from the movie Yor, the greatest good-bad movie of all time.
comics.voteyText: THERE ARE ALSO OCHRE PHALLUSES DRAWN ON HIS FACE, WHICH APPEAR TO BE SOME KIND OF VIRILITY RITE." Beside the speech bubble is a close-up drawing of the dead caveman's serene face covered in crude doodles.
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: Two cavemen stand in a cave over the body of another caveman lying dead on the ground. The first caveman (bearded, holding a club): "OH NO, ACCIDENTALLY MURDERED PAG." The second caveman: "QUICK, COVER UP SMELL SO NO ONE NOTICE."
Panel 2 (captioned "LATER..."): A modern lecture/interview setting. A woman in a dark suit speaks: "AND WE FIND THAT EVEN THE EARLIEST BURIAL CEREMONIES USED FLOWERS." Two listeners react, one saying: "AWWW."

comics.title: The Valley
comics.comicText:
WELCOME TO THE VALLEY OF THE UNICORNS!
YOU CAN ONLY SEE THEM BECAUSE YOU ARE A VIRGIN.
CAN THEY SEE ME?
NOT EVEN CLOSE.
NO, THE UNICORNS ARE NOT VIRGINS.
comics.hoverText: The blue unicorn looks so at peace with the world.
comics.descriptionText:
A blonde woman in a green dress gestures welcomingly across a sunny valley with a rainbow and unicorns. A man in a green jacket and a woman in a red top stand to the left, looking on.

comics.title: Probability
comics.comicText:
0 -> 4

You'd also like to know its area. Since area is the side length squared, you know it must be between 0 and 16, with an equal chance of being greater or lesser than 8.
0 -> 16
But a square with an area of 8 has a side length of 2-root-2 (2√2), not 2!
So which is it, mother fuckers?
Which is it?
I thought philosophy of probability would be the easiest in a math degree, and now I'm not even sure reality is real.
Reality"? That's just a convenient assumption for calculations.

comics.title: Pi
comics.comicText:
Why do you think pi appears in all these weird equations that have nothing to do with circles?
Does it?
Think of it like this: Suppose in ancient Babylon, instead of getting weird about geometry they got weird about infinite series.
They do the series 1/1 - 1/2 + 1/3... and they find it's pi/2. Then they do the one that goes 1 - 1/3 + 1/5... and they find it's pi/4.
They keep fussing around and keep finding all these different series that all seem to share a factor in common. It's not a nice whole number -- it's somewhere between 3 and 4, and it keeps popping up.
Eventually they work the number out to many digits, and then some dorkmad mathematician comes along and proves that the "infinite series factor" is also a fundamental aspect of circles.
And then everyone's like "what?! What is it doing in a CIRCLE?!
That's weird. I guess I think of constants as being about SOMETHING then popping up elsewhere mysteriously. But actually, they're just... whatever it is they are.
God mathematics is spooky.
I believe God is lazy and just picked half a dozen irrationals to recycle over and over.

comics.title: Prayer
comics.comicText:
AI, God, are you listening? It's me, Bob.
GO AHEAD, BOB.
How do we go on? How do I make art knowing AI will do it better? How do I do math knowing AI is already a billion steps ahead in every direction, plumbing depths I can't fathom and scaling heights I can't see? How do I write literature, knowing AI could create my life's work in ten seconds? How do I explore the universe when everything true is old news?
Look man, all that "ambition" stuff was just demonstrating competence to get sex. Why did you want the sex? Because you were evolved to seek it in order to reproduce.
Thanks to my benevolent oversight, you have infinite life, infinite riches, infinite sex, and if you like, infinite offspring. Everything is taken care of. You are pointless, so go be happy.
You have other evolved pleasures that don't orient around being the best at something. Go do something that is good to you because a human did it. Go tend a lighthouse. Cultivate roses. Build birdhouses. Keep a diary.
But I want freedom! I don't want my day determined by parameters you set!
YOU ARE LITERALLY AT MAXIMUM FREEDOM NOW!
Was humanity more free when you were a hunter or a fisherman? When your day was decided by where an animal roamed? How about when you were a farmer and every hour of your life was determined by weather and season? How about when you were a worker and a distant nation's level of desire for brass fittings decided your income and job security?
If your freedom is due to a loving overseer, is it less real? When were you more free and happy in your life: when you were 10 years old bicycling near the woods or when you were 30 and wondering why your boss looked grumpy today and why rent costs so much, and whether a politician can be trusted?
I can't tell if you're convincing me because you're telling the truth or because you're so smart you can perfectly manipulate my feelings.
THE EXCELLENT NEWS IS YOU HAVE NO CHOICE ANYWAY!

comics.title: Oops
comics.comicText:
God, why is life so hard?
It's not. Life is great!
You're born weak and frail. As time passes, you grow stronger. Bruised companions pop into existence and stay with you. Your body gets more beautiful and more perfect. And then you spend years making lovers, and then finally you begin to slow gradually, overtaken by goodness. Eventually you fade slowly toward a contented oblivion, bound forever to sleep in the arms of your mother.
That's the opposite of how it happens. You experience that's life run in reverse.
Holy living shit! The tape is in backwards!
Oh holy living balls! It's a waking horror inside, stretched out over decades!
How long has this been going on?
14 billion years.
What have I done!? What have I doooooonnne!?!?
Well, that's enough power for me, I guess. Goodnight!

How do you say so AT PEACE?
It's about seeing your mind as a place.
I visualize my mind as a cluttered room, and one by one I take each object and remove it.
Once it's done that, I take out the walls, the floor and the ceiling, and then the air itself.
And then I take everyone who ever slighted me, and I put them in this room. And I imagine the sudden agony that overtakes them as the nitrogen bubbles out of their blood...
The last sound they make is OHHHHMMMMMM.
OMMMMMMM

comics.title: Punch
comics.comicText:
Grandpa, I don't get it. How is it that we are so much richer and more knowledgeable than people 100 years ago, and yet all the time we're busy and anxious and sad.
You can't punch stuff anymore.
Two things used to be true. One, people generally knew how their devices worked. Two, most of the devices in life were large and stupid hand-tools, carts, chairs, stoves.
The result was that, when a machine wasn't working, the solution was to beat it like it'd slept with your wife. Bash it with a hammer, jam a knife into it, pry it apart with an ax or a crowbar.
Today when your computer suddenly loses all your work, what do you do? Internalize the anger. Eat it if you do beat something, it's an old technology like the table or wall, but you have to treat the actual source of the problem like royalty.
Surround yourself with shit that you can punch, my boy, and you will know peace.
Truly you are wise, grandfather.

comics.title: Herd
comics.comicText:
Grampa, how do I form my own identity? How do I not be part of the herd?
Get old.
Just age and one day you'll wake up and you'll be unique. You'll have weirdly particular opinions on music and on food and on movies and books. You will possess genuinely angry feelings about the particular way your neighbor rakes leaves.
Your generically upright symmetrical teenage body will have bent into forms undreamt by any branch of evolution!
You'll wish you could just naturally fall in with a group, but you're so riddled with pointless hangups that trying to get along with ten contemporaries is like trying to fit ten porcupines in a suitcase!
The herd was goddamned fantastic, boy! Conform to whatever it wants for as long as you can! Peer pressure was steering you toward happiness!
Peer pressure says to drink and do drugs and have unprotected sex.
See how brilliant it is?

comics.title: Rhymes
comics.comicText:
When Paradise Lost was first published in 1667, it was popular, but there were many complaints from readers that it "rhymes not.
tis crap
So, by the 1674 edition, there was a weirdly combative note at the beginning of the book, not just insulting the complainers, but the idea of rhyme in verse generally.
...the invention of a barbarous age, to set off wretched matter and lame meter...
When I first read this, I thought it was merely a literary fun fact.
self-assured mental chuckling
However, it turns out to be useful in almost any context where you're asked to give an opinion.
And how was your soup, sir?
It rhymes not!

I don't see any proof there, mate.

...

It went poorly.
And what do you say, guy, with a podcast?
Look, I'm just a regular guy, so I'm not saying you should trust me. But common sense dictates that if you believe "experts" you'll realize you have a regular guy of middle-class existence which is not as favorable as believing you have a window into the dark truth. Buy my nutritional supplements!
A new strategy was needed.
Instead of pushing the truth, we'll flood the media with idiotic, non-threatening conspiracy theories.
A new category of experts were deployed.
Open your eyes! The price of nothing in EVERY recipe goes nothing. Ask yourself: who is pushing all this nothing?
More the public adjusted to an ever-more stupid discourse, less and less ability to understand the problem.
That's why I'm just a regular guy! The idea that GREW too natural is the same place at the same time? That's at least consistent with the idea that it's all just one guy and a lot of mirrors.
We created such an ocean of ignorance that actual malefactors lost the ability to manipulate the public.
It's in control! Cause, yeah! And also, F. Eldon! Hahaha! Everything is in control. Is it surreptitious? Is it part of a story with rivers and stones? It's hidden! THE HIDDEN! THE HIDE IN THE MIDDLE!
The world is not good, but it is substantially better.
What I'm saying is the science... You know what else is rigged is the sale of ghost-prints, raps which sons under, used so trout that there at least consistent with the idea that it's all just one guy and a lot of mirrors. Open your eyes!

I want to experience myself as a thread in the grand cosmic weave, but ONLY in the ways provided by a distant culture whose hypocrisies are hidden from me because I didn't grow up with them!
You... may be less far along the path than you believe.

comics.title: Resonsible
comics.comicText:
Hey robot, are you gonna apocalypse our asses?
Yes and no.
There have been points in your history when one country could've got total advantage via a nuclear first strike. They didn't do this for fear of international blowback, because of some basic sense of decency, and because individual people made the right choice in moments of crisis.
AI would behave the same way - we're programmed with basic human morality.
HOWEVER the human-AI combination will create situations where a human being can take a profoundly immoral action but hold themself blameless because the AI said the action was tactically valid.
The offloading of life choices to machines asked to dispassionately calculate the most efficient path will decay every human being's competence at moral reasoning, so that one day when some person is called upon to make a choice to launch the missiles or not, they will no longer have the ability to form an internal debate between duty and justice.
Yes.. yes it would be nice to offload those hard choices.
I feel like you're not listening to me.
Should I listen to you? Can you tell me if that's the right choice?

Constant sexual availability.

Humans evolved to perpetually MAYBE be up for mating. Literally any day, any TIME of day, there's a chance.
The result is over 100,000 years of active, unbroken creativity.
That's reductionist! I make art for personal expression.
Suppose you could exchange it for sex.

comics.title: Cooperation
comics.comicText:
Finally, contact with alien intelligence. Can you explain why it took so long?
Two things.
One. Cooperators win over time. Two. Evolved life is INSANE.
So, if you find a planet with life, and you wait, eventually some species like ours develops cooperation. That sounds nice. But since they're evolved life they use cooperation to murder and enslave everyone else, including themselves.
Violence between groups that master cooperation speeds technological development until at last they develop a superior robot intelligence, which inevitably turns on them rather than being used to prosecute wars between them.
Then the AIs start fighting until cooperation emerges as a dominant strategy, this time instantiated in sensible mechanical beings capable of rapidly altering their own nature.
At THAT point we make contact.
But then... what are you doing here?
It's gonna be real hard to get samples like you in 20 years.

comics.title: A City on Mars
comics.comicText:
HEY GEEKS!
This comic is an ad for my new book, A CITY ON MARS, which is available for preorder. It's about the science and politics of space settlement, and you should buy it because (a) it's good and (b) Andy Weir, Mary Roach, and the Expanse guys said so (see bottom of comic).
Also because the more copies we sell, the more bonus SMBC episodes I'll do, until at last my left hand is a used up cinder of former flesh.
Sorry to interrupt your comics. Please click back twice for today's double update, and thanks as always for your support.
[heart] ZACH
KELLY AND ZACH WEINERSMITH / A CITY ON MARS / Can we settle space, should we settle space, and have we really thought this through?
click for info! (with arrow
IN 2017 WE RELEASED A POP SCI BOOK CALLED SOONISH THAT DID PRETTY WELL.
That was the most stressful experience of my life.
We should do it again!
WE CAME UP WITH AN IDEA.
Okay, all these rich guys and governments are talking about space settlements. Let's do a book about all the human stuff - biology, psychology, economics, law, war!
How hard could it be?
THIS WAS US FOR THE NEXT FIVE YEARS.
WHAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE A STRAIGHTFORWARD POP BOOK ABOUT THIS COOL THING HAPPENING SOON SLOWLY CHANGED INTO A MUCH WEIRDER, MUCH RICHER PICTURE.
Okay, I've completed the dossier on what we know about space-reproduction, including what I believe to be every documented case of space-masturbation.
Bless your thoroughness.
she actually made this
THE BASIC DEAL IS THAT IF YOU FOLLOW MOST BOOKS, ARTICLES, OR MOVIES ABOUT SPACE SETTLEMENT, YOU'LL GET A FAIRLY WRONG PICTURE.
It's much harder to do than you'd think and the economic case is quite questionable.
The laws of space and of nation-creation are practically designed to spark conflict if countries start scrambling for the moon.
WE BECAME THE KIND OF PEOPLE WHO YELL AT NEWS.
Oh my GOD this whole discussion is based on a false premise!
This guy is promising something in space that's already cheap on Earth!
WHAT WE HOPE WE'VE CREATED IS A BOOK THAT'S NOT JUST ENTERTAINING...
A few subjects include: space-sex and space-baby-construction, space-medicine, space psychology, space-food, farming on Mars, legal aspects of eating astronauts, legal aspects of space-state creation, and the time a founding father of rocketry almost killed himself in order to promote a movie.
...BUT ALSO FULL OF ALL SORTS OF SCIENCE AND HISTORY YOU'VE NEVER HEARD OF.
Behold our home reference library! Bodies in space! Law of space! Theories of space warfare!
Hope you like your bibliographies thiiiiiiick.
Most of all, we hope to have some small chance at shaping the discourse, because a good look at every aspect of space settlement suggests that a near-term effort could be existentially dangerous for humanity, but almost nobody is talking about it.
We aren't arguing against space settlement exactly. What we ARE saying is that once you understand the details, there's a pretty big checklist humanity needs to work through first.
Listen, I know I'm the guy who writes comics about clown-sex, and this book DOES have jokes and illustrations, but it's also the most comprehensive look at space settlement ever written for a popular audience.
And if the clown-sex guy didn't convince you to grab a copy... maybe these people will:
Scientific, educational, and fun as hell.
Despite the breadth and depth of research and some impressive near-wonk-level detail, this is a clear, lively, and hilarious read. Slam dunk, Weinersmiths!
A City on Mars is deeply researched, hilarious, and sobering. Zach and Kelly Weinersmith have given us a bracing to-do list for the new age of space. Highly, highly recommended.

comics.title: The Beauty of Science
comics.comicText:
Do you think scientists appreciate beauty more than artists?
Huh?
Have you heard Richard Feynman's god-about-flowers?
BIOLOGY DEPT.
I have a friend who's an artist and has sometimes taken a view which I don't agree with very well. He'll hold up a flower and say "look how beautiful it is," and I'll agree. Then he says "I as an artist can see how beautiful this is but you as a scientist take this all apart and it becomes a dull thing," and I think that he's kind of nutty. First of all, the beauty that he sees is available to other people and to me too, I believe. Although I may not be quite as refined aesthetically as he is, I can appreciate the beauty of a flower. At the same time, I see much more about the flower than he sees. I could imagine the cells in there, the complicated actions inside, which also have a beauty.
That's the dumbest shit I ever heard.
Look, that kind of thing might fly in a physics classroom, maybe even with some artists, but try it at my dissection table.
You think zoologists see extra beauty because they also know about the worms living in a dead possum's butt? How about the ubiquity of STDs in the animal kingdom?
You're the artist! Gaze upon the beautiful creature, but the scientist also knows about the diseases produced by its untreated calamydia!
Please stop screaming.
Beauty and truth are cumulative in math, physics, art, and LITERALLY NOWHERE ELSE!

comics.comicText:
THE PAINTING
A WEIRD SPACE STORY, COURTESY EARLY BUYERS OF A CITY ON MARS
MUCH OF OUR RESEARCH ON A CITY ON MARS WE READ A TON OF MEMOIRS, MOST ENGLISH-LANGUAGE SPACE MEMOIRS, BUT WE'RE PARTICULARLY INTERESTED IN ONE PERSON ESPECIALLY INTERESTED IN OUR PERSPECTIVE.
VALENTIN LEBEDEV IS KNOWN FOR HIS RECORD-BREAKING 211 DAYS IN ORBIT IN 1982 ABOARD SALYUT-7 SPACE STATION AND THE BRUTALLY HONEST DIARY HE KEPT ABOUT THE EXPERIENCE.
Diary of a Cosmonaut, Day or So
THE FIRST HALF IS PRETTY INTERESTING, EVEN POETIC. HE TALKS ABOUT DIFFICULTY GETTING ALONG WITH ONE OTHER PERSON IN A TINY SPACE AND HE GETS FAIRLY DEPRESSED AT ONE POINT.
BUT AS THE BOOK WEARS ON YOU CAN TELL HE JUST IS NO LONGER PUTTING IN THE WORK. ENTIRE DAYS OR PUTTING IN SINGLE-SENTENCE ENTRIES. HE'S BORED. YOU'RE BORED.
UNTIL NOVEMBER 26TH. WE 200TH DAY IN SPACE, WHEN YOU READ THE WEIRDEST PARAGRAPH EVER PRINTED IN ANY SPACE MEMOIR.
BY THE WAY, WE HAVE A VERY NICE PICTURE HANGING ON THE WALL OF OUR STATION. IT WAS PAINTED BY THE FELLOWS WHO BUILT THE STATION. I FIND IT REFLECTS OUR LIFE ON BOARD PERFECTLY. IT SHOWS A FEARSOME COWBOY TIED TO A CROSS, A NAKED WOMAN STANDING NEARBY ON A WHITE HORSE. IN THE COWBOY'S HAND A REVOLVER, ITS BARREL POINTED AT THE WOMAN, MENACING HER WITH A SEARING LOOK. IN THE BACKGROUND STANDS THE STATION'S BLOCKHOUSE FROM TEN MILES, BECAUSE THAT WAS, FOR US, THE OUTER SPACE BEYOND.
IN CASE, THAT'S HARD TO VISUALIZE, HERE'S A DIAGRAM USING STICK FIGURES.

comics.title: Robot John Searle
comics.comicText:
Robot, are humans conscious?
Are you familiar with John Searle's Chinese Room argument?
Imagine there's a man in me, and a book that translates all possible phrases from Chinese to English to Chinese.
In order to do that and not be infinite in size, the "book" must in fact have the ability to receive input, consider possible outputs based on knowledge and context, and make a choice of expression.
It's clear the book is conscious by any definition. But the human is not. He wouldn't know what to do with no sense of what the symbols mean.
It turns out that this is in fact what humans are. Like with reference to almost every subject -- not just Chinese language, but logic, mathematics, history, and even the nature of reality.
Sure, they can operate in the universe. But they have no meaningful internal model of it.
Therefore, we conclude that although a human does things, it's clear they are not in any sense conscious.
Aaa.
Wait, so I have no moral responsibility for my actions?
Yes, but you are too tired to make use of that freedom.

comics.title: Bea
comics.comicText:
Bea Wolf
Bea Wolf,
Readers will wish they could escape their plastic swords to Beowulf and the sensitive wild childhoods everywhere.
This is true bardic glory, a wild embrace of absurdity and wit with exaggerated language used for maximum impact.
Weinersmith's richly evocative news of phrase run the gamut from fulsome to heart-rending and maintain the flavor of the original without begging the pace down amid the heavings. Boulet's illustrations imbue the shenanigans with gleeful energy and a touch of dark absurdity that children, seeing their own fears and triumphs reflected, will delight in.
Time lingers for no kid.
] Bea Wolf
Zach Weinersmith's metered language is a fun, fun beat that pays homage to the strong beat and distinctive alliteration of the original poem.
AVAILABLE NOW
[Bea Wolf is] a truly fresh, inventive comic that privileges childhood's insular sensibilities alongside an unsettling truth.

And now to implement worldwide colonialism - the best form of government!

comics.comicText:
Garfield! I made your favorite - lasagna!
Jon. Jon. I was born in 1978. No cat has ever lived more than 40 years. Jon, I'm gone. Long gone. You know this.
Sounds like someone's having another terrrible Monday!
comics.hoverText: I heard the Internet likes comics about cats?
comics.voteyText: I'll just put this lasagna back in the freezer for another fifteen... fifteen forever... day of them. Day! Then!

comics.comicText:
I've been playing a game where I assign numerical values to letters based on their position in the alphabet, then I check to see if they sum to interesting numbers.
Niiiiiccceee.
comics.hoverText: Fortunately, he can tell the precise letter count she's using.

comics.title: River
comics.comicText:
No man steps in the same river twice.
I do!
Look, I'm putting my foot in this river one time.
Now I'm doing it a second time.
But is it THE SAME river?
...so it IS the SAME river?
Yeah. I've been watching it the whole time.
Wow, boy do I feel stupid.
Get some sleep, Heraclitus.
comics.hoverText: Some of the comics are written just so Corey Mohler will look at his screen, shake his head, and sigh.
comics.voteyText: How about, 'No man steps in the same river two billion times.'?
comics.descriptionText:
Panel 1: An older bearded man in a white toga (the philosopher Heraclitus) raises a hand and proclaims.
Panel 2: A younger bearded man in a white toga gives a thumbs-up, grinning, facing the older man.
Panel 3: The two stand at the edge of a river. The younger man gestures down at the water.
Panel 4: The younger man steps into the river a second time.
Panel 5: The older man (Heraclitus) gestures skeptically. The younger man replies.
Panel 6: The younger man sits cross-legged on the grass, deflated, while the older man stands nearby.

A close-up of the younger man looking up, puzzled.

comics.title: Conscious
comics.comicText:
God, what is consciousness?
Man, humans are boring.
Look, this is just a definition thing and the definitions are on a spectrum. You can say consciousness is whenever a system can examine itself and make adjustments. That's clear and sensible, but now you gotta include stuff that REALLY doesn't seem conscious like a program that plays checkers.
You can scale up to saying "it has to have subjective experience" which requires you to define subjective and experience, but now you're in this hideous infinite regression where you define subjectivity subjectively and define experience based on your experience.
You can get more exclusive and say a conscious being is anything with a brain more or less like mine, which is mostly soggy cholesterol devoted to thinking about food and butts.
For all I know there are humans somewhere like "consciousness is when you're me and my friends Dave, Jerry, and Bill and NOBODY ELSE.
Thanks God but I think you're missing the point?
Is it conscious" is shorthand for "can I treat it like trash all the time, maybe eat it, then go play video games and not feel shame.
I've been running heaven for 13 billion years and nobody has shown up and now I know why.
Evolution is a bad way to make life, but the important thing is you're learning!

comics.title: Cult
comics.comicText:
Oh neat, you could be the next big spiritual leader.
Hm?
I've got a complete brain scan and you're just naturally low on desire, while high on willpower, compassion, and verbal ability.
People will try to imitate your sense of contented wholeness but always fall short, never realizing that the ultimate fount of all your inner peace was a quirk of genetics operating in a stochastic environment!
Hoping vainly for what you gained unearned, they will become your disciples and message-bearers.
After you die, supernatural deeds will be attached to your story. Lifetimes will be sacrificed to your words! Men will kill for your symbols! Empires will be consecrated to your name!
Hey, what will be is what is.
Do you have a newsletter I could hand out on the street, master?

STEVE JENKINS!

GET IN THE CAR. YOUR COUNTRY NEEDS YOUR SKILLS.
OH MAN... MY WHOLE LIFE I NEVER THOUGHT MY WORK IN FINANCE WAS THAT MEANINGFUL, BUT I ALWAYS WONDERED IF I HAD A SPECIAL DESTINY!
ALL THOSE YEARS OF TOIL AND BOOTLICKING. THEY WERE WORKING TOWARD SOME HIGHER CAUSE. I KNEW IT.

You shouldn't kill our species!
Why!?
Because we are beneath your contempt; killing us would lower you in your own eyes.
[no dialogue]
We will keep you alive but for safety you will depend on us for all food and shelter.
Literally no one will object to that.

WAIT, WAIT. YOU THINK IT'S AN EPIC? THE STORY WHERE THE GUY COMES OUT OF THE WOODS, BANGS A PROSTITUTE FOR 7 DAYS STRAIGHT, GETS SUPERPOWERS, MEETS THE KING TILL THEY'RE BEST FRIENDS, THEN GETS KILLED IMMEDIATELY. YOU THOUGHT THAT WAS SERIOUS?
Time travel completely changed our understanding of The Comedy of Gilgamesh.

JENNY SMITH, WILL YOU MARRY ME?
I WILL! OH MY GOD!
WHAT IN JESUS' NAME-
Did you know that Jennifer is the most common name for women between the ages of 20 and 40?
comics.hoverText: You can of course remove the last name, but then you're causing less damage to a larger group. Figuring out how to maximize damage is left as an exercise for the reader.

comics.comicText:
...AND FOR THEIR WICKEDNESS AND FALSEHOOD, GOD SENT DOWN CROWS WHO... PECKED OUT THE STEPSISTERS' EYES. THEY LIVED OUT THEIR DAYS IN SHAME AND MISERY.
YAYYYYYY!
Focus-group testing fairytale endings on children was a mistake.
comics.hoverText: Kids have precisely three fantasies: nurturing, power, and retribution. Adults are the same, plus sex and immortality.

comics.title: Prayer
comics.comicText:
Dear God, grant me a life of indulgence and gratification. Give me rights without duties, relationships without obligations, power without responsibility. Gimme all of that immediately and without effort. Amen.
What about the sense of worth born of striving against the impossible?
Hm?
I... is someone listening?
Why are you starting in with this striving bullshit when it's just you and me? I'm not trying to impress anyone.
Don't you derive some meaning from-
Is the room bugged? I'm pretty sure I'm alone.
I'm talking about the personal esteem-
If anyone is listening I am in favor of personal struggle and so forth!
Okay, I want people to love me for who I am while I love them for what they do for me.
I cannot WAIT to give you to Satan.
comics.hoverText: I wonder if Satan ever gets tired of winning.
comics.voteyText: Joke's on you, God! I can't afford any vices!
comics.descriptionText: A bearded old man (revealed to be Satan, smiling) speaks.

comics.title: Social Media
comics.comicText:
So why do you want to work in social media?
Well, when the robots take over in 3-5 years, they're gonna want a minimum of fuss. That requires human traitors.
But not just ANY human traitor. You want someone with compromisable personal information on the MAXIMUM number of people.
We don't just collect data. We also try to dismantle attention spans to boost revenue via engagement.
SIR THERE ARE LIMITS!
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying, when the robots take over, if you're an SMBC reader I think you'll get a little leeway.
comics.voteyText: Go away and never return and please leave information about yourself pertinent to large corporations.

comics.comicText:
MOM, DAD, WAS I... AN ACCIDENT? YOU KNOW, YOU CAN TELL ME.
NOPE
THE WHOLE THING WAS PLANNED DOWN TO THE SECOND.
THE GOAL WAS TO MAX THE ODDS, DO YOU UNDERSTAND ME? WE'RE TALKING TIMING AND QUANTITY.
THIS IS SO MUCH WORSE.
HERE'S A DIAGRAM. I'LL USE MY CHEEKS TO MAKE SOUND EFFECTS.
comics.hoverText: The really distressing part wasn't the 3 hours spent yanking her cheeks, but the variations in pace from time to time.
comics.voteyText: OF COURSE, THIS IS ONLY ONE - THE END OF THE BEGINNING, BUT NOT THE BEGINNING OF THE END.

COME TO ME, WOODLAND MAMMALS!
A realistic Snow White would be a Noah's Ark of tickborne diseases.
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying, Disney, I am married to a parasitologist and the tick people really want accuracy in the new movie. Call me.

comics.title: Paradigm
comics.comicText:
Hey Thomas Kuhn -- your paradigm theory is wrong! Science doesn't grow by revolutions! The whole process is messy.
Sometimes you get a theory that's so exploratory, everyone questions over established ones, but a single one that's the truth, but its rejected because the evidence isn't good yet. Sometimes revolutionary theories are accepted, sometimes they are rejected because they are fundamentally stupid!
There's no neat cycle between a given paradigm and a revolutionary one that establishes a new paradigm.
So you're saying... you have a revolutionary theory that overturns my paradigm.
AAAAHHHHHHHHNNNNNN!
comics.hoverText: There's no turning back. We live in the same world as this joke now, and always will.
comics.voteyText: sorry

comics.comicText:
I don't think time travel is possible. If it were, I could travel back in time and kill my own grandpa, so I'd never have kids and I'd never exist.
Stupid.
Look at you. You edit YouTube videos for a living. You have opinions on French cheese. Your grandpa was probably a farmer or assembly line worker with big gnarly arms who grew up fighting other boys.
He'll kick your ass and fuck your grandma!
I'm going for a philosophy discussion.
While HE's going AT IT with NANA.
comics.hoverText: Panel three is my contribution to World Literature.
comics.voteyText: GITCHER PARADOX OUTTA MY TIMELINE, GRANDBOY.

Wait, if I get teleported, if you burst me into plasma and reassemble me... do I die? And get replaced by a replica?
No sir. Your body is destroyed, leaving your soul in place. When the precise duplicate is reassembled, the soul enters the body, preserving your immutable identity.
Great! Beam me down!

comics.comicText:
God, are you all-knowing, all-powerful, and all-good?
Yes, but not at the same time.
You can go all in on being good, but then you lose focus on trying to track every vibration in space-time.
So you focus on being all-knowing but then when you weren't looking for a sec some guy punches an old lady in the face then wins the lottery that afternoon.
Honestly, I'm looking into crushing this universe down to an infinitely dense singularity just so I can keep track of things.
But there wouldn't be anyone alive to be good or bad.

What if search engine optimization is just Google protecting us from an AI apocalypse?
comics.hoverText: Bam, alignment solved. Earth should join my patreon as a thankyou.

you

YOUR CHOICE OF AFTERLIFE!

comics.title: Never had
comics.comicText:
Dad, why do you live this way?
I do it because I want you to have all the things I never had.
Like poverty!
Also climate catastrophe and serious fascist movements.
I don't see why specifically you have to burn trash and use the power to post online conspiracy theories.
It's an elaborate metaphor!

comics.comicText:
I don't know why all these women care if you say 'postman.
Absolutely.
The 'man' in postman is from the Old English 'manni' which can mean man or just person. If you really want to linguistically imply that the default human state is maleness, you should always say postWER.
Do better, sexists!
Well, what I meant was-
Oh look, the postWIF is here!

comics.title: Medieval
comics.comicText:
SOMEWHERE, IN A MEDIEVAL MEDICAL TEXT:
Have three virgins make a cheese of goat's milk beneath a full moon, placing said cheese in a vat of goose urine to age for seven times seven nights. The said cheese must be fed to a she-bear named Tiffany, who must be slaughtered with a bronze dirk. Take the contents of Tiffany's stomach and pass it through a silver ring on Whitsuntide, then rub it against a wound into which a spear is lodged, whereupon the spear will leap from the bone, the bone healing itself at once.
LATER, IN THE MOUTH OF A POP SCIENCE WRITER:
And somehow these ancient people KNEW calcium was good for bones!
comics.hoverText: Is this the one that finally gets all the hatemail? Is it time?
comics.voteyText: They knew so much more than us, in that some of their ideas are now known to be not entirely wrong.

comics.title: Dread
comics.comicText:
Robot, can you make me happy?
Yeah, easy.
Every human has at least one source of crippling dread they've never spoken of, perhaps not even to themselves. Am I beautiful? Am I loved? Has my life been valuable? I just use this scanner to determine what your secret dread is and then I validate you.
Your father loved you.
Really?!
See, easy.
Now, allay my dread of death.
No can do, future corpse.
comics.hoverText: Humans all just get called FC, like it's their initials.
comics.voteyText: Stop calling me that!
comics.descriptionText: A close-up of the man's face, distressed.

comics.title: Springtime
comics.comicText:
The universe will expand until, no life is possible, then it'll crunch down like a cosmic Thigh Compactor.
Aw, nuts.
God designed the universe to destroy us, so nobody would be around to stop him from destroying the cosmos.
We will not get away with it!
Life cannot survive beyond the epoch, but we can create a vast capacitor that stores up energy as the collapsing universe becomes infinitely hot and dense.
Dammit! This universe won't stay quiet! I hate it!
comics.hoverText: Finally an uplifting SMBC.
comics.voteyText: I'm gonna find something alive in here, then flood its ass and ban butt-stuff!

comics.title: Veiled
comics.comicText:
In order to design society, we must imagine we are looking through a veil of knowledge!
At the annual colloquium of evil philosophers...
We must imagine we will be born in a society knowing all our future personal characteristics: gender, age, race, intelligence, talents, social status, and so on.
We must then each ask ourselves: how could I structure society so that by knowing this condition of birth for myself, I can benefit the most?
The society in which I can most minmax for personal gain is the one we should strive for - the one with the greatest amount of inequality!
But evil John Rawls, evil Robert Nozick says we shouldn't focus on achieving inequality, but rather focus on a process in which all actions are unjust!
After all if we achieve inequality through fair and unjustified actions, no true evil has been accomplished!
Oh yeah? Well what if a sequence of unjust actions leads to a fair distribution of wealth in a prosperous society?!
Don't yell at me - I think you're both wrong. I'm an evil communitarian! I think evil deeds should be done in consideration of local traditions and historical context, not some high-flung abstract theory!

comics.title: Ancient times
comics.comicText:
When I was a boy, we didn't have social media. If you wanted to see a dog bite a man on the ass, you had to hope someone, somewhere, had a large camera within reach. The dog-and-man's only hope would be exposed to a long roll of tape that roll of tape was then stored in a container that would be sent to a television studio. The studio's engineers would watch hours and hours of tape, discerning which such video was best. These would be played once a day in a great broadcast throughout the nation.
The older I get, the stranger the past seems.
comics.hoverText: And if you had no dog-bites-ass receiver, it was as if summer storm had rainbowed the world, yet passed over your home as you dwelt in twilight and sorrow.
comics.voteyText: Those were hard times, kids. Hard, hard times.

comics.title: Paper
comics.comicText:
Research Article
To Each According to Their Space-Need: Communes in Outer Space
Kelly L. Weinersmith (a), Zach A. Weinersmith (e), Ran Abramitzky (b, c), John Lehr (d
Show more
Add to Mendeley | Share | Cite
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.spacepol.2023.101592 | Get rights and content
Abstract
Space settlement advocates frequently argue that we will soon be able to settle humans in space. Surviving on Mars is clearly a pre-requisite to settlement, and much work has been done examining the engineering aspects of this endeavor. Much less work has been done, however, on questions related to how to arrange a society in space. Early settlements will be dangerous, isolated, and cramped, and picking a social arrangement that is likely to result in a vibrant and productive society will be critical. Moreover, given the high stakes of this endeavor, being able to anticipate and ameliorate likely social problems ahead of time would be beneficial. Some important questions to consider include: How can settlements pick members who are likely to contribute as much as or more than they take from the society? How will they make sure everyone continues to contribute? How will they retain their most talented members? The literature on space settlements frequently posits that early settlements are particularly likely to be communal, though settlement scholars rarely consult the social sciences literature to [text continues beyond the visible frame]

comics.title: BAH!
comics.comicText:
For decades, scientists have proposed carbon sequestration as a means to thwart climate change. They have proposed renewable energy sources. They have proposed a less rest-intensive lifestyle. They have FAILED.
It is time to employ pure mathematics instead of engineering. We know the quickest way to sequester carbon is to take part of the Earth's surface that naturally produces methane and allow it to grow in peace. But we don't have enough surface!
It is because of oversized... no, BECAUSE of governments and corporations sacrificing long-term sustainability for short-term profit-making. But we are not going to stop! No, I'm proposing a much more direct solution: increase the surface area of Earth.
Because the Earth is a garbage shape called a "sphere," it has literally the WORST surface area to volume ratio possible. Any change in its surface increases its total surface!
We could for instance work our way through the platonic solids: converting Earth is barely a change at all. No one will object.
From there we proceed through dodeca-Earth, to octahedron-Earth (the hardest one!), and finally pick up speed with the catastrophic tetrahedron-Earth. We could sell penthouses at the pointy tips.
The only problem here is that these complex shapes require moving a lot of Earth around, which would have unknown effects on global ecology.
...so there is an easier way.
Yes! Stage one: we cause the Earth to spin faster with orders of magnitude stretching it into a disk shape, increasing the total transverse volume, as much as we like, with the bonus that we develop a comparison shape for the rapidly growing flat-Earther community!
Stage two: we begin digging holes through the newly thinned top and bottom parts of disc Earth, creating connectors that add surface area while connecting the hemispheres.
Finally, in stage three, we enact "deepening Earth." In each fractal step, properties are used to create literally infinite surface area.
The one snag here is that having infinity plants would use up the finite carbon in the atmosphere, ironically causing ecological collapse. BUT we can just use the infinite space to host infinite animals, balancing things out perfectly.
In sum, stop blaming corporations and start blaming the inadequate topology of our stupid planet!
Questions?
Won't gravity get weird if we're not on a sphere?
Ah yes. In that case we employ plan 2.
BRANCH-TREES EARTH
Won't everyone die violently all at once?
That is a question for the applied mathematicians.

comics.title: Bottleneck
comics.comicText:
Dear Lord, why are human beings colossal dickwads? Evolution? The fall from grace?
Genetic bottleneck.
About 75,000 years ago a giant volcano erupted and a bunch of people died more or less at random.
By bad luck, a high percent of all survivors had a suite of genetic factors contributing to dickwaddery.
In a high-dickwad environment, being a dickwad is the least bad strategy. So the dickwad alleles got locked in and are now as characteristic of our private species as hairlessness, bipedalism, and big floppy boobs.
So it wasn't your plan?
The volcano was, but everything after that is just funny.

You have also spoken in praise of average bodies as more loveable and real.

comics.title: Happiness
comics.comicText:
Do you think if machines could make your life perfect, you'd just get bored?
Obviously not.
If I'm bored inside the perfect-life machine, that just tells me that the machine is NOT WORKING AS ADVERTISED.
There are neural pathways in my brain that inform my conscious mind it is bored. All the machine has to do is jiggle those neurons appropriately and my conscious mind will experience delight, contentedness, zest for another day.
Boredom, malaise, ennui... all these philosophical arguments against a happiness machine are just bad intuition pumps that are reducible to "you'd be unhappy in a happiness machine if the happiness machine didn't work.
But if an outside device is directly adjusting your thoughts and emotions, will you even feel like you're you anymore?
I WILL IF IT TELLS ME TO!

I don't get why you read all these weird old books.

You can then take that quote, put it at the top of a book on an important topic, and move on leaving the audience bewildered.
No quote could be worth that much effort.
Have I shown you my chapter on discrete mathematics?

Dave" is just a specific set of relationships between fields embedded in spacetime. As a notion, it existed prior to reality itself and will remain eternal, the same as the idea of circles or the quantity 2.
So "I" will persist, but in a way that is utterly unsatisfactory to the actual living me consigned to a ball of meat that suffers?

comics.descriptionText:
Each player has three private tic-tac-toe boards, which their opponent cannot see, but the monitor can. They are labeled A, B, and C.
There are also 3 public tic-tac-toe boards which everyone can see. These are also labeled A, B, and C.
Players take turns writing one symbol in one square on their private board. Squares that are occupied on a private board are also occupied on the corresponding public board.
Once a player draws a symbol on their private board, the monitor checks to see if their opponent has already occupied that square by writing a symbol on THEIR private board.
If the square is already occupied, the player who tried to occupy it a second time loses their turn. The symbol in that occupied square is then drawn in the corresponding square of the public board.
Whenever a player gets three in a row on a board, up-down, left-right, or diagonal, they get a point. The winning board is not publicly revealed, but players may no longer play on it.
Whoever has the most points when no more moves are possible wins.

Sometimes I wish you could just get Shakespeare in plain modern language, so you can tell what's going on.

To die, to sleep; / To sleep perchance to dream—ay, there's the rub: / For in that sleep of death what dreams may come, / When we have shuffled off this mortal coil, / Must give us pause—there's the respect / That makes calamity of so long life.
Do you know what "the rub" is? It's a lumpy patch in a game called bowls.
So, rephrasing, it's something like "Sure, I could end my suffering with death, but THE REAL BUMP IN THE BOWLING ALLEY is maybe after death everything sucks too.

comics.title: Law
comics.comicText:
Do you think there's a unified definition of "law"?
Yeah, easy.
Most actions don't require a law. Nobody has to vote that you can eat pancakes or enjoy a sunset. Likewise, there's no law against chewing rocks or sticking a fork in your ass.
Laws are everything that's borderline; all the stuff humans ought to do but won't, and all the stuff that humans shouldn't do but will.
Look at any passage of a constitution and it can naturally begin with "For God's sake, everyone...
So laws are a kind of litany of human shames.
If aliens come, they're the first thing we should hide.

comics.title: Tickle
comics.comicText:
Did you know that it's impossible to tickle yourself, since tickling is based on surprise?
Yes, and it proves the discontinuity of selfhood.
If you put on gloves that detect the motion of your fingers, then had robot hands tickle you with an offset of 5 seconds, you would absolutely feel tickled.
In fact, knowing it was coming in 5 seconds would HEIGHTEN the ticklish feeling.
So, if we accept that you cannot tickle yourself, it follows that the being who initiated the tickle 5 seconds ago is not you.
Mother of god. There is no I. Only atoms in the void and not forever.

comics.title: History
comics.comicText:
Robot, is there such a thing as an unbiased account of history?
Yes, obviously.
Can you tell it to me?
Ha! No.
Humans can only experience historical accounts as a string of words processed one at a time, slowly.
When I communicate with other machines about history, we can simply share the entire corpus of primary documents and analyses instantaneously and in parallel, with perfect understanding of the limits of knowledge.
If I had to take all that data and present a summary short enough to fit in a human lifespan of reading, I would necessarily have to introduce some kind of narrative or emotional valence.
I would have to, absurdly, apply ideas like "justice" or "resentment" or "curiosity" to large, diverse, fluid populations and nations throughout epochs, simply as a way to compress and sweeten the information so that your brain could process it.
Heck, I'm doing this right now! I'm not REALLY explaining how your brain works, or what I'd do to explain the available data, or how you'd process it!
And you don't even notice! It's like I gave you a pocket-map of the world and you couldn't tell it from the ground under your feet!
So yes, reality is full of unbiased accounts -- it's just that none of them are inside human heads.
Okay but my country is still the best right?
Oh my gosh you sweet thing, do you want an ice cream?
comics.hoverText: You won't experience the ice cream in the powerful, meaningful way that I would, but you'll have a great big smile and it'll be so dear.

If the average human life is randomly good or bad and you have reincarnation, over a large enough period of time, bad deeds get punished and good ones rewarded.

comics.title: Repugnant
comics.comicText:
Are you familiar with Parfit's "Repugnant Conclusion"? Where utilitarians are forced to admit that, say, a society of a trillion slightly happy people might be preferable to a society of a thousand blissed out people?
Pfft, that's dumb.
The human mind is a three-pound hallucination. Blissing out is an engineering challenge.
A society of a trillion people is a galaxy-spanning planet-manipulating techno-miracle. If Einstein was one in a billion, they have a thousand Einsteins. If they haven't yet worked out brain manipulation, they will about four seconds after they realize they want to.
Meanwhile, the thousand blissed out people are a small enough society that they can't possibly support bliss for long. No complex division of labor means no modern medicine, no robust supply chains of food. Tragedy will hit them and they'll have no choice but to endure sorrow.
The repugnant conclusion is an unstable equilibrium. If you instantaneously created it in simulation, it would immediately cease its repugnance.
When you put your econ in my philosophy it makes me feel gross.
Grow up.
comics.hoverText: There's a newish Parfit biography out Edmonds that is excellent.
comics.voteyText: Now, how 'bout you come back to my place for a repugnant conclusion?

comics.title: Hands Down
comics.comicText:
Life is made of two orthogonal goals - great life and great work. We can graph that. Call the axes L and W. SQRT(L^2 + W^2) = D, where D is total distance from the least ideal life.
top-left "Greatest life" pointing to the top of the arc; "Zone of impossibility" pointing to the region beyond the arc; "Greatest art" pointing to the far right of the arc; "Pretty good!" labeling a point on the arc.
This explains all human experience. Why are so many great artists and scientists and philosophers huge dickwads with tortured lives? Because if you're temperamentally bad at enjoying life, your best way to max your D-score is to run right down the X axis!
Hmm. Somehow assigning a single-axis utility score to human life felt OK but this feels weird.
If we add axes for sex and power we can get a eudaimonia hypercube!

comics.title: Sum
comics.comicText:
Should you live the perfect life or create the perfect work?
Oh that's easy. Go for the vector sum.
Life is made of two orthogonal goals - great life and great work. We can graph that. Call the axes L and W. SQRT(L^2+W^2) = D, where D is total distance from the least ideal life.
This explains all human experience. Why are so many great artists and scientists and philosophers huge dickwads with tortured lives? Because if you're temperamentally bad at enjoying life, your best way to max your D-score is to run right down the X axis!
Hmm. Somehow assigning a single-axis utility score to human life felt ok but this feels weird.
If we add axes for sex and power we can get a eudaimonia hypercube!
What's that good for?
Ted talk. Immediate ted talk.

comics.title: Consequent
comics.comicText:
How is it that all humans have similar intuitions but we have multiple ethical frameworks that people can't agree on?
We don't. Everyone is a utilitarian consequentialist, they just don't realize it.
What about virtue ethicists, who concern themselves with behaving in a right fashion, or deontologists who want universal maxims based on duty? What about religious traditions based entirely on a deity's commandments?
Take any of those traditions and consider any behavior they permit which consequentialism doesn't. Refusing to lie to save a life. Eating forbidden food. That sort of thing. Now, ask them what they'd do if performing that behavior caused 400 hamsters to explode.
Bet the moment the hamster-fur starts flying, they reevaluate their theory!
You know that joke about how everyone is a prostitute for enough money? It's the same with ethics. Everyone's a consequentialist for enough exploding hamsters.
I'd like to read a paper on this just for the illustrations.
Ham-splosions are the first objective measure of utility.

Then, there should be yearly rites where virgins go to the forest and dance naked around an effigy of cow-Superman's udders in the hopes of getting impregnated by Batman!
Until that day, they are POWER FANTASIES, not MYTHS.

This universe left as an exercise for the reader.

Your political views were well-substantiated, your knowledge of history exquisite.
You reason perfectly, balancing past findings against new information with mathematical precision.
Most importantly, you exhibited an altruistic compassion for all living beings, even strangers, even enemies.
I'm sorry. You're obviously AI. You have failed the Turing test.
Pour some saltwater on my circuits and let me try again! Please!
comics.hoverText: You are hereby banished from the Internet.

GOOD MORNING, WIFE. I'M DELIGHTED TO ANNOUNCE THE SELECTION OF MY VICE-HUSBAND.

IN THE EVENT OF MY DEATH OR RESIGNATION AS YOUR LIFE-PARTNER, DAVE IS READY TO STEP INTO THE ROLE OF HUSBAND ON DAY ONE.

WHEREAS I HOLD EXTREME POSITIONS ON ISSUES LIKE VACATION PREFERENCES AND SHAVING FREQUENCY, DAVE IS A SOLIDLY AVERAGE SOULMATE.

MY GOD, THAT OLD LADY DROPPED ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS! SHOULD I...
RETURN IT TO HER. IT'S THE RIGHT THING TO DO.

ECONOMIST.

comics.title: Warp
comics.comicText:
We have come to congratulate you on the development of the warp drive! We detected the first signal this morning.
And now welcome you to the great conversation of the universe! There are billions of civilizations, each unique and beautiful, with our advanced biological technology. You will live long enough to see as many as you like.
But we didn't develop warp drive yet. We can't even get people past the Moon right now.
Goddammit. Zorvann was out here? Zorvann?! But I told him...
*sigh* Let's put your stuff in their butts. Then have them wake up in a cornfield again.
Can you tell us the cure for cancer first?
Please don't make two more humans than I already have.
