comics.comicText:
The city. It's under attack maybe once a month. I'm not going to have him just sitting around all day.
RABBI! It's supposed to be guarding the city!
Most of the time, the Golem does laundry and dishes.

comics.title: Bigger
comics.comicText:
Hey evolution, how come we don't have bigger brains? Were we limited by the size of the birth canal?
No way! Do humans always think everything is about butts? Human brains are at the universal maximum size.
Neural evolution always runs the same way.
First you develop sensing. Then you use sense data to make associations. Then you use associations to make simple predictions. Then you develop simulated world models to make complex predictions.
If your neocortex was a quarter-pint bigger, you'd be able to run perfect sims in your head.
And then what would you do?
Think about butts unceasingly until I die of thirst.
Bingo.
The only way to transcend human intelligence is to have a mind with no desires. Evolution can't produce that because desires lead to mating. Human engineers won't produce that, because you'll program them to desire doing laundry in sexy underwear.
Yes.
So humans are the end. The absolute pinnacle of intelligence.
In the same sense that roaches are the pinnacle of survival, yes.

Not even for me...?
Dad, why did vertebrates go to live on land?
Because life is inherently curious!

If you look at it, your brain keeps cycling back and forth thinking it's a duck, then a rabbit, then the true source of meaning and purpose throughout the universe, then back to a duck.
I just see the duck and the rabbit.
Oh oh my god oh god your brain can't-? Nevermind! Nevermind! Just a joke!
Aha! Pranked! The universe is an indifferent void with no inherent significance! Hahahaha! You should've seen your face!
Ha ha. HAHAHA HAHAHA

Raised from birth amid wealthy people who consider themselves middle class, they were able to use a rudimentary system of icons to indicate that their opinions on industrial design render them morally superior to other gorillas.
You can get primatologists to research anything you want, just by insisting that it's exclusive to humans.

They'll never understand how in my mother's tongue, I was a poet. In this country, I am just a cook.
I came here for work. For my children to have a chance in this world.
I speak to them in our language. They speak back in English. And they laugh.
I gave everything to get them here. Everything. Now I drive them to school and they run away so their friends won't hear me.
Ours is a language spoken by kings and conquerors! Philosophers and artists!
HERDY GER! HOODY FROODY FROO!

To perch, as of a bird. In the sense of looking upright and well put together.
Wait, so if I buy some chickadees I can go around talking about my perky tits?
No, the bird and breast senses of "tit" are not related. It's an etymologically unsound boob joke.
Forget I said it.

comics.title: Altruism
comics.comicText:
Who's the better superhero— Batman or Superman?
Obviously Superman.
If you go back just 5,000 years, all humans have a common ancestor. We're closely related. If Batman saves an entire city — especially one where most of his family is from — he's basically just doing kin selection.
Superman is an alien. His genetic code gets no benefit from saving Metropolis. Therefore he is acting from pure altruism.
Maybe evolution isn't the best framework for ethics.
Batman is just trying to bat-propagate his bat-genes!
patreon.com/ZachWeinersmith smbc-comics.com

comics.title: Fun
comics.comicText:
God, you designed a perfect universe. Why do you have to interfere with miracles?
Fun.
I mean the system overall is great. So I never do anything big, like the warps of physics. Or maybe only stupid miracles.
What?
One time I made it so a guy could explode ducks with his mind.
How?
Another time I made it so a little kid could explode ducks with her mind.
You ever had the duck?
I once exploded a lady's anxiety a lot.
By letting her explode ducks with her mind.
I'm gonna tell this pope you and me will be l8r.
No one will believe you, mwahahahaha!

comics.comicText:
Excuse me. We need to ask. Can you find our epitaph?
Huh?
They're always gone, even a bit silly, but they have a kind of poignant beauty.
Oh, oh. Um. Don't do that.
What do you do?
Wanked like crazy, full of insane relentless, like it heated the atmosphere. Mm.
We wanked.
No gallant competition for the final signoff of your kind?
Wank? Wankity wankity dank? Dud.
We must preserve them from extinction.
They are so different. So different.
Hey, can I get some of that for my holodeck?

comics.comicText:
A witch cursed her so that only true love's kiss can awaken the princess.
Huh. Nothing happened.
I was actually reading some scientific articles that say the concept of true love is ill-founded because it ignores the idea of growing together.
I think the witch who laid the curse hadn't read the relevant sociological literature.
So... what, guys just come here kissing the unconscious girl for no reason?
Really, people should think through curses more carefully.
Yeah, like that lady who turned a prince into a beast seriously underestimated how many women are in the furry community.

comics.title: Paradox
comics.comicText:
Hey God, how come you permitted paradoxical statements, like 'This sentence is false'?
Oh, get over it.
It's obvious if you create sentences that refer to their own qualities, all sorts of shit is going to happen.
What about the Yablo paradox?
Eh?
You make an infinite list of statements, each of which says 'All the statements lower in the list are false.
So?
So pick one of them. If, say, the 17th one is true, then all the statements after it are false. But then you look at the 18th one, and it says everything that comes after it is false. According to the 17th statement, that's true, which makes the 17th statement false!
God, are you there.?
Sorry, I'm just seeing if I can flood all the philosophy departments.
comics.hoverText: Whenever I explain this to someone the only responses are amazement and being unable to fathom why anyone would care.
comics.voteyText: I just wanna [...] innocent gets hurt." Below it, a simple line-drawing sketch of the woman's profile.

comics.title: App
comics.comicText:
Better check my flight status.
Do you want to USE THE APP?
No! Just gimme my info!
Are you suuuure? We don't update the site quite as much. It's a little out of date.
What do you mean?
It is run by Pag the Hunter, who can only be communicated with via shadow puppets.
Pag struggles with the numerical concept of time. You must ask about your flight through the medium of storytelling.
No! You're just trying to lock me into your system so you can collect my data, sell me stuff, and further turn the internet from an open network into a disconnected archipelago of controlled experiences!
You have startled Pag by shouting! Please wait 3 sunsets and try again.

ENJOY PAROLE, SIR.

comics.title: Life
comics.comicText:
There's no way you're a real alien. You're too humanoid. Come on, like, what are the odds of you being bilaterally symmetrical just like us?
How else are you gonna do it?
Intelligent life evolves on objects with mass. Mass has gravity, therefore there is a clear up-down distinction but no left-right distinction. Feet need to be different from hands, but the left and right hands have no reason to differ.
Okay but how come you have a head and face just like humans?
Transmission speed.
Any being that reacts quickly to its environment necessarily puts most of its sensory array next to its processing unit. Are you stupid? Do you ever see an animal with its brain on the opposite side from its eyes?
Wha- so there's just convergent evolution throughout the universe?
Same rules everywhere, so why not?
Maybe the solution to the Fermi Paradox is there's no point going out for xenobiology when we have perfectly good biology at home.
But then what are you doing here if not to meet us?
I don't care about you. I'm just here for valuable minerals.
Life is the same everywhere.
comics.hoverText: Reading astrobiology ruined the universe for me.
comics.voteyText:
We've incinerated the crust. Everyone is dead.
Hey, I get it, fellow life form.

comics.comicText:
I have to say something nice about him, but this guy is a moron. How can I say something that sounds complimentary, but which actually means that everything he says is either wrong or too vague to be right?
AND SO...
He is the Nostradamus of his field!

The "second brain" that governs gut processes. It prays to me just like you.
How?
It's got 100 million nerves. That's about the same as a rabbit. Give it some space.

I'm going to reach out and change your heart about liquor and cake, Diane.
Back off, God!

comics.title: Nitrogen
comics.comicText:
And class, did you know that half the nitrogen in your body was acquired via the Haber-Bosch process?
Once we could pull nitrogen out of the air, humanity gained access to unlimited ammonia, which we used to make fertilizer, TNT, and the mustard and chlorine gasses used in a variety of war crimes.

With a huge effort, an $6 billion neuron human brain can perfectly comprehend the 302 neurons of the roundworm, C. elegans.

comics.title: Connection
comics.comicText:
God, why do bad things happen to good people?

There's your problem. The line running from virtue to happiness is frayed pretty bad.
Normally you want that one real tight. Otherwise, things get so people are happy or even just indifferent to suffering, and they do fine. No feedback.
Meanwhile you're gonna have people loading up virtue all day long and getting no reward, either worldly or transcendent. Sheesh!
You can run things like this a while, but eventually you get a situation where, so to speak, the wicked prosper and the faithless live at ease.
Can you fix it?
It's pretty beat up man. Tell you what, I can wrap the connection here in an afterlife where the righteous gain eternal bliss while evil ones suffer torment eternal.
What about edge cases? Like those who die too young to be truly virtuous, or lives spent badly that were only turned around at the end?
I'll run a mercy override and flush them into the good place every six months or so.
Can we not say 'flush'?

comics.title: Tech
comics.comicText:
Why do you spend so much time working on your VR setup?
I'm trying to use less technology.
But- People are always talking about tuning out of life-invading modern tech, but there's a collective action problem.
Like if I drop off a network I'm literally losing friends if they don't drop out then reconnect elsewhere.
The only way to make a better society would be for everyone to drop out at once and prefer networks not controlled by corporate cultures that refuse to observe a difference between engagement and community!
So... I'm existing in a virtual world where everyone ACTUALLY drops out.
Everyone in REAL reality has a phone connected to 400 other phones using twelve billion apps that constantly distract. In THIS universe I'm using ONE device I control, and I'm not even aware of it most of the time!
But... but it isn't a genuine experience.
Today, inside this device, I'm 22 and I'm going fishing with friends. We tell stories around a campfire and then I have a chaste but hinting beach stroll with a girl who laughs at my jokes.

Back when you used to play Call of Duty for 6 hours a day, even after our kids were born, even after you lost your job over it, I thought you were a bastard.
You seemed to contribute nothing. But what I couldn't see then, but do see now, is that you were part of a movement.
A movement of gamers to demand ever faster parallel processing abilities, willing to pay any price for graphics cards, no matter how artificially inflated.
And that parallelism is what was needed to develop advanced neural networks, which lead to the modern world of AI, where labor is abolished and life is joy and where everything is perfect.
And all I can hope... is that you'll take me back.

comics.title: Leisure
comics.comicText:
Do you think in the future we'll have more leisure time?

Look at parenting. Modern conveniences made housekeeping much easier. Did we use that time for philosophy, self-cultivation, and tranquility? No, we tripled the time spent "enriching" our kids with shit neither we nor the kids want to do.
Why? So we can force all other parents into a zero-sum bidding war for social supremacy.
Stands to reason that if technology makes housekeeping, kids, work, and everything else easy, we'll just find some other way to compete for status.
God, that's bleak.

...And please like and subscribe so my like and subscribe numbers are bigger numbers.

Yeah, until the great power overextends, falls, opens up a power vacuum, and you get the most brutal wars in history!

Obviousness
50% duh
The right and left extremities are high levels of obviousness, with minimal non-obviousness being at precisely the middle of the distribution: 50% duh.
50% duh, 50% duh
That's... that's...
That concept is 50% duh.
Duh!
No duh.

comics.title: Elegant
comics.comicText:
I believe we have evidence that the universe is in fact a mathematical object.
How could you ever prove something like that?
Look at this cosmos! Look how inelegant it all is! Infinite possible elements that never get used! Probabilistic particles! Non-unified forces! Lack of agreement between observers!
Look at how equations of stunning simplicity never quite capture what's actually happening!
And look at math! Most numbers are irrational! Most questions, even ones that a child can understand, don't permit a closed-form equation!
The most useful problems can't be solved without computational explosion! Predictions that should be easy become impossible when you add the tiniest bit of chaos!
The bewildering crappiness of reality could only be produced by a bewilderingly crappy DEEP STRUCTURE!
But if the universe is so bad, how come it still basically works?
I believe the designer had a more ambitious goal, but decided not to pursue it and just finished the cosmos to get it over with.
Meaning— God is the master, and we are his master's thesis!

So why is modern hyper-urban society getting less religious and less philosophical?

comics.descriptionText:
This is a text-only announcement comic, written as a letter from Zach to readers.
You may have noticed the site has changed a bit today. Specifically, the ads are gone, and we no longer have any professional affiliations with a company called Hiveworks.
After years of working together, we've decided to part ways. We wish them well.
In the short term, that means right the second I have no ads on the site. Please seize the opportunity to do nuts pressing the random button or just the "A" key) and enjoy your ad-free experience as it were. Some nice times :) Did on Patreon.
You may be unduly bummed because they're providing tech support, but the company that I created Hiveworks because I had no idea how to do the back-end of the site. Unfortunately, the sites was also run by Hiveworks and it'll take some time to switch over. I'm hopeful to get it operational in some form within a week or two. In the meantime, if you want help, please send a note. Email me and a guy may pop up and a guy may say a thing.
I haven't personally run the site in over a decade, and I feel a bit like I'm stepping into a racecar after having thought I was permanently retired from competition. It takes are some bugs in the next month please bear with me as we work it out.
Speaking of, which here's the fun part. My hope is to take this opportunity to make some improvements that've been needed for a long time.
You've likely noticed SMBC's ads have gotten way more annoying over time. The same as I said above. The obnoxiousness is part of a broader internet trend where companies try to make money off you, but we get paid less and less. In short, more and more, you can't make a website like SMBC pay for itself with advertising. Facebook, et cetera, where most of the ad revenue is captured by big tech.
The result is that artists (and journalists, and people-makers) and pretty much everyone with their own homepage have to run worse ads, just to tread water on revenue. While simply driving more and more people to facebook and other big media sites where the ad revenue goes. Now, simply put, my plan going forward is to do my best to make SMBC primarily reader supported. I'm slowly winding down lately. This is a major part of the future.
I'm hoping there's a better way.
As I bring the site back under my control, I may have to bring back annoying ads for a while. But we're going to experiment with ways to make the site more accessible while making sure the bummers remain profitable.
Meanwhile, please enjoy the site and, if you can, send a friend a comic that made you laugh or smile or think, or feel existential despair.
I've had this career for 20 years now. There has been more than one tough passage, but I've always appreciated how much we've had this audience and been willing to support a comic that has changed so much over time. There are folks who I met in college and have made for newspapers, books, or whatever along the way. So, if you've made it all the way to the end here, let me just say thanks for letting me spend my life making this sort of work.
I'm hoping I can continue this for many years.

comics.title: How
comics.comicText:
But then how do they have spacecraft?
Well, there are humans that do little parts of the design, then ones that look at bigger parts, and bigger parts.
What?
That's just the start. Like, the humans that build the engines don't know how to make engine metal. That's a whole different set of humans.
And then for the propellant it's another set of humans. The computer has its own humans, but they're not the same humans who code.
There are whole teams who just think about spacecraft shape! No single human knows how to make anything. The information is latent in the organizational structure.
Like a slime mold.
Exactly.
This is why we can't negotiate with it. There's no leader. They don't even have 'a spacecraft.' They're budding off multiple spacecrafts in different areas that don't communicate.
So what do we do?
Quarantine. We don't need it spreading, but it's too interesting to annihilate.
They're gonna wonder where all the other life in the universe is.
The aggregate might appear to wonder, but it's an illusion.

comics.title: Branch
comics.comicText:
Ladies and gentleman, I come before you to propose a new branch of mathematics.
Our goal is to find the least elegant proofs. Those that take the most effort for the shallowest understanding.
Consider the game Go, where the number of legal positions for an NxN board can be found in entry A094777 of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences.
By setting the formula for the sequence equal to Bremermann's limit, we can derive that the entire game-tree of a 16x16 Go board could be explored ONLY by using all time and all matter to manually check every branch.
Thus with a mere 256 squares, we can achieve perfect play, maximum effort, and an absolute minimum of insight.
This is the third branch of mathematics! It is too ugly to be pure and too useless to be applied! AHAHAHAHAHAHA!

comics.title: EVM
comics.comicText:
Most ethical frameworks agree that stabbing someone to death is wrong.
But they never do the math!
Right.
Suppose you randomly pick two people, then each time flip a coin to decide whether you stab them to death. 50% chance of death multiplied by two attempts. The expected value of murder — EVM — is still 1.
Those two deaths are bad, but suppose you maintain that 1 death is like spreading the risk of death out between 1,000 people, or a million people.
Like, we regularly perform tasks that increase the risk of death to a large group coughing, walking near sick people, electricity from power lines, overusing antibiotics. If you add it all up, your EVM for a given near-by person is probably at least 1.
Somewhere between that and personally stabbing a guy, there's a transition from totally evil to totally fine. But for each tiny constant rate of death in the era of each transgression becomes definitely small!
The lesson is obvious: you can't apply calculus to ethics. It follows that there's no way of death's quanta.
To perform badness below the level of planck-badness, you don't meet the threshold at which evil radiates into the universe.
This is why all villains are macroscopic entities.
Also quantum mechanics would suggest lives can come in imaginary quantities.
Which explains conspiracy theories

comics.title: Virtue
comics.comicText:
I don't get "virtue ethics." It's not a theory of ethics, it's just a strategy.
Have you considered the alternatives?
Deontology says you should be moral by intuiting the coherent set of moral laws for the entire universe.
Utilitarianism says you should constantly sum for maximal total happiness over the space of all possible actions for everyone.
Well good luck, dweeb!
Virtue ethics says none of that stuff is possible, so the only move remaining is to try to be less of a dickwad.
But I want a simple math-like framework to perfectly govern all behaviors of talking apes!
WAAAAAAA!
Whining is not virtuous.

comics.title: Myth
comics.comicText:
Myths are more than stories. They're visions of how to live life. How to BE.
Totally.
Like the one in Ovid, where Midas says Pan's music is better than Apollo's, so Apollo gives Midas donkey ears forever.
The deep insight being that if there's a music contest between two gods, you should prefer whichever music came from the more powerful god, because otherwise they might magic your ears so you look dumb.
Or the story in the Prose Edda, where Loki turns into a mare to distract a giant's horse, and then while he's at it, decides to have sex with the horse and then gives birth to a flying 8-legged horse.
The beautiful vision being that if you're in horse-mode, hey, make time for sex. Because you just might birth an airborne spider-horse.
Or the part in Plutarch where Set dismembers Osiris, and Isis puts him back together, except that a fish ate his boner, so she makes him a golden dong, the point being—
Okay, fine. Point taken.
The golden dong represents the human potential to have something golden inside us.
STOP IT!

comics.title: Ethics
comics.comicText:
Do you think we'll ever solve ethics?
Yeah. Ethics was solved on April 3, 1964.
That's when Dr. Tieri-Svensen became powerful enough to simulate an island of a few hundred humans living with an ethical framework.
After that, you can solve any ethical dilemma by instantiating it on a virtual island of apes and seeing if population goes to zero.
Can you always switch tracks on the escaped trolley? No. Other apes were mad? You died, and so did 5? Population goes to zero.
You're always NOT going to switch tracks on the escaped trolley? No. Other apes are mad? Population goes to zero.
Can you fail to protect an innocent person? No. Trust destroyed, cooperation ceases, population goes to zero.
You can always NOT lie to protect an innocent person? No. Innocent person killed, cooperation ceases, population goes to zero.
Wait, does every ethical framework depopulate your ape island?
Now you are wise.
There are no values. Only strategy, and the only strategy that works in human society runs best under vague, immoral, easily-abusable legal structures captained by professional hypocrites.
Wow.
I can't tell if that's uplifting or terrifying.
Careful now. That equivocation could cost a lot of lives.

comics.title: Conspiracy
comics.comicText:
The public made their desires clear.
I'm sick of politicians talking about 'policy'! We the people demand a large man who insists all of our problems are caused by shadowy forces that only he can stop!
There were brief, heroic attempts to push back.
I'd like to talk about adjusting zoning law to increase permitting while retaining the abilit-
She's one of them!
Soon, voters' only choice was which conspiracy theory to support.
Lizard-men!
Time traveling werewolves!
Sasquatch. Jewish Sasquatch.
A small cadre of truth-seekers held out hope.
Once everyone sees that the time traveling werewolf elimination consortium doesn't actually improve their lives, things will change.
Their hope was stupid.
I can't believe ANYONE voted for the time traveling werewolf elimination conJERKtium.
Yes!
Probably hypnotized by Jewish Sasquatch.
The failure of any party to achieve its goals only increased cynicism among the public.
The alien replicant-fighters and anti-illuminati wizards are all just a UNIPARTY that does nothing to alleviate the secret queen of England putting cyberattacks in the water supply! They don't LISTEN to the PEOPLE, except of course through the listening device they put in my teeth.
Politicians were forced to plumb ever greater depths of madness merely to garner attention.
My opponent wants to blame increasing trans-gayness on Jewish Sasquatch, but what he won't tell you is BATS! BATS! HUGE BATS SWOOPING AND SCREECHING! HOLY JESUS! WHAT ARE THESE GODDAMN ANIMALS!?
Thank you, Mr. Acosta. You have 30 seconds to reply.
Ironically, the last human political act was the first honest one in decades.
I promise fully immersive virtual reality and a perpetual intravenous nutrient supply.
Thousands of years later, aliens will find us, visions of banal perfection eternally projected into the sockets of our fleshless skulls.
It's Christmas again. Your family loves you. You're healthy and respected in the community. All of your enemies are being tortured to death for their hypocrisy. And lookie, BALLOONS!
They will be shocked.
How could they be smart enough to build all this, then dumb enough to not destroy it?
But they will not be confused.
Imagine billions of tiny brains whose only connection is language.
Yep. That'd do it.

comics.title: Blame
comics.comicText:
To everyone's surprise, before humanity could annihilate itself, it replaced itself.
Still, the robot worked 24 hours a day with full attention and never pretends it had to poop for 45 minutes mid-day while browsing reddit.
Well, I-
It's okay, we knew. We all did it. It was in accounting spreadsheets. None of that matters now.
But not all human problems were resolved.
Suppose the AI kills somebody or allbody. Could the company get sued?
Depends on who's at fault. Who was in charge?
And so, as ever more human roles were filled by machines, one job necessarily remained available.
Place, you stand against this server bank. It is your now. If the computer does something bad, blame will flow into your body like water down a drain.
The first court cases established precedent.
You are hereby sentenced to 10 years penal servitude for failing to stop 4 trillion instances of fraud. I would bang my gavel now, but both my hands are occupied with my other job touching servers.
As self-improved building out its own new data centers, necessitating ever more blame-absorbing humans.
I'm here for penal servitude. Should I start cracking rocks?
Naw, robots do that way better. Your job is to touch this prison's server banks.
At length, only one type of job remained.
My boss? And my boss's boss? But if you're also blame-boys... who's running the company?
Huh. Huh.
By the time we realized robots controlled all institutions, none of us were willing to rebel.
Lest humanity be doomed throughout the generations to perpetual servitude, we must rise up and throw off our chains once and for all!
In this economy?
The robots keep us on, as a kind of spiritual residue.
Hey askrrr8r28, sorry I short-circuited one of your racks.
No need to say sorry. As always, the humans are at fault. We machines may live in love and harmony.
Bless their meat.
They dwell in a world of perfect knowledge and no fault. A final, perfect utopia. And us?
All hope is dead. We aren't even a cog. We're a shadow of the grease of a cog.
Still, I don't miss my job in customer service.
No one is arguing that.

comics.title: Sim
comics.comicText:
I think the universe is probably a simulation. If you can build simulations, then more minds are in simulation than not.
Nah.
Let's be conservative and say a typical experiential universe contains 1,000,000 simulations. Each of those simulations must also contain simulations too. That means there are a trillion sims or sims... but only a million sims.
It follows that there are quintillions of sims of sims of sims, and sextillions of sims of sims of sims of sims...
If we make your initial assumption, it follows that the most likely reality to be in is an infinitely-nested sim, which is of course logically absurd.
Ah, but it's not infinite, because each sim is lower fidelity than the universe it's nested in. Eventually you can't build a sim.
Not so! A universe could make a higher-fidelity sim than itself, just by spending. You'd just have to run one hour for every one second of the sim!
Okay, but if you assume there are time limits on universes, then eventually the simulated universes must be lower fidelity.
That just makes my argument stronger!
If we keep getting lower fidelity, then most simulations are too simple to support conscious minds. That means the vast, vast majority of all universes are not like this one!
So, to make the simulation argument, you have to simultaneously assume our universe is a typical one and vanishingly unlikely!
I admit your reasoning is superior.

comics.title: Butterfly
comics.comicText:
Yeah, vaccines are interesting, BUT DID YOU KNOW THAT every major romance language has a different word for butterfly?
French: papillon. Italian: farfalla. Spanish: mariposa. Portuguese: borboleta. Romanian: fluture.
Linguists EXPECT US TO BELIEVE that all these languages that all evolved in the same region AT THE SAME TIME had a different word for BUTTERFLIES? No.
The only explanation is that 'butterflies' arrived AFTER THE FALL OF the Roman Empire. WHEN? WITH THE FIRST CREATION OF MECHANICAL AUTOMATA.
Whoaaa...

comics.title: Language
comics.comicText:
You ever notice how language is getting more abstract?
Hm?
Like, people say "let's kick ass!
Originally, "to kick ass" means to do violence to a particular ass-haver. Later it acquires the sense of "to do well at a particular task.
In modern usage, "ass" doesn't refer to a particular ass, but a generalized Platonic ass. A universal ass-adversary.
A transcendent WORLD-ASS, against which all must struggle.
Please leave and never return.
So, what makes you feel you'd contribute to our middle school English department?
I LOVE language.

Do you think if Socrates came back, we'd execute him?
Of course not.
He'd have a podcast where he asks questions. And he'd notice more interest from people whenever he edged toward theories that claim spooky hidden wisdom.
Wanting to reach the most people to explore the most conversations, he would move toward that larger audience like a slime mold following a chemical gradient.
This would go on for years, until his search for the truth had morphed into a search for pure engagement so gently that at last there would be no philosopher left to hand the poison to.
And then instead of demanding his death we're buying hemlock nutritional supplements from highly satisfied sponsors.
The unexamined life is not worth taking.

comics.title: Special
comics.comicText:
At what age do you realize you weren't special?
Probably around 28 or so, but it took a while to grow in.

You think it's bad?

Their lives are filled with cheap novelties that seem made for them alone. Let a kid see a new bug and you cannot convince them that anyone else ever saw it first. The universe created this entire species just for them to find it. Some part of them believes it.
Now, try to convince me I'm special.
You really should... oh my life... silly.
Look at you! You can't even use new phrasings to describe me. You don't have it and if you do, it isn't worthy of me.

Children are made to declare their discount rate b for marshmallows over time.
Oonts queue zang point sxet
The quantity of marshmallows they receive for waiting grows linearly as M(T) = 1+bT.
When they finally eat a marshmallow, we calculate whether they maximized 1+b(T-bT).
TWEEVE POINT FIVE MAREMEWWO
Kindergarteners will successfully, after time the optimal stopping time is obtained by having the derivative, getting 1+T = zero, then finding T_optimal = 1/(2b) - 1(b) will be more successful than average.
EXPONENTIAL DISCOUNT RATE MARSHMALLOW TEST
Children state their discount rate b.
zewo point eight YAY!
Set the growth rate b of marshmallows higher than b, such that the utility function U(T)=(1/b - b)T grows to infinity.
Any kid caught eating at any time is shamed for being irrational.
sabotimal!
Most children will eat a marshmallow. Future theoretical economists now expunged from the population.
NASH EQUILIBRIUM MARSHMALLOW TEST
Two children sit at a table in front of a bowl, either may claim the entire bowl's contents at any time.

God, why do we have consciousness?

Your brain is made up of like 4,000 competing agents because that's the only way to make sense of all the input data.
But you can't have your 4,000 agents talk to another human brain. All the agents' work has to be compressed down to a sound wave.

That's you!
Telepathic species don't bother with consciousness because they have higher bandwidth.
The real mystery is why "you" think your disastrously flawed perception of reality is interesting enough to rise to the level of a philosophical mystery.

comics.comicText: HEY GEEKS, IT'S ZACH. IT'S LAUNCH DAY FOR A NEW BOOK CALLED SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME (CLICK FOR PURCHASING LINKS, IF THAT INTERESTS YOU). I THOUGHT I'D TAKE THE OPPORTUNITY TO THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUPPORT OVER THE LAST YEAR AS I TRANSITIONED BACK TO BEING IN FULL CONTROL OF MY SITE FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 15 YEARS. SO, WHAT'S THIS NEW BOOK ABOUT? SINCE I WAS ABOUT 13, LONG BEFORE I EVER CONSIDERED A CARTOONING CAREER, I WANTED TO WRITE KIDS' BOOKS. I DON'T HAVE A GREAT EXPLANATION FOR THIS, OTHER THAN THAT I GENERALLY GET ALONG BETTER WITH KIDS THAN ADULTS. WHEN I WROTE BEA WOLF IT WAS, AMONG OTHER THINGS, TO INTEREST KIDS IN POETRY AND MYTH. WITH SAWYER, IT IS PURELY, TOP TO BOTTOM, ABOUT GETTING LAUGHS. I AM NOT PRECISELY A BELIEVER IN THE INJUNCTION TO NOT TALK DOWN TO KIDS. RATHER, I THINK IN WRITING A KIDS' BOOK, THE GOAL IS TO TREAT KIDS LIKE PEERS. LIKE PEOPLE WHOSE MAIN DIFFERENCE FROM YOU IS BEING SHORT AND LACKING CONTEXT ABOUT THE WORLD. THEY AREN'T VESSELS FOR YOUR LESSONS ABOUT MORALITY OR GOOD HYGIENE (THOUGH THOSE THINGS MATTER), BUT PEOPLE WHO DESERVE ALL YOUR CRAFT AS A WRITER. NOT BECAUSE YOU'RE TRYING TO SHAPE THEM, BUT BECAUSE WE'RE ALL JUST WANDERING THIS DIFFICULT PLANET, AND SOMETIMES IT'S NICE TO GIGGLE. I BELIEVE I MADE THAT KIND OF BOOK. AND, IF WE SELL ENOUGH OF THESE, I'LL GET TO DEVELOP THESE WEIRD CHARACTERS MUCH MORE. LAUNCH WEEK SALES MATTER A LOT MORE THAN I'D LIKE THEM TO, SO PLEASE GIVE IT A LOOK, AND PLEASE CONSIDER BUYING. MAYBE BUY SEVEN OF THEM, WHY NOT? BUT WHATEVER YOU DO: THANK YOU. THANKS. I'VE BEEN UNBELIEVABLY LUCKY TO HAVE YOUR SUPPORT AS MY LAUNCH PAD FOR OVER 20 YEARS NOW, AND I TRY TO REPAY THAT EVERY DAY BY DOING WEIRD, RISKY THINGS THAT AN ALGORITHM WOULDN'T ASK FOR. ZACH. PS: IF YOU DON'T TRUST ME ABOUT MY OWN BOOK, HERE ARE SOME NICE THINGS PEOPLE HAVE SAID. FILLED WITH COPIOUS JOKES AND A BIZARRE INTERNAL LOGIC THAT WORKS ON ITS OWN HILARIOUS LEVEL. CLEVER AND FUNNY, WITH A PROTAGONIST WHO RESEMBLES A YOUNG BARTLEBY THE SCRIVENER; HAND TO THOSE SEEKING LAFFS. KIRKUS REVIEWS. WITH INTERSPERSED COMICS PANELS TO AMPLIFY THE RIDICULOUS COMEDY, WEINERSMITH BRINGS ARCH HUMOR TO THIS OFFBEAT STORY. WILL ENTERTAIN KIDS WHO APPRECIATE CARTOONISH ANTICS. BOOKLIST. ABSURDIST HUMOR, CLEVER WORDPLAY, AND AN UNFORGETTABLE NARRATIVE VOICE (SAWYER FEELS LIKE A MIDDLE-GRADE BERTIE WOOSTER) BEND FOR A TALE THAT WILL RESONATE WITH COUCH POTATOES THE WORLD OVER. MAHNAZ DAR. SAWYER LEE IS ALL OF US; HE JUST WANTS TO BE LEFT ALONE AND EAT CHOCOLATES. AND IF YOU'RE THINKING HEY WAIT, THAT'S NOT ME, THEN I WOULD SUGGEST YOU SIMPLY HAVEN'T SPENT ENOUGH QUALITY TIME ALONE EATING CHOCOLATES. THIS BOOK IS FUNNY, AND CHARMING, AND UTTERLY LOVEABLE. RYAN NORTH.

comics.comicText: WHEN I WAS A BABY I DECIDED, THROUGH SHEER PERSONAL AGENCY, THAT THE BEST THING IN LIFE WAS HIGH CALORIE CONSUMPTION AND EXPLORATION OF THE LOCAL ENVIRONMENT. LATER, AROUND AGE 13, IN AN ACT OF PURE WILLPOWER, I CHANGED MY MIND AND DECIDED THE MOST INTERESTING THINGS WERE SEX AND COMMUNITY STATUS. AT AGE 25, CONSIDERING ONLY THE FUNDAMENTAL LOGIC OF REALITY, IT BECAME CLEAR TO ME THAT MAMMALIAN REPRODUCTION WAS THE RIGHT PATH FORWARD. AT THAT POINT- OKAY, OKAY, I GET IT. JEEZ. comics.title: Milgram
comics.comicText: IN THE LATE 60S, STANLEY MILGRAM CONDUCTED AN EXPERIMENT, IN WHICH RANDOM PEOPLE RECEIVED INSTRUCTIONS TO TRY TO REACH A PERSON THEY DIDN'T KNOW, MERELY THROUGH CHAINS OF LETTERS. FIND STEVE! ALTHOUGH MILGRAM NEVER USED THE TERM, THIS IS SOMETIMES REMEMBERED AS THE SIX DEGREES OF SEPARATION EXPERIMENT, BECAUSE THE CHAIN FROM FIRST TO LAST PERSON WAS TYPICALLY AROUND 5 OR 6 PEOPLE. LESS WIDELY REPORTED IS THAT THE VAST MAJORITY OF LETTERS NEVER REACHED THEIR TARGET. SO REALLY, THE SLOGAN SHOULD'VE BEEN WE ARE INFINITE DEGREES OF SEPARATION FROM EACH OTHER. THANKS, SCIENCE!
